movies.title: 14th
movies.cast: Sherrilyn Ifill, Stacey Abrams, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Jeff Flake, Hasan Piker, Alex Padilla
movies.description: Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?
notes: Open Fri Nov 27, showtimes to be announced.

movies.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon
movies.cast: Soraya Akhlaghi
movies.country: France, UK, USA, Denmark, Iran, Austria
movies.description:
Sixteen-year-old Soraya is a strong-willed Afghan sculptor and illustrator trying to find a way out of Iran and join her mother in Austria. This subtly textured self-portrait, shot by Soraya with her cell phone camera and directed by Mehrdad Oskouei, interweaves Soraya’s illustrations with chilling scenes of her escape attempts, political news from Afghanistan, and videos in which she sings and dances, or shows the bruises inflicted by her violent husband. Through masterful cinematography often filmed in dangerous conditions – and the protagonist’s radiant energy – this empowering collaboration between an established filmmaker and a young new artist enables her to reclaim her identity. Winner: Best Film, International Competition – IDFA 2025

“Inventive and engaging. A compelling, shape-shifting blend of thriller and dark fairy tale.” – Screen Daily

movies.title: A Knight’s Tale
movies.cast: Heath Ledger, Mark Addy, Rufus Sewell, Shannyn Sossamon, Paul Bettany, Laura Fraser
movies.description:
After his scene-stealing turn in 10 Things I Hate About You , Heath Ledger closed out the 1990s and entered the new century with the keys to the pin-up-boy castle, playing the hunky lead in Brian Helgeland’s bubblegum medieval romp, A Knight’s Tale .

Hoping to climb the 15th-century social ladder, lowly squire William Thatcher (Ledger) seizes an unexpected opportunity to pass himself off as a knight. But what begins as a swashbuckling quest for glory gets complicated when William falls head over heels for Lady Jocelyn (Shannyn Sossamon), putting both his ruse and his heart in jeopardy.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Accident
movies.director: Joseph Losey Screenplay by Harold Pinter Based on the 1965 novel Accident by Nicholas Mosley
movies.cast: Dirk Bogarde, Stanley Baker, Jacqueline Sassard, Michael York, Vivien Merchant, Delphine Seyrig, Alexander Knox
movies.description: A country home on a warm summer night; the sound of a sickening car crash; a startled horse; a white-clad woman with a feathery boa; a curious dog. A long Sunday that begins with guests, expected and unexpected, arriving for lunch, and then staying for supper, and then overnight; interspersed with clumsy tennis, near-silent walks through an idyllic countryside, drinkers upending their beer glasses to clear for the whiskey, and... “What room is everybody in?” Oxford don Dirk Bogarde’s mid-life crisis, struggling with the tensions, rivalries, lusts and distrusts shared with his students Michael York and Jacqueline Sassard, pregnant wife Vivien Merchant, and unpleasant bespectacled colleague Stanley Baker, as the flashbacks unfold à la Alain Resnais, including a wispy, dreamlike reunion with old flame Delphine Seyrig (LAST YEAR AT MARIENBAD).

movies.title: Agora
movies.cast: Neji Kanaweti, Majd Mastoura, Bilel Slatnia, Sonia Zarg Ayouna
movies.description:
In a remote Tunisian town, people who were previously thought to be missing make a sudden return, causing growing tensions within the families, community, and local police.

As a result, local police inspector Fathi, with the help of his doctor friend Amine, tries to understand the enigmatic and bizarre circumstances that led to their initial disappearance and unexpected return.

As the investigation deepens, a police inspector from the capital, Omar, arrives to solve the mystery. Will Omar’s arrival bring understanding or further complicate matters?

movies.title: Air Mail
movies.cast: Pat O’Brien, Ralph Bellamy, Gloria Stuart, Slim Summerville, Lilian Bond, Russell Hopton
movies.description: Before Howard Hawks’ aviation melodrama Only Angels Have Wings , director John Ford hoisted Depression-era audiences up, up, and away to a cockpit-level view of airmail delivery! Ford’s trademark penchant for the American West provides a perilous backdrop to the surprisingly sensational workaday lives of thrill-junkie postal pilots, centering on a reckless daredevil who won’t let anything – a pal, a dame, or even the Christmas shipping rush! – clip his flight feathers.
notes: Presented in 35mm
Hosted by Caroline Golum and Cristina Cacioppo

movies.title: American Psycho
movies.cast: Christian Bale, Justin Theroux, Josh Lucas, Bill Sage, Chloë Sevigny, Reese Witherspoon
movies.description:
“Look at that subtle off-white coloring. The tasteful thickness of it. Oh, my God. It even has a watermark.”

Before Christian Bale was the savior of Gotham, he was the chainsaw-wielding, business card-slinging scourge of Manhattan. Caught during the height of American Yuppieism in the late '80s, Patrick Bateman finds himself surrounded by friends who he hates and a culture he can’t stand. Can anyone blame him for allowing his nightly bloodlust to overflow into the day?

It’s hard to imagine anyone aside from Bale lecturing a soon-to-be victim on the cultural undertones found within Huey Lewis and The News’ “Hip to be Square,” all while wearing a raincoat and holding an incredibly shiny axe. But, what now seems meant to be almost wasn’t! The role was originally offered to none other than Leonardo DiCaprio. However, due to his newfound fame within the teenaged female demographic, Leo’s managers felt that a stint as a sociopathic mass murderer might somehow taint his image. I guess a career in murders and executions isn’t for everyone.

Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have to return some videotapes.

movies.title: Artificial
movies.cast: Andrew Garfield, Monica Barbaro, Billie Lourd, Mark Rylance, Chris O’Dowd, Cooper Hoffman, Ike Barinholtz, Jason Schwartzman, Zosia Mamet
movies.description: A comedic drama set in the world of artificial intelligence, around the period at OpenAI in 2023 that saw CEO Sam Altman fired and rehired in a matter of days.

When a computer scientist and AI pioneer Professor Geoffrey Hinton makes a breakthrough they are certain will alter humanity forever, Sam Altman, Elon Musk and the most prominent figures in Silicon Valley race to become part of their vision. As the technology becomes more powerful and more valuable than anyone ever imagined, a battle wages over who should control the tech that could change the fate of humanity.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Back to the Beach
movies.cast: Frankie Avalon, Annette Funicello, Lori Loughlin, Tommy Hinkley, Demian Slade, Joe Holland
movies.description:
Life can be hard for a stressed out car salesman in Ohio, even if you have the perfect wife and two children to carry on your legacy. But, when the husband and wife are played by Frankie Avalon and Annette Funicello, the beach will always call them back to its sandy shores. The beach blanket power couple are drawn to California to visit daughter Sandi (Lori Loughlin) on the way to Hawaii and get waylaid to help her sort out her life. The family soon encounters a series of hiccups that keep them in Cali longer than planned, but they have some fun along the way. The band Fishbone stops by to get groovy, Paul Reubens' Pee-wee Herman celebrates on the beach, and we get even more musical with Stevie Ray Vaughan and Dick Dale. All of this with more polka dots than you can shake a surfboard at. BACK TO THE BEACH might not make sense, but dammit it is fun. (Dede Crimmins)

movies.title: Batman Returns
movies.cast: Michael Keaton, Danny DeVito, Michelle Pfeiffer, Christopher Walken, Michael Gough, Pat Hingle
movies.description: Gotham City faces two monstrous criminal menaces: the bizarre, sinister Penguin (Danny DeVito) and the slinky, mysterious Catwoman (Michelle Pfeiffer). Can Batman (Michael Keaton) battle two formidable foes at once, especially when one wants to be mayor and the other is romantically attracted to Bruce Wayne? Like the groundbreaking 1989 original, BATMAN RETURNS is directed by the wizardly Tim Burton. And like the first blockbuster, it’s a dazzling adventure that leaves you breathless.

movies.title: Beginners
movies.cast: Ewan McGregor, Mélanie Laurent, Christopher Plummer, Goran Visnjic, Mary Page Keller, Kai Lennox
movies.description: Mike Mills’ Beginners imaginatively explores the hilarity, confusion, and surprises of love through the evolving consciousness of Oliver (Ewan McGregor). Oliver meets the irreverent and unpredictable Anna (Mélanie Laurent) only months after his father Hal Fields (Christopher Plummer) has passed away. This new love floods Oliver with memories of his father, who, following the death of his wife of 45 years, came out of the closet at age 75 to live a full, energized, and wonderfully tumultuous gay life – which included a younger boyfriend, Andy (Goran Visnjic). The upheavals of Hal’s new honesty, by turns funny and moving, brought father and son closer than they’d ever been able to be. Now Oliver endeavors to love Anna with all the bravery, humor, and hope that his father taught him.

movies.cast: Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Will Arnett

movies.title: Ben’imana
movies.cast: Clémentine U. Nyirinkindi, Kesia Kelly Nishimwe, Arivere Kagoyire, Isabelle Kabano, Antoinette Uwamahoro, Leocadie Uwabeza
movies.description:
In 2012, eighteen years after the genocide against the Tutsi, a Rwandan village is still learning how to live with itself. Vénéranda has spent years helping survivors and the families of those responsible speak the words that were never said between them. However, forgiveness comes easier when it’s someone else’s story. When her own daughter’s future becomes entangled with the past, Vénéranda is forced to find her own words at last.

Spanning three generations of women, BEN’IMANA is an intimate portrait of inherited silence — and the fragile question of whether people who have survived the unspeakable together can still build a life side by side.

movies.title: Billy Joel Tonight
movies.description: The BILLY JOEL TONIGHT concert film contains the original December 1976 performances from Connecticut College. Broadcast as a television special in 1977, this newly transferred, edited, restored, and mixed version captures Joel and his band at a crucial moment just before mainstream success arrived. Featured songs include “Captain Jack,” “New York State of Mind,” “Piano Man,” and many more.

movies.title: Billy Lynn's Long Halftime Walk
movies.cast: Joe Alwyn, Kristen Stewart, Chris Tucker, Garrett Hedlund, Makenzie Leigh, Vin Diesel
movies.description:
Four years after LIFE OF PI took the Oscars by storm, director Ang Lee returned to push the limits of digital filmmaking with BILLY LYNN'S LONG HALFTIME WALK. When 19-year-old American soldier Billy Lynn is brought home from Iraq as part of a publicity tour, he finds himself unable to reconcile the reality of combat with the pomp and circumstance greeting him stateside. What results is a hyperreal head trip that turns Billy - and the audience - inside out.

Shot in 4K UHD at 120 frames per second, and originally screened in 3D, BILLY LYNN is a technical and visual experiment unlike anything else released in major movie theaters. See it to believe it.
notes: Screening in 3D.

movies.title: Birth
movies.cast: Nicole Kidman, Cameron Bright, Danny Huston, Lauren Bacall, Alison Elliott, Arliss Howard
movies.description:
Ten years after her husband suddenly died, Anna (Nicole Kidman) has finally restarted her life and accepted a marriage proposal from her boyfriend. At the engagement party, a stranger wanders in to announce that he's Anna's dead husband. That stranger is a ten-year-old boy. Against her better judgment, Anna decides to hear him out.

Arguably the apex of a stretch of roles proving her to be the most adventurous movie star of her generation, Nicole Kidman gives a pitch-perfect performance in the chilly world Jonathan Glazer creates in BIRTH. (Mike Keegan)

movies.title: Bitter Christmas
movies.cast: Barbara Lennie, Leonardo Sbaraglia, Aitana Sanchez-Gijon
movies.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant. The film narrates the close relationship between reality and fiction, between inspiration and life, exploring the limits of autofiction and stories within stories.

movies.description: In Dolby Atmos! Harrison Ford stars in this fascinating, dark vision of the near future as a policeman who tracks engineered humans--a Blade Runner. In the year 2019, the police department forces Rick Deckard (Ford) out of retirement to hunt four genetically engineered humans who have come to earth. Designed to do difficult, hazardous work, the manufactured humans are stronger, faster and smarter than nonengineered humans. They feel no pain or remorse; they are almost indistinguishable from other humans ... and they are killing people. Now Deckard must stop them before they kill again. Based on the novel Do Androids Dream Of Electric Sheep? by Philip K. Dick.

Bowled over by actress Virginia Hill (Annette Bening), the dapper Siegel courts her, despite having a wife and children. Obsessed with creating a gambling haven, Siegel takes racketeering to the Nevada desert and helps develop Las Vegas, only to find himself in deep water over his reckless construction of the Flamingo Hotel.

movies.title: Burning

However, when Jongsu learns of Ben’s mysterious hobby and Haemi suddenly disappears, his confusion and obsessions begin to mount, culminating in a stunning finale.

movies.description: In an adaptation of Patricia Highsmith's seminal novel The Price of Salt, CAROL follows two women from very different backgrounds who find themselves in an unexpected love affair in 1950s New York. As conventional norms of the time challenge their undeniable attraction, an honest story emerges to reveal the resilience of the heart in the face of change. A young woman in her 20s, Therese Belivet (Rooney Mara), is a clerk working in a Manhattan department store and dreaming of a more fulfilling life when she meets Carol (Cate Blanchett), an alluring woman trapped in a loveless, convenient marriage. As an immediate connection sparks between them, the innocence of their first encounter dims and their connection deepens. While Carol breaks free from the confines of marriage, her husband (Kyle Chandler) begins to question her competence as a mother as her involvement with Therese and close relationship with her best friend Abby (Sarah Paulson) come to light.

movies.cast: Sophie Okonedo, David Oyelowo, India Amarteifio, Toheeb Jimoh, Ayo Edebiri
movies.description: Across a single day in Lagos, Nigeria, Clarissa (Sophie Okonedo) prepares to host a high society party at her home, as her complicated past begins to consume her, in the form of now-distant friends and loves from her youth. Simultaneously, Septimus (Fortune Nwafor), a young soldier, is haunted by his own memories of the horrors he has witnessed and endured. As the perspectives traverse past and present, across the bourgeois class and those too easily forgotten by society, a delicate portrait of contemporary Nigeria emerges. Directors Arie and Chuko, adapting Mrs. Dalloway by Virginia Woolf, take the renowned source material and deliver a unique and deeply felt story.

movies.cast: Karen Wasciuna, Stacie Arden Smith
movies.description: When a disturbing animal cruelty video spreads through Bangkok's suburbs, it deeply traumatizes 10-year-old Olivia. Soon after her beloved kitten disappears, she's abducted by a man who plans to sell her to a predator. As her parents desperately search for their daughter, they are forced to confront the darkest corners of humanity. Blending faith, trauma, revenge, and redemption, CRUSHED builds toward a shocking act of vigilante justice that challenges everything they believe.

movies.title: Dead City Punx
movies.description:
When COVID shut down venues in 2020, Los Angeles punk band Dead City Punx took their shows to the people—outside, under freeway overpasses, up the coast, to the desert and in otherwise abandoned spaces. Starting with their explosive breakout performance in Lafayette Park that drew nearly 5,000 fans while under fire from LAPD rubber bullets, this group of graffiti writers/musicians became LA’s most notorious DIY act.

Born from stolen equipment and street life connections, the band—Meka, Grumpy, Mike, and Adrian—built stages for their shows from shoplifted wood, used social media as their “bat signal,” and turned every performance into a crime scene complete with graffiti backdrops, bonfires, and police helicopters.

Through fan-filmed concert footage and exclusive interviews, Dead City captures how four outcasts from society’s margins ignited a pandemic-era music movement that challenged definitions of public space, rebellion, and the right to assemble. BEYOND THE STREETS presents the story of Dead City —raw, unfiltered and as real as their shows.

movies.title: Doctor Who: The Satan Pit
movies.description:
Celebrate Doctor Who Day with an exclusive big-screen event marking 20 years of the Tenth Doctor and Rose Tyler.

For the first time ever in cinemas, the acclaimed two-part adventure The Impossible Planet and The Satan Pit has been specially re-edited into a single movie-length presentation, created exclusively for theatrical audiences. Join the Doctor (David Tennant) and Rose (Billie Piper) as they travel to Sanctuary Base 6, a remote outpost perched on a planet orbiting a black hole. When an ancient force awakens beneath the surface, the crew find themselves trapped in a battle against an evil older than time itself.

This special Doctor Who Day screening also includes exclusive bonus material, featuring previously unseen content and a brand-new interview with a special guest, reflecting on the making of one of the most celebrated stories of the modern era – from encounters with the Ood to facing the terrifying Beast, alongside behind-the-scenes memories from the set.

movies.title: Dog Star Man
movies.cast: Stan Brakhage, Jane Wodening
movies.description:
A man and his dog struggle up a snow-covered mountain. The sun erupts, blood courses through veins, bodies merge with landscapes, and the boundaries between the microscopic and the cosmic dissolve. In Stan Brakhage’s monumental DOG STAR MAN (1961–64), a simple ascent becomes an ecstatic journey through the origins of life, the mysteries of perception, and the possibility of creating myth through cinema.

One of the towering achievements of American avant-garde filmmaking, this five-part epic (Prelude and Parts I–IV) abandons conventional narrative in favor of a radical exploration of vision itself. Through a dazzling interplay of superimpositions, shifting colors, fractured perspectives, and images of the natural world and the human body, Brakhage transforms a physical struggle into a spiritual and cosmic odyssey. Filmed with the collaboration of his wife, Jane Brakhage, and featuring the filmmaker himself and his dog as its protagonists, DOG STAR MAN collapses distinctions between inner and outer worlds, memory and imagination, the human and the universal.

DOG STAR MAN was selected for preservation and inducted into the National Film Registry by the Library of Congress in 1992.

Conceived by Brakhage as an intentionally silent work, in which the images themselves generate their own rhythm and music, DOG STAR MAN will be presented in its entirety on 16mm with a live, original musical accompaniment by The Flushing Remonstrance, the New York City-based duo of Catherine Cramer (percussion, electronics) and Robert Kennedy (keyboards, electronics, voice). Known for their adventurous sonic interpretations of silent and experimental cinema, including works by Kenneth Anger, Guy Maddin, and Dziga Vertov, the duo offers a contemporary sonic encounter with Brakhage's extraordinary universe of images.

movies.cast: Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Hassam Ghancy, Robert Pattinson, Florence Pugh, Anya Taylor-Joy, Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem

movies.cast: Will Ferrell, James Caan, Bob Newhart, Ed Asner, Mary Steenburgen, Zooey Deschanel
movies.description:
Don’t think ELF is one of the best holiday films ever? You sit on a throne of lies!

Christmas movies come and go, but few join the pantheon of the greats. You know the ones – A CHRISTMAS STORY, IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE, and MIRACLE ON 34TH STREET. These are just a few that are invited to sit at the adult table of holiday movies. While the last couple of decades have been pretty sparse when it comes to quality Christmas movies, ELF, the 2003 Will Ferrell comedy, undoubtedly has taken a corner seat at this proverbial table of fame.

Directed by Jon Favreau, ELF is one of those Christmas movies that's impossible to not love It's funny in all the right places, highly quotable, and surprisingly tender. It's Will Ferrell at his Ferrellist.

Don't miss a full night of pointy-toed, jingle bell bliss – especially if you need a pick-me-up in the holiday cheer department – because attending ELF is the Christmas spirit equivalent of putting syrup on your spaghetti.

movies.title: Elsinore
movies.cast: Andrew Scott, Olivia Colman, Billie Piper, Monica Dolan, David Webber, David Rintoul
movies.description: The deeply emotional and inspirational true story of Ian Charleson, a gifted actor whose greatest challenge becomes his greatest triumph. Facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit and grace, Charleson delivers a courageous performance that becomes a source of healing and inspiration for those around him.

movies.title: Elsinore
movies.cast: Andrew Scott, Olivia Colman, Johnny Flynn, Billie Piper
movies.description: In the face of mortality, Scottish actor Ian Charleson (Andrew Scott) takes on his greatest challenge and transforms it into his greatest triumph. Set in London 1989, this biographical drama tells the inspirational true story of Charleson’s acclaimed performance as Hamlet at the National Theatre while living with AIDS. Directed by Simon Stone ( The Dig ), Elsinore explores not only the enduring power of Charleson’s work, but also the profound impact of his courage, wit, and grace on those around him during the final months of his life. A moving tribute to the healing and transformative power of theater.

movies.title: Enter the Void
movies.cast: Nathaniel Brown, Paz de la Huerta, Cyril Roy, Ed Spear
movies.description:
Provocative, audacious and visionary, Gaspar Noé ( Irreversible ) pushes the boundaries of hallucinatory cinema with this exploration of sex, drugs, life and death. A brother and sister scratch out a living in Tokyo’s underworld–Oscar’s a small-time dealer, Linda (Paz de la Huerta, The Limits of Control ) is an exotic dancer. One night, a police bust goes horribly wrong, and Oscar is shot. But as he lies dying, his spirit refuses to leave the world. Instead, it wanders through the city, its visions growing ever more distorted and nightmarish.

“Four stars! A tour de force… strong contender for both the artiest drug movie and the druggiest art movie ever made… [the climax] leaves you dazed, elated and absolutely awestruck.” – David Fear, Time Out New York

“Terrifying and surpassingly beautiful… a revolutionary break from ordinary movie storytelling… daring, thrilling… with this movie Noe jumps to the front rank of mindf**k acid-trip filmmakers, right next to David Lynch, and I wandered out afterwards… feeling dazzled, dizzy, exhausted, grateful… love, hate, disgust, arousal, amazement — all are appropriate reactions to one of the most mind-blowing and ambitious feature films ever made.” – Andrew O’Hehir, Salon

Screening as part of Late Night Favorites: Fall 2026

Previously screened as part of our 2025 series 20 Films for 20 Years and our 2022 series Too Much Is Never Enough: The Films of Gaspar Noé

movies.title: Eyes Wide Shut
movies.cast: Tom Cruise, Nicole Kidman, Sydney Pollack, Marie Richardson, Rade Šerbedžija, Todd Field
movies.description:
In IT’S A WONDERFUL LIFE, Jimmy Stewart’s George Bailey, at the height of his suicidal despair and panic, imagines a world in which he doesn’t exist. Stanley Kubrick goes one step further in sending Tom Cruise down an odyssey of sexual confusion and paranoia to learn the true meaning of Christmas.

Adapted from the Austrian short story Traumnovelle , Kubrick’s final film peeks us into the privileged world of Dr. Bill Hartford and his wife Alice (Cruise and Nicole Kidman), two well-to-do attractive socialites who, by all accounts, have it made. In a marijuana-fueled argument, Alice reveals thoughts of infidelity that send Bill into an existential panic, leading to an absurdist walkabout through New York that involves – you guessed it – a mysterious sex cult run by a shrouded aristocracy.

Did Kubrick make this to break up Cruise and Kidman’s marriage? How much did he know about mysterious sex trafficking rings? Did Sydney Pollack originate the shirtless-in-suspenders look? Clearly, the film poses more questions than it answers. For certain, EYES WIDE SHUT is a brutally funny sexscapade that puts an ellipses at the end of Kubrick’s storied career – and, most importantly – stands as a crucial text for our modern world. Fidelio!

movies.cast: Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro, Ariana Grande, Skyler Gisondo, Owen Wilson, Blythe Danner

movies.title: Game
movies.cast: Dulquer Salmaan, Kayadu Lohar, Antony Varghese, Mysskin, Kathir, Samyuktha Viswanathan
movies.description: In late summer 1993, a tense and claustrophobic battle of wills and wits unfolds after aging raver David (Marc Bessant) steals a stash of money and drugs, then crashes his car deep in the woods. Trapped in the wreckage, injured and helpless, he hangs suspended between life and death. When a mysterious poacher (Jason Williamson) discovers him, no rescue comes – only a watchful, unsettling presence that seems intent on letting nature finish the job. As the hours stretch and the elements close in, survival hinges on outlasting both the wilderness and the predator at its edge.

movies.title: Gassan + Woman of Tokyo
movies.description: At the twilight of his life, a man spends the winter in a village at the foot of Mount Gassan, a holy site venerated for millennia. Finding refuge in a snow-buried temple, he has a mystical experience on the frontiers of the living and the dead. The Theater of the Matters is proud to present the first US screening of Shinji Somai’s rare and deeply personal final film, completed shortly before the director’s death from cancer in 2001. Produced as an installment in “Reading Journey: Masterpieces of Japan,” an experimental public television program, Gassan is a marvel of spare means: shot on location in just four days with an HD camera, one performer, and a small crew. In a series of intricately orchestrated long takes, actor Akira Emoto recites the text of the eponymous 1974 novel by Atsushi Mori, a fictionalized account of the writer’s travels in remote Northern Japan, suffused with the region’s language and folk traditions. Gassan will be followed by a 35mm screening of Woman of Tokyo , a furious, oblique Depression-era silent film by Somai favorite Yasujiro Ozu, presented without accompaniment. Gassan (2001) Dir. Shinji Somai With Akira Emoto 52min; Digital In Japanese with English subtitles Woman of Tokyo (1933) Dir. Yasujiro Ozu With Yoshiko Okada, Ureo Egawa 45min; 35mm In Japanese intertitles with English subtitles

movies.director: Mark Polonia, Todd Michael Smith, John Polonia
movies.cast: John Polonia, Mark Polonia, Todd Michael Smith

Filmed on a family camcorder during the dead of winter in Pennsylvania, this is a warped take on POLTERGEIST from siblings Mark and John Polonia with friend (and future gay underground filmmaker) Todd Michael Smith. Eerie, surreal, and containing surprisingly thoughtful themes, HALLUCINATIONS is an impressive mix of splatter-filled chaos and homoerotic phantasms. (Joseph A. Ziemba, Bleeding Skull)

movies.title: Joan of Arc
movies.cast: Ingrid Bergman
movies.description: “From the time I was a little girl, [Joan of Arc] has always been my greatest heroine,” recalled Ingrid Bergman. “Instead of saving butterflies or stamps, my hobby was to look for things about Joan of Arc, and to collect books and medals and statues of her... She became the character I liked to play most.” Bergman spent her first decade in Hollywood trying to persuade producers to give her an opportunity to play the Maid of Orleans. (“There’s no love story in it,” sniffed David O. Selznick.) Finally Bergman played the role on stage in Maxwell Anderson’s Joan of Lorraine , winning a Tony for her performance. Anderson adapted the play to the screen for this lavish independent production, shot in Technicolor at the Hal Roach Studio under the direction of Victor Fleming, who had guided Bergman through her early triumph in DR. JEKYLL AND MR. HYDE (1941). The epic rendition of Joan’s military campaign and trial was accorded road show treatment before being cut by 45 minutes for general release. JOAN OF ARC won Academy Awards® for its cinematography and costumes, and producer Walter Wanger received a special honorary Oscar® for “distinguished service to the industry in adding to its moral stature in the world community by his production of the picture Joan of Arc”—an honor he refused because the Academy had failed to supply a Best Picture nomination, too.

movies.cast: Kate Winslet, Jennifer Connelly, Patrick Wilson
movies.description: Sarah (Kate Winslet) is a well-educated woman who cannot come to terms with her life as a housewife and mother. Brad (Patrick Wilson), a stay-at-home dad, is married to a beautiful filmmaker (Jennifer Connelly) and goes skateboarding instead of studying for the bar exam. movies.title: Little Mother
movies.cast: Christiane Krüger, Siegfried Rauch, Ivan Desny, Mark Damon, Anton Diffring, Elga Sorbas
movies.description:
Marina Pinares, the wife of the president of a South American country, insists on being his vice-presidential running mate in the next election. She's no stranger to assassination to get what she wants, so some suspect she'll kill her own husband after the election to become president. In a series of flashbacks we see her rise to power: a party girl willing to sacrifice a friend's virtue to gain favor; the lover of a soldier she later tortures; the mistress of the military man she soon marries.

Based on the life of Eva Peron and directed by adult filmmaker Radley Metzger (SCORE, THE OPENING OF MISTY BEETHOVEN), LITTLE MOTHER is a rarely-seen tale of political intrigue that's ready for rediscovery.

movies.title: Little Women
movies.cast: Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Florence Pugh, Eliza Scanlen, Laura Dern, Timothée Chalamet

showtimes.label: Sad Girl Cinema Club · Lower Manhattan
Sad Girl Cinema Club · Staten Island
Sad Girl Cinema Club · Downtown Brooklyn

movies.description:
Having already once revolutionized the coming-of-age story with her debut LADY BIRD, Greta Gerwig has somehow outdone herself with this gorgeous and thoroughly original rendition of the beloved Louisa May Alcott classic. Bringing her effusive humor, authenticity, and irresistible warmth to the otherwise mannered Civil War-era New England, Gerwig's adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN breathes visceral new life into the March sisters – portraying them as unique, complicated, flawed, and astonishingly human. So human that you will leave the theater wanting to text Jo March and, for several reasons, this will not be a possibility.

You may also find it physically impossible not to chef's kiss at the cast, which is as close to pitch-perfect as it gets. Starring Saoirse Ronan as Jo, Emma Watson as Meg, Florence Pugh as Amy, and Eliza Scanlen as Beth, LITTLE WOMEN also features Laura Dern (!), Meryl Streep (!), Bob Odenkirk (!), and Timothée Chalamet as the dashing but lovelorn Laurie (!!!).

Save for a fireworks show, sky-written ode, or Mount Rushmore-type situation, we cannot recommend this rich, heartrending wonder of a film anymore. Its timeless charm is sure to capture the hearts of little women (and men) everywhere.

movies.title: Look Back
movies.cast: Natsuki Deguchi, Aju Makita, Furi Nanase, Rokka Okada
movies.description: Palme d’Or winner Kore-eda’s ( Shoplifters, Monster ) latest, adapted from the beloved manga, is a love letter to the artistic process and a meditation on friendship. Confident grade-schooler Fujino’s comics are adored by her classmates. But one day, her work is upstaged by a reclusive peer. When the two girls finally meet, however, Fujino discovers that the other girl has been her devoted fan all along. Bound by their shared passion, they become the closest of artistic collaborators, until a fateful event changes their lives forever.

movies.cast: Diane Keaton, Tuesday Weld, William Atherton, Richard Kiley, Richard Gere
movies.description: Raised in a strict Catholic family, Theresa (Diane Keaton) teaches deaf children during the day and cruises singles bars and discos at night. Theresa favors rough sex with random suitors, ignoring the advances of well-meaning but nerdy social worker James (William Atherton). Instead, Theresa pursues the likes of Tony (Richard Gere), whose threatening knife and swagger excite her.

movies.title: Lucid
movies.cast: Philip Albrecht Bartels, Danny Rohrback
movies.description:
It’s 1994, and art student Mia Sunshine Jones must pass her self portrait project or be kicked out of school. The problem is that she can’t seem to figure out who the hell she really is!

She is desperate to break free of her terrible creative block and finds her last hope in a magical Lucid Dreaming Elixir. The potion sparks her creativity but also unleashes dark monsters from her subconscious. As Mia battles these creatures, including a Fried Chicken Monster, her art flourishes! When her estranged mother appears as a hairy monster, Mia must face the truth about her past.

movies.title: Lunar Sway
movies.cast: Liza Weil, Douglas Smith, Noah Parker, Irina Dubova, Mark Acheson, John Tench
movies.description: Cliff is an eccentric young man looking for love in all the wrong places. When his estranged birth mother, Marg, shows up unexpectedly, they quickly bond, but she has her share of secrets and ulterior motives, and is being followed into town by a vengeful figure from her past.

movies.title: L’Innocente
movies.cast: Giancarlo Giannini, Laura Antonelli, Jennifer O’Neill In Italian with English subtitles
movies.description: A loose adaptation of Gabriele D’Annunzio’s 1892 novel, L’INNOCENTE is set in aristocratic Rome at the turn of the 20th century, wealthy and self-absorbed nobleman Tullio Hermil (Giannini) carries on an affair with a sophisticated yet possessive widow, Countess Teresa Raffo (O’Neill), while treating his devoted wife, Giuliana (Antonelli), with cold condescension. Wounded by his years of neglect, Giuliana takes a lover of her own with young novelist, Filippo (Marc Porel). When she becomes pregnant with Filippo’s child, Tullio’s wounded pride cannot be contained, setting off a chain of events leading to ultimate tragedy.

movies.title: Mars Attacks!
movies.cast: Jack Nicholson, Glenn Close, Annette Bening, Pierce Brosnan, Danny DeVito, Martin Short
movies.description:
How do you follow the success of gargantuan blockbusters like BATMAN and BATMAN RETURNS? Well, if you’re oddball director Tim Burton, you decide to make a campy, violent, big-budget alien invasion comedy based on a series of sci-fi trading cards from the 1960s.

With an absurdly star-studded cast, including Pierce Brosnan, Glenn Close, Annette Bening, Danny DeVito, Michael J. Fox, Martin Short, Natalie Portman, Jack Black, Sarah Jessica Parker's head on a chihuahua’s body, and Jack Nicholson in two different roles, MARS ATTACKS! is a demented piece of retro-pop madness that represents Tim Burton at his very best. If you've never seen this epic, raucously funny cult classic, don't miss your chance to experience it on the big screen.

movies.title: Megalopolis
movies.cast: Adam Driver, Giancarlo Esposito, Nathalie Emmanuel, Aubrey Plaza, Shia LaBeouf, Jon Voight
movies.description:
Like the famed empire that Francis Ford Coppola’s epic passion project is styled after, MEGALOPOLIS is a towering, monumental spectacle that most people will think about at least once a day. The City of New Rome is at a crossroads. At one end sits Cesar Catilina (Adam Driver), the idealistic artist striving for a utopian future, and at the other sits Mayor Franklin Cicero (Giancarlo Esposito), a powerful figure perpetuating greed, special interests, and partisan warfare. Their titanic struggle will shake the foundations of their city and lay the groundwork for a new tomorrow.

As engrossing and ambitious as you would expect from the filmmaker behind THE GODFATHER and APOCALYPSE NOW, MEGALOPOLIS is an unforgettable vision that could only have come from Coppola. Of course, he didn’t do it alone, and everyone in the unbelievable cast (including Driver, Esposito, Nathalie Emmanuel, Aubrey Plaza, Laurence Fishburne, and more) delivers some of the most memorable performances of their careers.

movies.title: Metropolis
movies.cast: Alfred Abel, Brigitte Helm, Gustav Fröhlich, Rudolf Klein-Rogge
movies.description: Incorporating more than 25 minutes of newly discovered footage, this 2010 restoration of Metropolis is the definitive edition of Fritz Lang’s science fiction masterpiece. Backed by a new recording of Gottfried Huppertz’s 1927 score (presented here in 5.1 Stereo Surround), the film’s dazzling visual design and special effects are more striking than ever. And the integration of scenes and subplots long considered lost endows Metropolis with even greater tension and emotional resonance, as it dramatizes the conflict between wealthy über-capitalists and rebellious subterranean laborers—orchestrated by a diabolical scientist capable of destroying them both.
notes: Preceded by the restored “Superman” short The Mechanical Monsters from Fleischer Studios.

movies.title: Millennium Actress
movies.cast: Miyoko Shôji, Shôzô Îzuka, Mami Koyama
movies.description:
Experience the gorgeous new restoration of what many believe to be Satoshi Kon’s ( Perfect Blue, Paprika, Tokyo Godfathers ) greatest work, Millennium Actress .

When the legendary Ginei Studios shuts down, filmmaker Genya Tachibana and his assistant are tasked with interviewing its reclusive star, Chiyoko Fujiwara, who had retired from the spotlight 30 years prior. As she recounts her career, Genya and his crew are literally pulled into her memories where they witness her chance encounter with a mysterious man on the run from the police. Despite never knowing his name or his face, Chiyoko relentlessly pursues that man in a seamless blend of reality and memory that only Satoshi Kon could deliver.

Boasting countless awards, including the Grand Prize in the Japan Agency of Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival, which it shared with Hayao Miyazaki’s Spirited Away , Millennium Actress is a must-see for anime fans of all ages.

movies.title: Minotaur
movies.cast: Dmitriy Mazurov, Iris Lebedeva, Boris Kudrin
movies.description: Russian corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) is under siege on all fronts: haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful and facing a demand to draft a quota of employees for war. Though he’s desperate to keep his hands clean, his struggle to reassert control accelerates toward violence. Loosely based on Claude Chabrol’s 1969 film The Unfaithful Wife , this new feature by veteran, exiled Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev ( Loveless , Leviathan ) won the Grand Prix and Cannes Soundtrack Award at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in May.

movies.title: Misery
movies.cast: Kathy Bates, James Caan, Richard Farnsworth, Lauren Bacall, Frances Sternhagen, Graham Jarvis
movies.description: Imagine any artist's worst nightmare of running into a crazed "#1 fan" who takes you hostage and forces you to "dance like a monkey" to play out their own sadistic fantasies. Maybe Stephen King was thinking about this when writing MISERY, a book and movie about a famous author (James Caan) who gets into a violent car accident and is then saved, coincidentally, by his "#1 fan." What unfolds is an absolute nightmare of seclusion, captivity, and abuse that reaches a boiling climax of white-knuckle suspense! This is easily one of the best King adaptions.

movies.title: Moulin Rouge!
movies.cast: Ewan McGregor, Nicole Kidman, John Leguizamo, Jim Broadbent, Richard Roxburgh, Garry McDonald
movies.description:
If you’re a true romantic, you already know the story: Christian (Ewan McGregor) moves to Paris to pursue a Bohemian lifestyle and then, of course, falls into a doomed love affair with Satine (Nicole Kidman), the most beautiful girl at the Moulin Rouge.

Your heart will swell! Your lungs will burst! Your brain will explode with rainbows! Bring a date, or else make sure you choose your seat carefully because you WILL end up falling in love with the person sitting next to you.

movies.title: Mystery Transmission
movies.description: At the stroke of midnight, otherdimensional creatures invade a local cable station. That’s Video Vortex: a monthly mystery transmission from the outer limits of home video history, featuring J-horror nightmares, underground gore, tokusatsu battle-parties, and lost TV broadcasts you can’t see anywhere else. Warm up the cathode tubes, dim the lights, and let your senses intermingle with the glow.

movies.title: National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation
movies.cast: Chevy Chase, Beverly D'Angelo, Juliette Lewis, Johnny Galecki, John Randolph, Diane Ladd
movies.description:

Fueled by the ambitious programming executive Diana Christensen, the focus of the network takes on a new trashy but lucrative turn that is to the disappointment of the news division president Max Schumacher (Beale’s longtime friend and Christensen’s occasional lover). movies.title: Nuisance Bear
movies.cast: Mike Tunalaaq Gibbons, Saad Kassis-Mohamed
movies.description:
Winner of the U.S. Documentary Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Film Festival and hailed by Werner Herzog as “truly groundbreaking”, Nuisance Bear places viewers inside the world of a polar bear to deliver a cinematic pressure cooker and an urgent parable for our times.

Filmmakers Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman follow a polar bear in Churchill, Manitoba — the self-styled “Polar Bear Capital of the World” — forced to navigate tourists, wildlife officers and hunters as climate change pushes it into town.

Guided by Inuit narrator Mike Tunalaaq Gibbons, whose perspective resists simplification, Nuisance Bear overturns the conventions of the nature documentary to ask: when a sacred predator is branded a “nuisance,” who truly belongs in this shared landscape?

movies.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
movies.cast: Aaron Douglas, Richard Bruce Nugent, Ernest Crichlow, Eubie Blake, Leigh Whipper, Arna Bontemps
movies.description:
A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance. For four hours, this extraordinary group – many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years – reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape.

Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance. William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive.

movies.title: Point Blank
movies.cast: Lee Marvin, Angie Dickinson, John Vernon, Keenan Wynn, Carroll O'Connor, Lloyd Bochner
movies.description:
British director John Boorman brought a European sensibility to a Los Angeles neo-noir: POINT BLANK is Antonioni plus violence, Francesco Rosi without politics. The title reverberates like a pun-point: blank. Lee Marvin is Walker, left for dead in an Alcatraz heist and now out to find the $93,000 he has coming. No more, no less, unless you count revenge. The trail leads to the City of Angels and the syndicate that runs it out of car lots and Santa Monica penthouses, the kind of places you know exist only with a little larceny. Picking up on the modern surface of his locale, Boorman takes a champagne-blonde color scheme to a hallucinatory degree, blonde on blond, like Angie Dickinson's bouffant and Marvin's silvery pate (here, we have the bad, the brunette, and the bald). Los Angeles is inherently horizontal. The payoff, visually and narratively, occurs in that storm drain affectionately known as the L.A. River, viewed from a bridge over imagined waters. (BAMPFA)

movies.title: Romeo + Juliet
movies.cast: Leonardo DiCaprio, Claire Danes, Jesse Bradford, Vondie Curtis-Hall, Brian Dennehy, John Leguizamo
movies.description:
"Dost thou get it?" asked the TV commercials for director Baz Luhrmann's ROMEO + JULIET in the fall of 1996. For millions of young moviegoers, the answer was definitely yes: they were spellbound by the allure of Leonardo DiCaprio and Claire Danes (both so amazingly young and fresh-faced!) as Shakespeare's star-crossed couple.

Most viewers also enjoyed Luhrmann's wildly outside-the-box depiction of the Capulets and the Montagues as feuding mafia-style families in violent Verona Beach, where gangsters and hipsters rule the bullet-riddled streets. Five years before MOULIN ROUGE!, Luhrmann introduced the world to his pop-operatic style, incorporating gorgeous visuals, stunning sets, and modern hits like the Cardigans' "Lovefool," club classics like Kym Mazelle's cover of "Young Hearts Run Free," and even a choral version of Prince's "When Doves Cry" into his romantic tapestry. This was a far cry from the stuffy, stilted Shakespeare most of us snoozed through in school; even if you couldn't understand every phrase, Luhrmann made sure you got the meaning.

The movie was an international hit, and DiCaprio and Danes – both better known for their TV appearances than their movies at this point – would, of course, go on to have extraordinary careers. Twenty years later, ROMEO + JULIET remains one of the liveliest, most imaginative, and surprisingly moving interpretations of the Bard ever to hit the screen.

movies.title: Rossellini 120
movies.description:
Roberto Rossellini entered Italy’s film industry as a sound effects man before becoming a screenwriter. Summing up his time writing for others, Rossellini declared, “I was their slave.” He maintained his disdain for scripts in a career that swerved between fiction and documentary, cinema and television, present-day reality and the lessons of history.

Rossellini’s breakthrough came with ROME, OPEN CITY , the film that revitalized Italy’s battered industry, brought a new frankness to the screen, introduced moviegoers around the world to the legendary Anna Magnani, and helped prove that international films could be big box office in U.S. arthouses. His next two films, PAISAN and GERMANY YEAR ZERO, became classics of “Neorealism” in their own right. Rossellini’s iconoclasm would later prompt François Truffaut to famously cite him as the father of the French New Wave as well.

Following his neorealist trilogy, Rossellini moved on to L’AMORE, a two-part film starring both Magnani and OPEN CITY co-screenwriter Federico Fellini, the latter in a controversial episode (“Il Miracolo”) that spurred a landmark U.S. Supreme Court case; the dark satire THE MACHINE TO KILL BAD PEOPLE; and THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS , a loose biographical film of Saint Francis of Assisi.

After receiving a fan letter from Hollywood star Ingrid Bergman, Rossellini cast her in his next film, STROMBOLI , a visceral character study shot on location on the Sicilian island. The film’s artistry was overshadowed by the tabloid-fueled scandal provoked by Rossellini’s affair with Bergman and their protracted divorces. The couple made four more features together: EUROPE ‘51, FEAR, JOAN OF ARC AT THE STAKE and the masterpiece of the collaboration, VOYAGE TO ITALY . A new 4K restoration of the latter by Cinecittà labs will have its New York premiere as part of the Rossellini retrospective.

“I have never been able to do what I wanted to do from beginning to end,” Rossellini once lamented in an interview. “In cinema, my desire to speculate has been stronger than my desire for survival.” Rossellini actually wound up doing both, speculating and surviving, crafting a body of work that evolved alongside an industry whose assembly-line method he so vehemently rejected. Tossed together, shakily financed, and often refined during shooting to conform to an obscure plan Rossellini kept in his own head, the films retain a sense of dangerous spontaneity.

movies.title: September Songs: The Music of Kurt Weill
movies.description:
September Songs: The Music of Kurt Weill is a fusion of film, theatre, and concert performance that reimagines the music of the German composer Kurt Weill whose songs bridged opera, cabaret, and popular music with piercing social and emotional insight.

Featuring an extraordinary ensemble — Teresa Stratas, Lou Reed, Nick Cave, PJ Harvey, Charlie Haden, Elvis Costello & The Brodsky Quartet, Betty Carter, Mary Margaret O’Hara, William S. Burroughs, and more — September Songs transforms Weill’s work into a haunting collage of performance, theatre, and cinema. Each artist reinvents Weill’s legacy through their own lens, creating a living dialogue between past and present, exile and belonging, beauty and decay. Blended throughout the film are stylized “documentaries”, evocative imagery, and cinematic transitions that transform Weill’s haunting melodies and biting social commentary into a contemporary meditation on art, exile, and the human condition. The film celebrates Weill’s enduring influence on 20th-century music and culture.

Through its visuals, its music and its original choreography, the film merges concert, cabaret, and expressionist cinema into a single dreamlike experience. The restoration — undertaken by Sphinx Productions with the generous support of Telefilm Canada — faithfully revives the film’s original textures, sound design, and the distinctive cinematography of celebrated German DOP Horst Zeidler, preserving a landmark of Canadian music cinema for new audiences worldwide.

Sundays on Fire: Secret Hong Kong 35mm Feature
movies.description:
Warning: Images are not from the movies we’re showing. Trust us, you can’t imagine what we’re showing!

A career-making film from the late-90s, this caper flick rarely gets screened, but it turned out to be a landmark for both its director and its stars. An anthem to urban loneliness, job dissatisfaction, and unconsummated romance, it’s as light on its feet as Ocean’s 11 , as stylish as North By Northwest , and as heart-achingly emotional as a Cantopop power ballad. Featuring two of Hong Kong’s biggest stars playing lonely men who re-discover their love of life by shooting at each other, it’s a rousing, ridiculous, over-the-top supernova of fun, that reminds us this holiday season that what we have to be thankful for are Hong Kong movies.

movies.title: Tally Brown, New York
movies.cast: Tally Brown, Paul Ambrose, Edward Caton, Divine, Gil Fontaine, Elizabeth Kashy
movies.description:
2K restoration by the Deutsche Kinemathek

“The bewigged Miss Brown, with false eyelashes capable of sending her short, round body aloft, is the most memorable raconteur and cabaret artist you’ll hear all year.” – Melissa Anderson, The Village Voice

Both a loving portrait of a larger-than-life personality and a vivid record of New York’s 1970s downtown demimonde, this captivating documentary follows Tally Brown—cabaret chanteuse, underground film star, and a staple of Andy Warhol’s Factory—as she takes filmmaker Rosa von Praunheim on a tour through the grit and glamour of the city that made her. Capturing Brown’s mesmerizing performances (including her breathtaking bilingual cover of David Bowie’s “Heroes”) as well as her social world among fellow queer cult icons like Holly Woodlawn, Divine, and Taylor Mead, Tally Brown, New York is an essential snapshot of a scene that has passed into legend.

movies.description: As the demands of work and family begin to converge, two best-friend social workers and those closest to them discover the strength found in compassion, community, and one another. Set in post-Brexit England, Mike Leigh’s Tender Loving Care is a richly observed portrait of resilience, humor, and the enduring power of human connection. “As great as anything he’s ever produced,” The Daily Beast proclaims of the feature that might be Leigh’s last, “a small-scale domestic drama that reverberates loudly, and urgently, as a celebration of everyday compassion and solidarity.”

movies.title: The Apartment
movies.cast: Jack Lemmon, Shirley MacLaine, Fred MacMurray, Ray Walston, Jack Kruschen, David Lewis
movies.description:
A young upstart, C.C. Baxter (Jack Lemmon), will do anything to move up in the world...even loan out his apartment to the higher-ups for their romantic flings and extramarital trysts. All seems relatively fine and dandy until C.C. finds a romance of his own.

Billy Wilder is a genius – there aren't enough words in the world to describe all the films he's made and express how much he means to cinema – but in 1960, Wilder wrote and directed a perfect movie. I'm not saying this to sell you on the idea of seeing this film at the Alamo; I'm stating it as a fact. There are very few instances where you watch a movie and realize you are witnessing pure magnificence in that moment. Sometimes you think about a movie after the fact, and it gets better and better until you begin to love a movie you previously only really liked. THE APARTMENT is NOT one of those movies. It is a movie where, within 15 minutes of watching, you realize it is unlike anything you have ever seen before. Jack Lemmon is amazing, Shirley MacLaine is a full-on pixie dream girl, and the chemistry and dialogue snap and sparkle like you wouldn't believe.

After failing with his new team of misfits, Buttermaker enlists feisty and gifted pitcher Amanda Whurlitzer to lead the charge -- but can he find the luck and patience to whip these outcasts into shape?

movies.title: The comedy genius of Sid Caesar
movies.description: In the early 1950s, 20 million people tuned into see the weekly TV extravaganza Your Show of Shows , starring Sid Caesar, a master of physical comedy, “double talk” and pantomime, supported by “second bananas” Imogene Coca, Carl Reiner, and Howard Morris, and a truly legendary writing staff that included Reiner, Lucille Kallen, Mel Tolkin, Mel Brooks, and Neil Simon (and, later, Woody Allen). This special compilation of some of Caesar’s greatest sketches, from Your Show of Shows and the later Caesar’s Hour , will be followed by an onstage conversation with Bruce Goldstein, Film Forum’s Founding Repertory Artistic Director (and Caesar fanatic), and longtime New York Times and Vanity Fair writer David Margolick, author of the definitive biography When Caesar Was King: How Sid Caesar Reinvented American Comedy (Schocken Books).
