movies.title: The Debut
movies.cast: Julianne Moore, Paul Giamatti, Halle Bailey, Jesse Eisenberg, Bernadette Peters, Craig Bierko
movies.description: When Mona Friedman (Julianne Moore) is cast in a bit part at a small community theater, she transforms from a shy, unassuming housewife into a zealous method actor willing to do anything to protect the artistic integrity of her marginal role—even if it means waging war against the show’s domineering director, Jerry Blankenbuehler (Paul Giamatti). “You are watching a woman who can’t act being played by a woman who very much can,” the Daily Telegraph reports, “and the result is as psychologically scrambling as it is spiritually elating.”

movies.title: The Departed
movies.cast: Leonardo DiCaprio, Matt Damon, Jack Nicholson, Mark Wahlberg, Martin Sheen, Ray Winstone
movies.description:
"If they're lucky, directors make one classic film in their career. Martin Scorsese has one per decade (TAXI DRIVER in the '70s, RAGING BULL in the '80s, GOODFELLAS in the '90s). His 2006 Irish Mafia masterpiece kept the streak alive." – Entertainment Weekly

In South Boston, the state police force is waging war on Irish-American organized crime. Young undercover cop Billy Costigan (Leonardo DiCaprio) is assigned to infiltrate the mob syndicate run by gangland chief Frank Costello (Jack Nicholson). While Billy quickly gains Costello's confidence, Colin Sullivan (Matt Damon), a hardened young criminal who has infiltrated the state police as an informer for the syndicate, is rising to a position of power in the Special Investigation Unit. Each man becomes deeply consumed by his double life, gathering information about the plans and counter-plans of the operations he has penetrated. But when it becomes clear to both the mob and the police that there's a mole in their midst, Billy and Colin are suddenly in danger of being caught and exposed to the enemy – and each must race to uncover the identity of the other man in time to save himself. But is either willing to turn on the friends and comrades they've made during their long stints undercover?

movies.title: The Friend’s House Is Here
movies.cast: Mahshad Bahram, Hana Mana, Farzad Karen, Zohreh Pirnia, Parham Ghanavat, Erfan Tehranifar
movies.description: In Tehran’s underground art scene, Pari, a theater director, and Hanna, a dancer, are roommates, best friends, actors, and professional partners, navigating rehearsals, performances, and the quiet rituals of everyday life while confronting the ethical compromises and political pressures that increasingly shape their futures. Shot in secret but far removed from familiar portrayals of Iran, directors Ataei and Keshavarz blur the boundaries between theatrical performance and lived experience, crafting a luminous portrait of sisterhood where art becomes inseparable from life and even the smallest creative choices can become acts of resistance.

movies.title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
movies.cast: Brad Pitt, Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, Karren Karagulian
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: The History of Concrete
movies.cast: John Wilson, Michael Imperioli, Jack Macco, Nathan Fielder, Timothée Chalamet, Josh Safdie
movies.description: Following the finale of his acclaimed HBO series, How To with John Wilson , documentarian John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure. Concrete, the world's most widely used building material, appears as an ever-present life force, and John sets out to make the definitive documentary on the matter. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he decides to use the industry-approved Hallmark formula to tell this seemingly drab story and increase his movie’s appeal. But his foundation soon begins to crumble—literally and figuratively—as he struggles to balance artistic freedom with the realities of the modern film industry.

movies.title: The Holiday
movies.cast: Cameron Diaz, Kate Winslet, Jude Law, Jack Black, Eli Wallach, Edward Burns
movies.description: We could all use an escape every now and then. That’s certainly true for Amanda (Cameron Diaz) and Iris (Kate Winslet), two strangers who connect online and temporarily swap houses as a means of escaping from the stresses of their lives. And we’re inviting you to escape with us for a little bit with this special screening of Nancy Meyers’ utterly charming rom-com, THE HOLIDAY. With charismatic movie stars, enchanting settings, and a heaping helping of humor and romance, it’ll feel like a mini-vacation in the middle of your busy season.

movies.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
movies.cast: Joseph Zada, Jennifer Lawrence, Mckenna Grace, Ralph Fiennes, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin, Maya Hawke, Glenn Close, Lili Taylor
movies.description: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping revisits the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games , starting on the morning of the reaping of the 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell.

movies.title: The Last Waltz
movies.cast: Robbie Robertson, Rick Danko, Levon Helm, Richard Manuel, Garth Hudson, Eric Clapton
movies.description: Seventeen years after joining forces as the backing band for rockabilly cult hero Ronnie Hawkins, Canadian roots rockers The Band call it quits with a lavish farewell show at San Francisco’s Winterland Ballroom on Nov. 25, 1976. Filmed by Martin Scorsese, this documentary features standout performances by rock legends such as Bob Dylan, Van Morrison, Eric Clapton, Joni Mitchell and Muddy Waters, as well as interviews tracing the group’s history and discussing road life.

movies.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
movies.cast: Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Liv Tyler, Viggo Mortensen, Sean Astin, Cate Blanchett
movies.description: The future of civilization rests in the fate of the One Ring, which has been lost for centuries. Powerful forces are unrelenting in their search for it. But fate has placed it in the hands of a young Hobbit named Frodo Baggins (Elijah Wood), who inherits the Ring and steps into legend. A daunting task lies ahead for Frodo when he becomes the Ringbearer – to destroy the One Ring in the fires of Mount Doom where it was forged.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power
movies.description: Set thousands of years before the events of J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings , this epic drama follows an ensemble cast of characters, both familiar and new, as they confront the long-feared re-emergence of evil to Middle-earth.

movies.title: The Maltese Falcon
movies.cast: Humphrey Bogart, Mary Astor, Gladys George, Peter Lorre, Barton MacLane, Lee Patrick, Sydney Greenstreet
movies.description: Academy Award winner Humphrey Bogart stars in this classic film noir as tough San Francisco private detective Sam Spade in the classic, convoluted story of Spade's involvement with a deadly band of international thieves who will lie, double cross and murder to obtain a small, jewel-encrusted statue known as The Maltese Falcon. Sam Spade's (Bogart) partner, Miles Archer (Jerome Cowan), accepts a job protecting a young woman (Mary Astor). Neither Spade nor Archer believe the woman or the story she tells them, but they do believe her money. Then, when Archer is murdered, Spade's search for the killer drags him in the web of lies and death spun by the desperate people seeking The Maltese Falcon.
notes: Presented in 35mm
35mm print, preserved by the Library of Congress.
Preceded by the restored “Superman” short Billion Dollar Limited from Fleischer Studios.

movies.title: THE Parent Trap
movies.cast: Lindsay Lohan, Natasha Richardson, Dennis Quaid
movies.description: “ THE PARENT TRAP is based on story elements so ancient and foolproof, they must have their roots in Shakespeare’s day: the twins changing places, their divorced parents falling in love again, and, for low comedy, their servants falling in love, too. And of course there’s a wicked would-be stepmother lurking about. The story is ageless and so is the gimmick: The twins are played by the same actress, using trick photography. Hayley Mills did it in 1961, and Lindsay Lohan does it this time, seamlessly. One twin is American, one is British, but even their accents don’t help us tell them apart, since half of the time they’re pretending to be each other. ‘I’ll teach you to be me, and you teach me to be you,’ one twin says, after they meet by chance at summer camp and realize that they’ve been raised separately by divorced parents. It’s a splendid story premise, but in a way, the switch is just the setup, and the real story involves the parents. They’re played by Dennis Quaid and Natasha Richardson, who bring such humor and warmth to the movie that I was amazed to find myself actually caring about their romance. ” – Roger Ebert

movies.title: The Polar Express
movies.cast: Tom Hanks, Leslie Zemeckis, Eddie Deezen, Nona Gaye, Peter Scolari, Michael Jeter
movies.description:
Tom Hanks and director Robert Zemeckis (FORREST GUMP, CAST AWAY) reunite for THE POLAR EXPRESS, an inspiring adventure based on the beloved children's book by Chris Van Allsburg. When a doubting young boy takes an extraordinary train ride to the North Pole, he embarks on a journey of self-discovery that shows him that the wonder of life never fades for those who believe.

We believe...do you?
notes: Join us for a family adventure aboard THE POLAR EXPRESS!

movies.title: The Room Returns
movies.cast: Bob Odenkirk, Brando Crawford, Bella Heathcote, Cameron Kasky, Mike Flanagan, Kate Siegel
movies.description: What happens when great actors collide with the worst script ever written? Tommy Wiseau's original THE ROOM (2003) infamously burned through $6 million and months of shooting with no-name actors. This reimagining flips the myth on its head. Filmed in under 12 hours, on virtually no budget, with Bob Odenkirk ( Better Call Saul ), Bella Heathcote (THE NEON DEMON), executive producer Mike Flanagan ( The Haunting of Hill House ), and directed by newcomer Brando Crawford. With no rehearsal and only teleprompters to guide them, the cast embraced the chaos with Shakespearean gravity, transforming cinematic disaster into unpredictable spectacle – all for charity.

movies.title: The Shining
movies.cast: Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall, Danny Lloyd, Scatman Crothers, Barry Nelson, Philip Stone
movies.description:
An alcoholic, out-of-work teacher takes a job as the wintertime caretaker of a snowy resort. He brings his wife and young son with him. He wants to get some writing done. Things take a very dark turn...

THE SHINING is Stanley Kubrick’s chilling symphony of deft manipulation: Wendy Carlos’ score alternating with Ligeti compositions, Jack Nicholson and Shelley Duvall’s push-and-pull performances, and the omniscient Steadicam taking the whole thing in. THE SHINING transcends any trappings of paperback adaptation or genre exercise to become one of the most elementally terrifying works of art of the 20th century. Come lose yourself in its marvelous madness on the big screen, where it forever belongs.

movies.title: The Shop Around the Corner
movies.cast: Margaret Sullavan, James Stewart, Frank Morgan, Joseph Schildkraut
movies.description:
Programmer Shay Filmore tackles her watchlist anxiety through the series My First Time . This program features films Shay hasn’t seen but fall into the specific category of “movies you know you’ll probably love, but you hold off seeing because you really want to see them in the theater.”

For the second screening, prepare to get cozy in chilly Budapest for Ernst Lubitsch’s 1940 Christmastime classic The Shop Around the Corner .

Holiday genres are very funny. Every horror film is essentially part of the Halloween canon, yet comparatively few Christmas movies exist. In fact, we are always quick to enthusiastically claim that something is a Christmas movie just because it has one scene set during the holidays (like Lorene Scafaria’s 2019 masterpiece Hustlers ). This makes Shay’s oversight even more baffling since there aren’t really that many Christmas films to begin with.

In pre-war Budapest, two employees at a leather goods shop can barely stand each other, without realizing that they are falling in love through the post as each other’s anonymous pen pal.

Join Shay in your favorite holiday attire as she watches The Shop Around the Corner … for the first time!

movies.title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre
movies.cast: Marilyn Burns, Gunnar Hansen, Edwin Neal, Paul A. Partain, Allen Danziger
movies.description:
50 years ago, five youths on a weekend getaway in the Texas countryside fell prey to a butcher in a mask made of human skin and his cannibalistic family, and horror cinema would never be the same. Violent, confrontational, and shockingly realistic, director Tobe Hooper’s THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE terrified audiences in a way never thought possible when it was unleashed on a politically and socially tumultuous America in 1974. Facing a storm of controversy, censorship, and outcry throughout its troubled release, this masterpiece of horror has stood the test of time to become a landmark motion picture and cultural milestone.

Staff pick by Anthony

Screening as part of our series Staff Picks 2026

movies.title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre Part 2
movies.cast: Dennis Hopper, Caroline Williams, Jim Siedow, Bill Moseley, Bill Johnson, Bob Elmore
movies.description: Exploding with day-glo visuals and over-the-top gallows humor, THE TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE 2 is not what audiences expected from recovering wunderkind Tobe Hooper in 1986. But that’s exactly what makes it so special. Using the surreal terror of the first movie as a jumping off point, TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE 2 plays out like a deranged form of vaudeville with Leatherface as a sexually frustrated straight-man. Featuring electric performances from Bill “Chop Top” Moseley, Caroline Williams, and a chainsaw-wielding Dennis Hopper, it’s time to praise this movie for what it is—a drop-dead masterpiece of subversive 1980s horror. (American Genre Film Archive)

movies.title: The Thing
movies.cast: Kurt Russell, Wilford Brimley, Keith David, David Clennon, T.K. Carter
movies.description:
In the winter of 1982, a twelve-man research team at a remote Antarctic research station discovers an alien buried in the snow for over 100,000 years. Once unfrozen, the form-changing alien wreaks havoc, creates terror and becomes one of them.

Screening as part of Late Night Favorites: Fall 2026

Previously screened as part of our 2025 series Waverly Midnights: Winter Vacation our Autumn 2019 series, “ Waverly Midnights: Late-Night Favorites .”

movies.title: The Vile
movies.cast: Ryan Phillippe, Amélie Hoeferle, Sara Canning, Sage Linder, Beverley Elliott, Phil Burke
movies.description:
Fantastic Fest 2025 entry

Amani is living a happy family life—until one day, her husband, Khalid, shows up at the door with his new wife, Zahra. Citing Amani’s inability to bear him a son as the reason, Khalid insists he still loves her and their daughter, Noor, and that nothing will change.

But change comes quickly. Zahra grows increasingly comfortable, inserting herself into every corner of the household and getting involved in Noor’s struggles with bullying at school. Bit by bit, she wins Noor over—much to Amani’s distress. Amani begins to suspect there’s something dark and evil about Zahra.

Trying to adjust to this new reality, Amani turns to her sister for support—only to be told she’s overreacting. Gradually, she finds herself pushed to the margins, handling the household duties while Zahra enjoys a life of ease.

When Amani uncovers details about Zahra’s previous marriage, she tracks down the former wife, Huda, now living in an institution. There, she gets the confirmation she feared: Zahra is truly dangerous. Determined to protect her daughter, Amani prepares to do whatever it takes.

Majid Al Ansari is one of the rare Emirati filmmakers working in genre cinema. A Fantastic Fest alumnus, he made waves in 2015 with his debut feature, ZINZANA (RATTLE THE CAGE). Blending supernatural and horror elements, his new film THE VILE is a gripping exploration of polygamy, greed, betrayal, and trauma—told through the eyes of a mother and her daughter. Al Ansari undertook extensive research for the film, including in-depth interviews with women about their experiences and perspectives. While polygamy is a familiar concept in the UAE, Al Ansari boldly questions notions of gender inequality and consent in relationships, making THE VILE as thought-provoking as it is unsettling. (ANNICK MAHNERT)
notes: Presented in Arabic with English subtitles

movies.title: To Hold a Mountain
movies.cast: Mileva Gara Jovanović, Nada Stanišić
movies.description: The highlands of Montenegro are the breathtaking setting for this story of mother Gara and teenage daughter Nada, who tend to sheep and cows, gather herbs, and make cheese every summer. The Sinjajevina plateau is a remote, sacred, ancestral pasture, yet the modern world intrudes in the form of an incongruous government plan to install a NATO military shooting range there. Filming over seven years, co-directors Tutorov and Glomazić vividly capture the indefatigable efforts of Gara to cultivate support from her neighbors to guard the land that benefits them all, as Nada learns hard truths about her family’s history.

movies.title: Tokyo Godfathers
movies.cast: Aya Okamoto, Yoshiaki Umegaki, Tohru Emori, Satomi Korogi, Mamiko Noto, Ryuji Saikachi
movies.description:
Presented in an English dub

In modern-day Tokyo, three homeless people’s lives are changed forever when they discover a baby girl at a garbage dump on Christmas Eve. As the New Year fast approaches, these three forgotten members of society band together to solve the mystery of the abandoned child and the fate of her parents. Along the way, encounters with seemingly unrelated events and people force them to confront their own haunted pasts, as they learn to face their future, together.

Co-written by Keiko Nobumoto ( Cowboy Bebop ) and featuring a whimsical score by Keiichi Suzuki, TOKYO GODFATHERS is a masterpiece by turns heartfelt, hilarious, and highly original, a tale of hope and redemption in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds. (GKIDS)
notes: Presented in Japanese with English subtitles

movies.title: Trouble in Paradise
movies.cast: Herbert Marshall, Kay Francis, Miriam Hopkins
movies.description: “You are a crook. I want you as a crook. I love you as a crook. I worship you as a crook.” Partners in crime and romance, Herbert Marshall (Gaston) and Miriam Hopkins (Lily) hatch a plan to rob perfume executive Kay Francis (Mariette), sending Gaston in as personal secretary to their employer. The plan is afoot and the joint is cased... until Gaston falls in love with Mariette and is forced to choose in a film that pairs grace and elegance with swindling and social vulgarities.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk With Me
movies.cast: Sheryl Lee, Ray Wise, Madchen Amick, Dana Ashbrook, David Bowie, Phoebe Augustine, Moira Kelly, Peggy Lipton
movies.description:
In the town of Twin Peaks, everyone has their secrets—but especially Laura Palmer (Sheryl Lee). In this prequel to his groundbreaking 1990s television series, David Lynch resurrects the teenager found wrapped in plastic at the beginning of the show, following her through the last week of her life and teasing out the enigmas that surround her murder. Homecoming queen by day and drug-addicted thrill seeker by night, Laura leads a double life that pulls her deeper and deeper into horror as she pieces together the identity of the assailant who has been terrorizing her for years. Nightmarish in its vision of an innocent torn apart by unfathomable forces, TWIN PEAKS: FIRE WALK WITH ME is nevertheless one of Lynch’s most humane films, aching with compassion for its tortured heroine—a character as enthralling in life as she was in death. – Janus Films

Screening as part of Late Night Favorites: Fall 2026 Previously screened as part of our 2025 series Wonderful and Strange: The Complete Twin Peaks and Remembering David Lynch , our Winter 2019 season of Waverly Midnights: The Feds , The Films of David Lynch , and Late Night Favorites: Fall 2024

movies.title: Violent Night 2
movies.cast: David Harbour, Kristen Bell, Daniela Melchior, Jared Harris, Joe Pantoliano, Maxwell Jacob Friedman
movies.description: David Harbour reprises his role as Santa Claus in a propulsive new chapter in yuletide mayhem from 87North, as not-so-jolly Saint Nick suits up again to take on a ruthless gangster terrorizing the merchants of the Silver Bell Mall.

movies.title: Werwulf
movies.cast: Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe, Lily-Rose Depp
movies.description: Witness Robert Eggers’ most visceral and haunting experience yet. Focus Features presents Werwulf , a harrowing tale of devotion, damnation and the devil within.

movies.title: Werwulf
movies.cast: Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe, Lily-Rose Depp
movies.description: Experience Robert Eggers’ ( Nosferatu ) latest visceral and haunting vision. In a small rural village, local superstition becomes terrifyingly real when a ravenous creature begins to stalk the countryside. While a local farmer (Taylor-Johnson) struggles beneath the weight of a werewolf curse, a ruthless hunter (Dafoe) begins a campaign to eradicate wolves. A harrowing tale of devotion, damnation and the devil within.

movies.title: Werwulf
movies.cast: Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe, Lily-Rose Depp
movies.description: Witness Robert Eggers’ most visceral and haunting experience yet. Focus Features presents WERWULF, a harrowing tale of devotion, damnation and the devil within.

movies.title: When Harry Met Sally...
movies.cast: Billy Crystal, Meg Ryan, Carrie Fisher, Bruno Kirby, Steven Ford, Lisa Jane Persky
movies.description:
We all know those couples. They see each other from across the room, they meet, and wham! They’re desperately in love.

That’s not the case for Harry and Sally. In fact, when they meet, they don’t particularly like each other. Sally is earnest and good. Harry is cynical and depressive. It’s not a match made in heaven.

But lovers of rom-coms know that opposites have a way of attracting.

With some of the most palpable on-screen chemistry in movie history, Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan take viewers on a journey through friendship, heartbreak, and the pitfalls of relationships with the help of expert direction from Rob Reiner, a pitch-perfect supporting cast (including Carrie Fisher and Bruno Kirby), and one of the best romantic comedy screenplays of all time from the brilliant Nora Ephron.

movies.title: Which Way is Up?
movies.cast: Richard Pryor, Lonette McKee, Margaret Avery
movies.description: Orange picker Leroy Jones (Richard Pryor) inadvertently becomes a union leader and is forced out of town, leaving behind his sexually obsessed father, Rufus (also Pryor), and spouse, Annie Mae (Margaret Avery). He heads for Los Angeles, where he falls for union organizer Vanetta (Lonette McKee). Annie Mae seeks solace from the local preacher, Lenox Thomas (also Pryor), who eventually impregnates her. When Leroy catches wind of this, he heads home for a showdown with Lenox.
notes: Presented in 35mm
35mm print!
Preceded by the Looney Tunes animated short Mouse Wreckers .

movies.title: Wto/99
movies.cast: Joan Claybrook, Bill Clinton
movies.description:
Building from a roughly 1,000 hour archive, WTO/99 reanimates the ideological conflicts that drew thousands to the streets of Seattle in hopes for a better future. The film is an immersive visual artifact of a week that brought 40,000 people together to warn of environmental collapse, the vanishing middle class, and what the full inclusion of China in the World Trade Organization would mean for our collective future. The protesters—seen as a rabble-rousing nuisance at the time, yet appearing prophetic today—were met with extreme violence by a militarized police force, an all-too-fitting way to usher in a new century; one that is now defined by US failure to address climate change and increasing state aggression.

This immersive archival documentary depicts the four-day clash between the then-emerging World Trade Organization (WTO) and the 40,000+ people who took to the streets of Seattle in 1999 to protest the WTO Conference and sound the alarm on the WTO’s impact on human rights, labor, and the future effects of continued globalization.

movies.title: Zodiac
movies.cast: Jake Gyllenhaal, Mark Ruffalo, Anthony Edwards, Robert Downey Jr., Chloë Sevigny, Elias Koteas
movies.description:
Based on the true story of one of America's greatest unsolved mysteries of one of its most notorious serial killers, ZODIAC is as much a story of obsession as it is a story of murder. In the ‘60s and ‘70s, the Zodiac was a serial killer in the San Francisco area who would routinely taunt the police with letters and ciphers in newspapers. One day, a young political cartoonist, Robert Graysmith (Jake Gyllenhaal), cracks one of the Zodiac’s ciphers and spirals into a sea of perpetual preoccupation with solving his riddles and finding out his true identity with the help of his co-worker/crime reporter friend Paul Avery (Robert Downey Jr.).

Always intrigued by the case while growing up in the Bay Area, the Zodiac was David Fincher’s “ultimate boogeyman.” Fincher set out with his screenwriter and producer to conduct an 18-month investigation into the unsolved case while rewriting the screenplay. The result is the story of a reporter determined to get the story at any cost. New to being an investigative reporter, he becomes all-consumed by his obsession to know the truth. Somehow along the way, it seems as though Fincher and company got caught up in that compulsion and created a spectacularly layered, investigative, and riveting narrative in their attempt to find a culprit posthumously.

This film was a technical marvel and a true cinematic masterpiece of Fincher’s career that, despite overwhelming positive reviews and an all-star cast, was left basically ignored by audiences. Don’t make the same mistake twice and miss your chance to get swept up in this gut-wrenching sea of anxiety!

movies.title: 2026 Oscar Nominated Animated Shorts
movies.description: These meticulously animated works of art follow a wide range of fascinating characters, from an Olympic swimmer who survived the Holocaust to an intrepid kid bravely attempting to rescue her village. Please note that some films contain disturbing material and may not be suitable for very young children. Butterfly Dir. Florence Miailhe France, 15min A poignant retelling of Olympic swimmer Alfred Nakache’s life, from his rise to fame to surviving Auschwitz, presented as memories flashing back during his final swim. Forevergreen Dirs. Nathan Engelhardt & Jeremy Spears US, 13min A joyful adventure featuring an orphaned bear cub and a fatherly tree turns serious when the cub is tempted by the allure of easy food. Fire and deadly danger ensue as the cub is left bereft of hope and on the verge of a ruinous end, until the sacrificial love of the tree falls into place. The Girl Who Cried Pearls Dirs. Chris Lavis & Maciek Szczerbowski Canada, 17min A haunting fable about a girl overwhelmed by sorrow, the boy who loves her, and how greed leads good hearts to wicked deeds. Retirement Plan Dir. John Kelly Ireland, 7min Ray (voiced by Domhall Gleeson) fantasizes about everything he’d love to do in retirement, once he finally has the “time.” The Three Sisters Dir. Konstantin Bronzit Israel & Cyprus, 14min Three sisters live a lonely life on an isolated island, each in their own small house. One day, circumstances change, and they are forced to rent out one of the houses. Also screening in this program: Éiru Dir. Giovanna Ferrari Ireland, 13min When the water mysteriously disappears from the well in a warrior clan’s village, an intrepid child descends into the belly of the earth to retrieve it. Éiru is the story of a kid in search of a challenge and a goddess in search of a champion.

movies.title: 2026 Oscar Nominated Live-Action Shorts
movies.description: These Oscar-contending films from Israel, the UK, the US, and France explore the messy, beautiful, and often forbidden ways we seek connection. Butcher’s Stain Dir. Meyer Levinson-Blount Israel, 26min Samir, a Palestinian butcher working at an Israeli supermarket, is accused of tearing down the Israeli hostage posters in the break room. Samir sets out to prove his innocence in order to keep the job he so desperately needs. A Friend of Dorothy Dir. Lee Knight UK, 21min Dorothy is a lonely widow whose body is failing but whose mind remains sharp as ever. When 17-year-old JJ accidentally kicks his football into her garden, an unlikely friendship blossoms. Jane Austen’s Period Drama Dirs. Steve Pinder & Julia Aks US, 12min In 1813 England, Essy Talbot’s long-awaited marriage proposal takes a messy turn when her period arrives at a very bad time. The Singers Dir. Sam A. Davis US, 18min The Singers is a film adaptation of a 19th-century short story written by Ivan Turgenev, in which downtrodden patrons in a lowly pub connect unexpectedly through an impromptu sing-off. Two People Exchanging Saliva Dirs. Natalie Musteata & Alexandre Singh France, 36min In a society where kissing is punishable by death and people pay for things by receiving slaps to the face, an unhappy woman shops compulsively in a department store and becomes entranced by one of the employees.

movies.title: 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple
movies.cast: Ralph Fiennes, Alfie Williams, Jack O'Connell, Erin Kellyman, Chi Lewis-Parry, Connor Newall
movies.description: The nature of the infected is changing… Director Nia DaCosta expands the grisly, post-apocalyptic world first forged by Danny Boyle and Alex Garland with 2002’s 28 Days Later and built upon in 2025’s 28 Years Later . In this third entry, Dr. Kelson (Fiennes) forms a relationship whose consequences could alter the fate of humanity, while Spike’s (Williams) encounter with Jimmy Crystal (O’Connell) spirals into a nightmare he can’t escape. In the world of The Bone Temple, the infected are no longer the greatest threat to survival—the inhumanity of the survivors proves far more terrifying.

movies.title: 7 Women
movies.cast: Anne Bancroft, Sue Lyon, Margaret Leighton, Flora Robson, Mildred Dunnock, Betty Field
movies.description: For his final film, the preeminent poet of the American West on screen lit out for the East, or at least a soundstage version of it—and eschewed his usual masculine ensembles for a decidedly more feminine group. Ford’s swansong takes place among a group of female Christian missionaries—Anne Bancroft, Sue Lyon, and Margaret Leighton among their number—in a c. 1935 rural China ravaged by cholera and ransacked by Mongolian warlord Tunga Khan (hulking wrestler Mike Mazurki), whose horde, including Ford regular Woody Strode, pose a clear and present danger to the ladies’ redoubt. “Ford brings a mix of rigor and playfulness, of something hieratic and something erratic, because he allows a bit of playfulness into the game and puts himself into it… The truth, in Ford’s films, is not at the end of the trail, but always before there has even been a road.” —Serge Daney

movies.title: A Clockwork Orange
movies.cast: Malcolm McDowell, Patrick Magee, Carl Duering, Michael Bates, Warren Clarke, James Marcus
movies.description: Wendy Carlos’s score of switched-on Moog synthesizer classical, Kubrick’s punchy framings, and Malcolm McDowell’s cruelly charismatic, Nadsat slang-spouting performance as teen reprobate Alex combine to make for cracking cinema, and a hallucinatory imagination of a future broken Britain. Based on the stinging satire by Anthony Burgess, a work by turns exhilarating and nauseating, the film of A Clockwork Orange would be withdrawn from British cinemas at Kubrick’s behest, citing concern over reports that it had inspired copycat crimes in the UK.

movies.title: A Knight's Tale
movies.cast: Heath Ledger, Mark Addy, Rufus Sewell, Shannyn Sossamon, Paul Bettany, Laura Fraser
movies.description:
Layering medieval anachronism over the familiar beats of a sports narrative, only with jousting replacing football or baseball, A Knight’s Tale succeeds as both an underdog story and a postmodern pastiche. ... And can we just say that the choice of David Bowie’s “Golden Years” for the unforgettable dance scene is argument enough for the queerness of this movie.

– Natalie Zutter, Den of Geek
notes: Preceded by a live performance by medieval music ensemble ALKEMIE and an introduction by critic and writer Natalie Zutter .

movies.title: A Separation
movies.cast: Payman Maadi, Leila Hatami, Shahab Hosseini, Sareh Bayat, Sarina Farhadi, Ali-Asghar Shahbazi
movies.description: Farhadi combines elements of the domestic drama and psychological thriller in his trenchant, lacerating 2012 Academy Award winner for Best Foreign Film. Simin (Leila Hatami) wants to emigrate with her 11-year-old daughter and with or without her husband, Nader (Payman Maadi), who, with the support of the court, has dug in his heels to keep the family in place while he looks after his ailing father, aided by a caregiver with costly secrets. Through the intersecting stories of two deadlocked couples—one middle-class, the other working-class—and their necessary deceptions, Farhadi shows us a microcosm of contemporary Iranian society and the insoluble moral dilemmas it presents to ordinary men and women.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Afternoons of Solitude
movies.cast: Andrés Roca Rey, Roberto Domínguez, Francisco Manuel "Viruta" Durán, Antonio Chacón, Paco Gómez, Manuel "Larita" Lara
movies.description: Serra’s visceral yet elegant documentary portrait of young, Peruvian-born superstar torero Andrés Roca Rey sees him risking life and limb on the clock, and in unglamorous off-hours traveling via minibus between arenas with an extensive, officious entourage. A privileged, patiently observed perspective on the flamboyant showmanship, ritualized grace, and terrible violence of bullfighting, that most controversial of the sporting arts, its time-honored spectacle of man’s cultivated, calculated intelligence facing down an elemental force of primal animal aggression, a spectacle that ends, invariably, in a welter of hot, bubbling blood. “Impressionistic and intimate… Perhaps the most immersive encapsulation of tauromachy yet achieved in cinema.” —Sight & Sound

movies.title: All of a Sudden
movies.cast: Virginie Efira, Tao Okamoto, Kyōzō Nagatsuka, Kodai Kurosaki, Jean-Charles Clichet, Marie Bunel
movies.description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

movies.title: Alpha
movies.cast: Mélissa Boros, Tahar Rahim, Golshifteh Farahani, Emma Mackey, Finnegan Oldfield, Louai El Amrousy
movies.description: Life swiftly starts to unravel for Alpha and her single mom after the rebellious 13-year-old comes home with a stick-and-poke tattoo made with a used needle at a house party—a mark that may be related to a contagious blood-borne disease that turns its victims into disintegrating stone. The third feature by French director and screenwriter Julia Ducournau, winner of the Palme d’Or at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival for Titane , is a mysterious, unsettling allegory for the 1980s AIDS crisis and the waves of hysteria, prejudice, and exclusion it produced.

movies.title: Andrew Norman Wilson: Sound Works
movies.description:
Andrew Norman Wilson presents a selection of his disparate short works united by their shared attention to the aural, each beginning with or inspired by a sound, a song, or the spoken word. In a format inspired by VH1 Storytellers (1996-2015), the screening will be punctuated by Wilson discussing the manner in which sound shapes the creation and perception of his work. The evening’s bill of fare includes video art, music videos, narrative shorts, and the New York premiere of Silvesterchlausen (2025), exploring a little-known New Year’s Eve tradition whose origins remain wreathed in mystery, still practiced today in Switzerland’s most conservative region, the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden.

Filmmaker Andrew Norman Wilson in person for a special presentation on Saturday, December 12th

movies.title: Arco
movies.cast: Margot Ringard Oldra, Oscar Tresanini, Nathanaël Perrot, Alma Jodorowsky, Swann Arlaud, Vincent Macaigne
movies.description: In the year 2075, a 10-year-old girl witnesses a mysterious boy in a rainbow suit fall from the sky. Arco comes from an idyllic far future where time travel is possible. Iris shelters him, and will do whatever it takes to help him return to his time. In return, Arco gives Iris hope for an optimistic future. Directed by author and comic-book illustrator Ugo Bienvenu, this vivacious animated feature debuted at Cannes and won recognition from the New York Film Critics Online and Lumière Awards alongside dozens of prestigious nominations. Academy Award nominee, Best Animated Feature

movies.title: Art Cinema for Tots: Tales from the Forest
movies.description:
Born out of a commitment to the idea that it’s never too early to introduce kids to the pleasures of movies made outside of the commercial mainstream—and the suspicion that young audiences are often more open-minded and curious than their elders when it comes to such matters—Metrograph presents the latest iteration of Art Cinema for Tots, a celebration of handcrafted, kid-friendly films that reconcile the smart and the silly. In this edition, join us for Tales from the Forest, a quartet of films by venerable Russian animator Yuri Norstein, whose meticulous, slow-moving perfectionism—each minute of finished film is the result of untold hours of labor—long ago earned him the nickname “the Golden Snail.”

Director of Programming (and mom) Inge de Leeuw describes the experience: “The sound levels will be dimmed, and there will be a gentle light on, creating a relaxed atmosphere where young viewers feel at ease. They won’t be confined to their seats; they can move around, explore, and enjoy the wonder of the big screen. It will be a playful, interactive cinematic journey, designed with little explorers in mind.

Fox and the Hare (Yuri Norstein, 1973, 12 mins)

Heron and the Crane (Yuri Norstein, 1974, 10 mins)

Seasons (Yuri Norstein, 1969, 9 mins)

Hedgehog and the Fog (Yuri Norstein, 1975, 11 mins)

Each ticket includes free admission for one child, if you’d like to bring more than one child per ticket, please email [email protected] to book a seat.

movies.title: Asako I & II
movies.cast: Masahiro Higashide, Erika Karata, Koji Seto, Rio Yamashita, Sairi Ito, Daichi Watanabe
movies.description: Following up Happy Hour, his justly acclaimed epic of everyday life, Hamaguchi offers a different but no less quietly revolutionary vision with this pop romance that moves from youthful exuberance and delusion to mature circumspection and compromise, while keeping up throughout a magical tonal balance of wistfulness, comic buoyancy, and the ineffably heartbreaking. As a student in Osaka, Asako meets and falls in love with a drifter named Baku who one day drifts right out of her life. Two years later, working in Tokyo, she sees Baku again—or, rather, a young, solid businessman named Ryohei who is Baku’s double in every respect save personality. After initial astonishment, they begin to build a life together—but a twist in circumstances threatens to tear it all down, and forces Asako to confront her long, lingering love affair with a half-ghost fantasy.
notes: Introduction by filmmaker Kogonada on Saturday, November 7th

movies.title: Autumn Sonata
movies.cast: Ingrid Bergman, Liv Ullmann, Lena Nyman, Halvar Björk, Marianne Aminoff, Arne Bang-Hansen
movies.description: Ingmar and Ingrid, Bergman and Bergman, together at last. Sweden’s most popular export before the Volvo, in her final screen role, plays a world-renowned concert pianist who returns home to reunite with her now-married daughter (Liv Ullmann), long a distant second to her mother’s career ambitions, the two women exhuming old resentments and struggling towards reconciliation over the course of an emotionally draining 24 hours. “So unrelenting, so harrowing, that I walked out of the theater on shaking legs. If you’re open to the experience that Bergman means to provide, you may leave the film muttering a wrung-out ‘Whew!’ followed quickly by an appreciative ‘Wow!’” —Richard Corliss, Time Magazine

movies.title: Backrooms
movies.cast: Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, Finn Bennett, Lukita Maxwell, Mark Duplass, Avan Jogia
movies.description: Drawing on the deep dread of so-called “liminal” spaces—the non-places of depopulated office buildings and parking lots of late capitalist America—this feature debut from 20-year-old Kane Parsons was inspired by a sprawling fictional location first chronicled in a 2019 4chan thread. A simple premise straight out of the internet age snowballs into psychological terror as store-owner Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor) and his therapist (Renate Reinsve) venture into an unknown dimension through a strange doorway that has appeared in the basement of a furniture showroom.

movies.title: Benedetta
movies.cast: Virginie Efira, Charlotte Rampling, Daphné Patakia, Lambert Wilson, Olivier Rabourdin, Louise Chevillotte
movies.description: Inspired by the life of Benedetta Carlini, a nun of 17th-century Tuscany whose claims of mystic visions drew the attention of church higher-ups, their investigations eventually revealing a verboten sexual relationship between Carlini and one of her fellow nuns and leading to her imprisonment, Verhoeven’s earthy, irreverent film immerses one in the squelchy squalor and earthly delights of Counter-Reformation era Europe, with Virginie Efira a revelation in the title role and Charlotte Rampling, as the abbess of the convent, conveying roiling inner turmoil beneath a cooly composed exterior. An examination of the difficult relationship between religious submission and sexual liberation, featuring some of the most memorable foley sounds in recent cinema.

movies.title: Best Pancakes in the County
movies.cast: Nicolas Cage, Justin Long, Shelley Hennig
movies.description: Set over the course of one explosive night, BEST PANCAKES IN THE COUNTY transforms an unassuming small-town diner into the epicenter of a deadly standoff involving rogue federal agents, a fast-talking con man with a dangerous past and a waitress harboring secrets of her own. As loyalties blur and tensions erupt, survival depends on who can outthink — and outgun — everyone else.

movies.title: Bitter Christmas
movies.cast: Barbara Lennie, Leonardo Sbaraglia, Aitana Sanchez-Gijon
movies.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

movies.title: Blood Rage
movies.cast: Louise Lasser, Mark Soper, Julie Gordon
movies.description:
Thanksgiving isn’t Thanksgiving without a viewing of Blood Rage . Todd and Terry are twin bros with twin problems—namely, one of them is an axe-wielding maniac. After a literal drive-in massacre, Todd is blamed for the carnage and institutionalized, while Terry goes free. Ten years later, Todd escapes from an asylum on Thanksgiving and the blood rage begins. Produced by whip-smart filmmaker Maryanne Kantor, directed by John Grissmer ( Scalpel ), and shot in Florida, this essential 1980s party slasher is what happens when you combine Thanksgiving, 1970s TV star Louise Lasser, a killer synth score, and the most unbelievable gore effects in all of slasherdom, courtesy Ed French ( Terminator 2 ).

Remember: “It’s not cranberry sauce.”

movies.title: Blue + Chinese Series
movies.cast: Len Cariou, Joe Carter
movies.description: Over the same, unceasing monochromatic sea of blue, Yves Klein’s patented “International Klein Blue,” the voices of Jarman and collaborating actors (including Tilda Swinton and Nigel Terry) read a poetic text by the director in which he muses on the physical and mental deterioration wrought by the ravages of AIDS, as well as the endless implications of the color blue. Jarman would be gone within a year, but he left behind one of the great final films, a vibrant work of courage and clarity in the face of oblivion. Screens with Brakhage’s Chinese Series, a long-contemplated short work inspired by Chinese ideograms completed in the filmmaker’s dying days.

movies.title: Blue Heron
movies.cast: Eylul Guven, Iringó Réti, Ádám Tompa, Edik Beddoes, Amy Zimmer, Liam Serg
movies.description: In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her Hungarian immigrant family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island, but their fresh start is interrupted by increasingly dangerous behavior from the eldest son, Jeremy. At wit’s end, their parents are presented with a shattering choice. Award-winning director Sophy Romvari’s semi-autobiographical debut feature is a lyrical, profound testament to the things we carry with us, masterfully chronicling the haze of a languid summer and the clarity of the moments that defined it. Q&A with director Sophy Romvari following the 4/21, 7pm screening

movies.title: Broadcast News
movies.cast: William Hurt, Albert Brooks, Holly Hunter
movies.description: A highly strung news producer finds herself strangely attracted to a vapid anchorman even through she loathes everything he personifies. To make matters worse, her best friend, a talented but not particularly telegenic news reporter, is secretly in love with her.

movies.title: Chinese Roulette
movies.cast: Anna Karina, Margit Carstensen, Brigitte Mira, Ulli Lommel, Alexander Allerson, Volker Spengler
movies.description: Fassbinder gives us the weekend getaway from hell in this suffocating chamber drama, in which unhappily and unfaithfully married couple Gerhard and Ariane Christ (Alexander Allerson and Margit Carstensen), intending to escape one another and their bitter disabled daughter, Angela (Andrea Schober), wind up in a family reunion, with lovers Anna Karina and Ulli Lommel in tow, at their country manse, where a vengeful Angela maneuvers the assembled parties into a round of the eponymous guessing game, designed to sow dissension and inflict maximum psychological torment. “More original and daring than anything I’ve yet to see by filmmakers who call themselves avant-garde… A mysterious comedy of deliberate elegance… Camp lyricism of such density it becomes a lethal weapon.” —The New York Times
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Chronicle of Anna Magdalena Bach
movies.cast: Gustav Leonhardt, Christiane Lang, Paolo Carlini, Ernst Castelli, Hans-Peter Boye, Joachim Wolff
movies.description: Renowned harpsichordist Gustave Leonhardt plays—and plays as—Johann Sebastian Bach in Straub and Huillet’s remarkable film on the composer, based in part on a fictional journal by his second wife, and built around live-sound recordings of Leonhardt…

movies.title: Chronovisor
movies.cast: Anne Laure Sellier, Nicholas Tebben, Nicole Dombrowski Risser, Alex Kolodkin, José Pacheco de Almeida, Sophie Queuniet
movies.description: Béatrice (Anne Laure Sellier), a Columbia professor deep into research for a monograph on theories of memory throughout the ages, stumbles across the purportedly true story of the “Chronovisor,” a device said to be able to reproduce images from any point in history onto a television screen, and in short order her curiosity becomes an all-consuming monomania. (The genesis of Walker and Auen’s story is a claim by one Father Pellegrino Ernetti to have collaborated on the creation of just such an invention.) An ingenious archival conspiracy thriller that might have tickled Umberto Eco and Jorge Luis Borges, unfolding amidst the shadowy stacks of New York City’s libraries. “Wonderfully unclassifiable. A tantalizing armchair mystery steeped in occult-ish authenticity [and] a sly commentary on our own relationship to the pursuit of curiosity.”—Los Angeles Times
notes: Q&A with filmmakers Jack Auen and Kevin Walker on Friday, December 11th

movies.title: Chronovisor
movies.cast: Anne Laure Sellier, Nicholas Tebben, Nicole Dombrowski Risser, Alex Kolodkin, José Pacheco de Almeida, Sophie Queuniet
movies.description: While writing a monograph on historical theories of memory, Béatrice, a respected academic, becomes beguiled by the allegedly true story of the Chronovisor, an occult device said to reproduce visuals from any point in history on a TV screen. Her obsession with the mysterious machine drags her from her Upper East Side apartment through the depths of New York City’s hidden libraries, to the edge of a breakthrough.

movies.title: Clayface
movies.cast: Tom Rhys Harries, Naomi Ackie, Eddie Marsan, Max Minghella, David Dencik, Francesca Corney
movies.description: What happens when a super-villain origin story gets a serious horror-movie makeover? CLAYFACE, that’s what. Director James Watkins (THE WOMAN IN BLACK) brings a nasty dose of body horror to Gotham, with DOCTOR SLEEP and Midnight Mass mastermind Mike Flanagan on co-writing duties. Tom Rhys Harries stars as Matt Hagen, a disfigured actor who undergoes a miraculous transformation that sends his grip on reality, and his appetite for revenge, somewhere very dark. Get ready to face your fears on the big screen.

movies.title: Columbus
movies.cast: John Cho, Haley Lu Richardson, Michelle Forbes, Rory Culkin, Parker Posey, Erin Allegretti
movies.description: Modern architecture acts as a vehicle for emotional expression in Kogonada’s lauded first feature, whose title refers to the Indiana city that, thanks to the patronage of Cummins diesel engines company cofounder J. Irwin Miller, has commissioned buildings from master builders including I.M. Pei, Eero Saarinen, and Robert Venturi. A Korean American translator (John Cho) arrives in this curious testing ground for advanced architecture after his estranged scholar father falls ill, there to cross paths with dad’s protégée (Parker Posey), an aesthete clerk at the local library (Haley Lu Richardson), and a bevy of singular structures. A film of rich colors and muted yearning, and one of the most distinctive debuts in the last decade of American independent cinema.
notes: Q&A with filmmaker Kogonada and actor Haley Lu Richardson moderated by filmmaker Christopher Radcliff on Sunday, November 8th

movies.title: Come Back to the 5 & Dime, Jimmy Dean, Jimmy Dean
movies.cast: Cher, Sandy Dennis, Karen Black, Sudie Bond, Kathy Bates, Marta Heflin
movies.description: One day in 1975, at a dusty Woolworth’s in small town McCarthy, Texas, the six members of the “Disciples of James Dean” reconvene 20 years after they first formed the club in the wake of the heartthrob actor’s death. Shifting between “present day” scenes and flashbacks to 1955 through an ingenious two-way mirror device, Altman’s film of Ed Graczyk’s play, which Altman had originally directed on the stage, is a touching meditation on dreams deferred and long-enduring female friendships, its peerless ensemble cast including Cher, Sandy Dennis, and Karen Black. Theatrical premiere of a new 4K restoration.
notes: Introduction by Vinegar Syndrome producer Justin LaLiberty on Friday, November 20th
4K restoration courtesy of Cinématographe and Vinegar Syndrome.

movies.title: Compartment No. 6
movies.cast: Seidi Haarla, Yura Borisov, Dinara Drukarova, Yuliya Aug, Lidiya Kostina, Tomi Alatalo
movies.description:
When her girlfriend bails on a planned trip to visit ancient petroglyphs in the remote city of Murmansk in the Arctic Circle, Finnish student Laura (Seidi Haarla) decides to go on alone, finding herself sharing a compartment on the long train from Moscow with Lyokha (Yura Borisov), a Russian returning to his work in the mines of the northeast who makes a belligerent and boorish first impression, but in time becomes a figure of fascination for Laura—and she for him.

“There are not enough films about uncategorizable love. Here is a marvelous corrective to that neglected genre.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue"

movies.title: Countercurrents
movies.description: Traumatized by his recent divorce, lovelorn Stanley takes off cross country to San Francisco, landing at his enterprising sister Nancy's doorstep. Nancy, who makes counterculture cinema-themed t-shirts, lives in "Camille's Castle," a frozen-in-time legacy home for displaced artists and outcasts. Together, they search for the remaining scraps of San Francisco's Summer of Love, and wind up at odds with each other. Countercurrents is an aggressive tribute to the counterculture films of the late 60's, with "easter eggs" in no short supply.

movies.title: Coyote vs Acme
movies.cast: Will Forte, Lana Condor, John Cena, Tone Bell, Martha Kelly, Luis Guzmán
movies.description: After countless ACME Corporation products backfire on Wile E. Coyote in his never-ending quest to vanquish the Road Runner, the despondent canine hires lawyer Kevin Avery (Forte) to sue the nefarious company. When the down-and-out attorney and Coyote realize they’ll be squaring off against the former’s ex-boss (Cena) in the case, it lights a fire under the duo—launching an unlikely friendship. The equally endearing and gut-busting adventure finally arrives in theaters after being shelved in 2023, giving Looney Tunes fans an opportunity to experience the whimsy of some of cinema’s most iconic cartoon stars back on the silver screen.

movies.title: Crocodile Dose
movies.cast: Chase Mackay, Graham Cox, Jason Waters, Avery Boggs, Owen Broghammer, Charlotte Hearn
movies.description:
On their first summer back from college, best friends Curtis (Chase Mackay), Jimmy (Graham Cox), and Abe (Jason Waters) embark on a fantastical 24-hour odyssey of drugs and alcohol on their way to a house party hosted by Curtis’s ex-girlfriend, Jane (Avery Boggs). When their pursuit of hedonism leads to Jane and Curtis reuniting prematurely, Curtis is unable to handle his emotions and loses touch with his relationships and reality.

CROCODILE DOSE is a teen comedy told through cell phones, digital photography, and the internet. Set in a magical Denver, the film explores falling in love and growing up in a technologically interconnected world.

movies.title: Cría Cuervos
movies.cast: Ana Torrent, Conchita Pérez, Mayte Sánchez, Geraldine Chaplin, Mónica Randall, Florinda Chico
movies.description: Taking its title from the Spanish proverb “Raise ravens and they will pick your eyes out,” Saura’s lauded allegorical masterwork, set during the twilight of Spain’s Franco dictatorship, stars Ana Torrent (also seen in Spirit of the Beehive, in the same series) as a traumatized eight-year-old, second of three sisters living with a domineering aunt in Madrid following the death of their parents, who feels herself to be drifting freely between the worlds of the living and the dead and is increasingly convinced she has the ability to snuff out her adult persecutors’ lives. “Both an uncanny drama of family dysfunction and a historical parable of the end of Franco-ism… [Geraldine] Chaplin and Torrent are both outstanding.” —The Guardian
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Cult Cinema
movies.description: Film Noir Cinema presents “CULT CINEMA”: a night of sheer cinematic madness dedicated to the most obscure films ever made.

movies.title: Cyclops
movies.cast: Kai Atô, Mayumi Hasegawa, Yoshimasa Kondô, Kazuhiro Sano, Nobuo Takahashi
movies.description:
New 2K transfer from original 16mm elements

“Evolution is about to get sloppy”

A secret group of scientists believes grotesque human mutations may represent the next stage of evolution – and they are willing to use living women to prove it. When their latest experiment ends in disaster, the researchers hunt the streets for a new subject, accompanied by a mysterious one-eyed mutant hiding behind dark glasses. Their obsession soon erupts into a delirious showdown of rupturing flesh, mutant bodies and spectacular practical gore in director Jôji Iida’s (Night Head, Ring, Spiral) notorious Japanese body-horror nightmare.

Shot on 16mm, Cyclops emerged from the same underground Japanese splatter culture as Guzoo, Biotherapy and Guinea Pig , mixing fears of pollution and mutation with gloriously tactile effects. Shuichi Kokumai and Yûichi Matsui turn the climax into an outrageous eruption of wounds, torn flesh and gelatinous transformation. A true cult artifact of late-’80s Japanese body horror – packed with Cronenbergian mutation, splatter-punk excess and DIY ingenuity in one goopy package.

movies.title: Daughters of the Dust
movies.cast: Cora Lee Day, Alva Rogers, Barbara O. Jones, Trula Hoosier, Umar Abdurrahamn, Adisa Anderson
movies.description: “This landmark film by pioneering director Julie Dash forever changed my thinking about the Great Migration, not to mention Gullah culture. Her key participation in Anthology—foregrounding the contributions of the remarkable Ann Lowe and Eartha Kitt—reveals Dash’s distinctive voice and ongoing commitment to centering the lives of Black women.”—Sylvia Yount, Lawrence A. Fleischman Curator in Charge of the American Wing, The Metropolitan Museum of Art Presented in DCP 4K

movies.title: Day Night Day Night
movies.cast: Luisa Williams, Josh Philip Weinstein, Gareth Saxe, Nyambi Nyambi, Frank Dattolo, Annemarie Lawless
movies.description: Before her epic My Undesirable Friends made Loktev one of the most-discussed figures in contemporary nonfiction, there was Day Night Day Night, the director’s riveting fiction feature debut, closely following 48 hours in the life of an unnamed young woman, played by an entrancing Luisa Colón, as she makes preparations to detonate herself in a Times Square suicide bombing in service to an unknown cause. Shot with remarkable immediacy and adroitness by cinematographer Benoît Debie, best known for his collaborations with Gaspar Noé, and lent a sense of subtly rising tension that reaches a point of near-suffocation by editor Michael Taylor, Loktev’s austere film—and its brooding, taciturn leading lady—exert a sinister undertow pull of fascination.
notes: Q&A with director/editor Julia Loktev, editor Michael Taylor, ACE, and actor Luisa Colón moderated by Joseph Krings, ACE, on Saturday, December 5th

movies.title: Death to Smoochy
movies.cast: Robin Williams, Edward Norton, Catherine Keener, Danny DeVito, Jon Stewart, Pam Ferris
movies.description:
Idealistic Sheldon Mopes (Edward Norton) has always wanted to bring his character, Smoochy the Rhino, to children’s television, and when the top star at the Kid’s Net channel, “Rainbow” Randolph (Robin Williams), is arrested in a bribery scandal, he sees his chance… But as it transpires, hell hath no fury like a “Rainbow” Randolph scorned, and Sheldon’s sunny disposition will be sorely tested by his predecessor’s sabotage and the sleazy reality of the children’s entertainment biz. An acrid dark comedy, with DP Anastos Michos lending the whole affair an air of blighted cheeriness.

“I picked Death to Smoochy because it is about innocence for sale. In 2002, the press and the audience found its cynicism over the top. Now it is a cult classic and its narrative reads like reportage.” —Anastas Michos, ASC

movies.title: Digger
movies.cast: Tom Cruise, Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg, Jesse Plemons
movies.description: Academy Award winner Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns to cinemas with Digger , a raucous black comedy satire helmed by Tom Cruise as Digger Rockwell, a wealthy oil tycoon—and the most powerful man in the world. When Rockwell unleashes a globe-threatening disaster, he embarks on a frantic mission to prove to humanity—his sister, (Hüller), the president (Goodman), the VP (Stuhlbarg), a scientist (Ahmed), and, well, everyone—that he is humanity’s savior. Shot entirely in VistaVision, Iñárritu’s latest is a vivid, big, and straight-up wacky entry into the resume of one of Mexico’s greatest filmmakers.

movies.title: Disclosure Day
movies.cast: Emily Blunt, Josh O'Connor, Colin Firth, Eve Hewson, Colman Domingo, Wyatt Russell
movies.description: If you found out we weren’t alone, if someone showed you, proved it to you, would that frighten you? This summer, the truth belongs to eight billion people. Spielberg’s latest sci-fi movie event, his first film since 2022’s The Fabelmans , returns to a legacy of grand, other-worldly, mysterious spectacle. Starring Emily Blunt ( Oppenheimer ), Josh O’Connor ( Challengers ), and Colin Firth ( The King’s Speech ), Disclosure Day thrills in the tense moment when the unknown becomes known.

movies.title: Dog Day Afternoon
movies.cast: Al Pacino, John Cazale, James Broderick, Charles Durning
movies.description: On a sweltering Brooklyn afternoon in 1972, Sonny (Al Pacino) and his anxious partner Sal (John Cazale) walk into a neighborhood bank expecting a quick score. Instead, a cascade of mistakes, unexpected complications, and mounting media attention transforms their plan into a public spectacle. As Detective Moretti (Charles Durning) closes in and Sonny's personal life becomes front-page news, tensions rise, loyalties are tested, and absurdity collides with desperation.

movies.title: Double Impact
movies.cast: Jean-Claude Van Damme, Geoffrey Lewis, Alonna Shaw, Corinna Everson, Philip Chan, Alan Scarfe, Bolo
movies.description:
Chad (Jean-Claude Van Damme), a charming, smooth karate instructor from Los Angeles is mysteriously urged to fly to China by the man who raised him like a son, Frank Avery (Geoffrey Lewis, “High Plains Drifter,” “Every Which Way But Loose”). There he meets Alex (Jean-Claude Van Damme), a streetwise gun-slinging smuggler raised on the back streets of Hong Kong. Chad and Alex discover they are twin brothers and were separated when their parents were brutally murdered twenty-five years ago.

Staff pick by Ray

Screening as part of our series Staff Picks 2026

movies.title: Dragon Superman
movies.cast: Kuei Chih-Pang, Lai Te-Nan, Chiang Ching-Hsia, Liu Ching, Wu Min, Wai Wang
movies.description:
A breakout success that spawned two sequels in rapid succession, Dragon Superman introduced Taiwanese audiences to the titular masked crusader, by day straight-arrow newspaperman San Lin, by night the bane of the chaos-sowing, satin suit-clad, hydrocephalic members of the Cosmos Gang. Fans of the Adam West Batman series, Mario Bava’s Danger: Diabolik, Japanese tokusatsu pictures, and swinging ’60s superheroics in general will find much to enjoy in this vivacious action romp, starring Kuei Chih-pang as the be-scarfed, motorcycle-riding vigilante, who has his hands full protecting a blind chanteuse (Wu Min), a supermarket magnate (Yang Weixi), and a hunk of Incan gold from the ne’er-do-wells.

movies.title: Drive
movies.cast: Ryan Gosling, Carey Mulligan, Bryan Cranston, Albert Brooks, Oscar Isaac, Christina Hendricks
movies.description: Drawing inspiration from Walter Hill’s The Driver, Refn’s high-style tour-de-force stars Ryan Gosling as a loner Los Angeles stunt driver who moonlights as a getaway wheelman on armed stickups, who’s put on a collision course with a nefarious criminal syndicate thanks to his protective affection for neighbor Carey Mulligan. A terse, tough, and morosely moody film propelled by a shimmering synth-pop score, with an extraordinary supporting cast that includes an against-type Albert Brooks as a sullen, profane gangster kingpin.

movies.title: Ebenezer
movies.cast: Johnny Depp, Rupert Grint, Daisy Ridley, Tramell Tillman, Ian McKellen, Andrea Riseborough
movies.description: This November, Johnny Depp is Ebenezer Scrooge. The name you know, the story you don’t. From Ti West, EBENEZER also stars Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley, Arthur Conti, Ellie Bamber, Henry Lloyd-Hughes, Charlie Murphy, with Tramell Tillman and Ian McKellen.

movies.title: Eleanor
movies.cast: Katrina Aldridge, Jordyn House
movies.description:
A medieval scandal gets an operatic glow-up in ELEANOR , a new work by Niccolo Seligmann about Eleanor Rykener — the gender-nonconforming Londoner whose 1394 arrest left the courts very confused.

This semi-staged performance at the experimental New Stage Performance Space on the Upper West Side dives into the story of Eleanor, who was arrested in London in 1394 while presenting as a woman. We only have one surviving document about Eleanor’s life, so we can’t know her full story – but this piece uses that fragment as a starting point to explore identity, gender, and belonging in the medieval world.

Niccolo Seligmann (they/them) brings a deeply personal lens to the work, and the role of Eleanor will be premiered by non-binary soprano Elisse Albian .
notes: Followed by a Q&A with Tracy Cowart and Sian Ricketts of medieval music ensemble ALKEMIE .

movies.title: Elsinore
movies.cast: Andrew Scott, Olivia Colman, Johnny Flynn, Billie Piper
movies.description: The deeply emotional and inspirational true story of Ian Charleson, a gifted actor whose greatest challenge becomes his greatest triumph. Facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit, and grace, Charleson delivers a courageous performance that becomes a source of healing and inspiration for those around him.

movies.title: Elsinore
movies.cast: Andrew Scott, Olivia Colman, Johnny Flynn, Billie Piper
movies.description: Andrew Scott plays Ian Charleson, the gifted Scottish stage star who prepares to take on Hamlet at London's National Theatre while living with AIDS. Facing his own mortality with wit, honesty, and grace, Charleson delivers a performance that becomes a source of strength for those around him. Olivia Colman, fresh off WICKER, co-stars in this story about the power of a final act.

movies.title: Emperor of the North
movies.cast: Lee Marvin, Ernest Borgnine, Keith Carradine, Charles Tyner, Malcolm Atterbury, Simon Oakland
movies.description:
Inspired by the writings of legendary hobo Leon Ray Livingston, under the pen name “A-No.1,” Aldrich’s tale of the risks run rail-riding in the ’30s northwest stars Lee Marvin as top tramp A-No.1, locked in a battle royale struggle with Ernest Borgnine’s fascistic, hobo-hatin’ conductor Shack on the speeding #19 of the Oregon, Pacific and Eastern Railroad, while Keith Carradine’s rascally fellow stowaway looks on. Featuring gorgeous location photography, suicidal stuntwork on speeding period locomotives, and bone-breaking action, Emperor of the North is Aldrich at his brutal best.

“Where a tramp is headed matters less than how long he can stay on the train, at least where it concerns the #19, ruled by the sadistic, bulging-eyed Shack. Outmaneuvering him becomes an irresistible challenge for seasoned hobos and, for railway workers who despise him just as much, a betting sport.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.title: Erupcja
movies.cast: Charli xcx, Lena Góra, Will Madden, Jeremy O. Harris, Agata Trzebuchowska, Maja Michnacka
movies.description: When Bethany (Charli xcx) and her soon-to-be fiancé (Will Madden) are unexpectedly stranded in Warsaw, Poland in the wake of a volcanic eruption, the former takes the explosive event as a sign to ditch her baggage, reunite with childhood friend Nel (Lena Góra), and traipse across lofts, clubs, and back alleys, all the while becoming entangled in an emotional web that challenges her sense of self. American maverick Pete Ohs ( Everything Beautiful Is Far Away ) directed, edited, photographed, and produced this dizzyingly charming European postcard, an anti-romantic comedy about the pains and pleasures of being in love. Join us for a Q&A following the May 6, 7:10pm screening with Pete Ohs and Jeremy O. Harris, moderated by Nia Dacosta

movies.title: Exit 8
movies.cast: Kazunari Ninomiya, Yamato Kochi, Naru Asanuma, Kotone Hanase, Nana Komatsu, Hirota Otsuka
movies.description: Director Genki Kawamura will join us for a Q&A on Friday, 4/10 at 8pm

movies.title: Fatherland
movies.cast: Hanns Zischler, Sandra Hüller
movies.description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

movies.title: Fatherland
movies.cast: Hanns Zischler, Sandra Hüller
movies.description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika—an actress, writer, and rally driver—embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

movies.title: Female Trouble
movies.cast: Divine, Mink Stole, David Lochary, Edith Massey, Mary Vivian Pearce, Cookie Mueller
movies.description:
“Sex offenses that would shock the Marquis de Sade!” sniffed critic Rex Reed in the Daily News, reviewing John Waters’ follow-up to the notorious Pink Flamingos . The perversities pile up in the tale of high-school delinquent and meatball sandwich-lover Dawn Davenport (played by Waters muse Divine), whose number one Christmas wish is for a pair of cha-cha heels. But her parents fail to heed her request, and her rage leads inexorably to stripping, prostitution, disfigurement, tabloid fame and mass murder.

Shot in Waters’ beloved native Baltimore on 16mm and featuring his regular Dreamlanders troupe–including Mink Stole, David Lochary, Mary Vivian Pearce, Edith Massey, and Cookie Mueller–this endlessly quotable, gloriously lurid satire was Divine’s favorite of his own films.

“The sordid tale of Dawn Davenport, who rises from high school hoyden to mistress of crime… A true original.” – Variety

Screening as part of Late Night Favorites: Fall 2026

Previously screened as part of our midnight series Late Night Favorites: Fall 2025, Sicks by John Waters and “Late-Night Favorites: Spring 2019.”

movies.title: Film Club
movies.description:
Film Noir Cinema presents: “FILM CLUB” - an evening with moving image.

The films are chosen each time by a different member of the club without anybody but the chooser knowing the title.

Pure cinematheque fun.

movies.title: Film Noir Monday
movies.description:
Film Noir Mondays are dedicated to bring to light lesser known as well as very obscure films that fit Film Noir cinema, including international titles.

In Noir fashion the movie titles are not revealed beforehand, keeping the audience in total darkness. . .

movies.title: Germany, Year Zero
movies.cast: Edmund Moeschke, Ernst Pittschau, Ingetraud Hinze
movies.description: Following the international acclaim and box office success of ROME, OPEN CITY and PAISAN, Rossellini took the first of many obstreperous swerves that would come to define his career. His next film would be another dispatch from war-torn Europe, with scenes playing out amidst the rubble with unvarnished immediacy, with unfamiliar and nonprofessional actors populating the cast—but this time, the protagonists would not be resistance fighters liberating Italy, but the defeated Germans muddling through their wasteland reich. Financed largely by the French government, GERMANY, YEAR ZERO became an experiment in radical empathy and its limits, casting about for signs of new life in a nation of crooks, unrepentant Nazis, and pederasts. The only innocent soul is twelve-year-old protagonist Edmund, who cannot qualify for a work permit, but must somehow earn a living to support his household. Even the child recognizes that he has no role models in this world: his brother is a mopey ex-soldier who refuses to register for a ration card, his father is an invalid who muses he’d be better off dead, his neighbors are coarse and severe, his friends are common swindlers, and his former school teacher still preaches that the strong must snuff out the weak. Unsentimental in the extreme and devoid of any comic relief, GERMANY YEAR ZERO plays like a seance for souls who have yet to recognize themselves as the walking dead.

movies.title: Ghost World
movies.cast: Thora Birch, Scarlett Johansson, Steve Buscemi, Brad Renfro, Illeana Douglas, Bob Balaban
movies.description:
The first film adaptation from the work of caustic cartoonist Daniel Clowes, Ghost World is a post-apocalyptic survival film set in the suburban AnyAmerica of 2001. Thora Birch and Scarlett Johansson co-star as two too-smart girls, freshly matriculated from high school and rudderless in early adulthood, who employ scalding irony as a ward to fend off the toxic effects of existence in a cultural wasteland, discovering an amiably creepy kindred spirit in the form of Steve Buscemi’s weedy record collector, Seymour. An anthem for opting out and modern-day classic, with editor Michael R. Miller displaying the gift for mordant, off-kilter comedy he’d honed working with the Coen Brothers.

Miller, ACE, moderated by editor Jamie Kirkpatrick, ACE, on Saturday, November 21st

movies.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
movies.cast: Minami Hamabe, Masami Nagasawa, Ryûnosuke Kamiki, Jun Kunimura, Sakura Andô, Yuki Yamada
movies.description: War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant. There is no third time. Everything ends here.

movies.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
movies.cast: Minami Hamabe, Masami Nagasawa, Ryûnosuke Kamiki, Jun Kunimura, Sakura Andô, Yuki Yamada
movies.description: War reduced Japan to zero. Godzilla plunged it into minus. Now the math gets even more terrifying. Takashi Yamazaki returns to direct, write, and oversee the visual effects for this epic follow-up to GODZILLA MINUS ONE, his Oscar-winning reinvention of Toho’s iconic monster. Set in 1949, two years after the events of the previous film, GODZILLA MINUS ZERO follows Japan’s hard-fought recovery as a new catastrophe threatens to erase it all. With returning stars Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe, bigger monster mayhem, and spectacular effects built for a huge screen, this is the latest chapter in a storied franchise that began in 1954. See the King of the Monsters at its most colossal, on the big screen.
notes: Presented in Japanese with English subtitles

movies.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
movies.cast: Lee Kang-sheng, Chen Shiang-Chyi, Kiyonobu Mitamura, Miao Tian, Shih Chun, Chen Chao-jung
movies.description: The Fu-Ho Grand, a movie palace in Taipei, is closing its doors. Its valedictory screening: King Hu’s 1967 wuxia epic Dragon Inn, playing to a motley smattering of spectators, including two stars of Hu’s original opus, Miao Tien and Shih Chun, watching their younger selves with tears in their eyes.

movies.title: Greetings from Out Here
movies.description: Accompanied by her dog Sam and a video camera, filmmaker Ellen Spiro traveled from Virginia to Texas and back exploring openly gay culture in the Deep South. Highlighted by spontaneous encounters with local eccentrics and mechanics (her van breaks down frequently), Greetings from Out Here provides detailed portraits of small-town queer Southerners—from Rita, a retired military officer turned drag queen in New Orleans to Iris, a Black lesbian living in a bus in the Ozarks. Filmed on location at the Texas Gay Rodeo, Mardi Gras, Gay Pride in Atlanta, Dollywood, Miss Miller's Eternal Love and Care Pet Cemetery, and the Short Mountain Radical Faerie sanctuary, Spiro captures the richness, vitality and courage of "out" gay Southern life in the early 1990s.

movies.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 1
movies.description:
“Gunvor Nelson launched her film career with a pair of raucous collage films made with her friend Dorothy Wiley. In Schmeerguntz, glamorized images of American womanhood clash with the reality of messy diapers and clogged kitchen sinks, revealing ‘a society which hides its animal functions beneath a shiny public surface’ (Film Quarterly). The surreal extravaganza Fog Pumas was a grand prize winner at the 1967 EXPRMTL festival in Knokke. My Name is Oona, perhaps Nelson’s best-known film, is an impressionistic portrait of her daughter with a memorably repetitive soundtrack partly created by Steve Reich. Kirsa Nicholina is at once a lyrical and boldly graphic birth film. Moons Pool, filmed entirely underwater with naked male and female bodies, is a dazzling example of Nelson’s visual and aural poetry. The serene Time Being is a loving, meditative film of Nelson’s mother, in bed, approaching death.” —Series curator David Schwartz

movies.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 2
movies.description:
“These three films, among Nelson’s most beautifully crafted works, were made during return trips to her home country, leading up to her move back to Sweden in 1993 after teaching for more than two decades at the San Francisco Art Institute. Frame Line blends still photographs (some of which she paints on) and moving images, showing the full range of her artistry as she revisits her past. Red Shift, filmed at her parents’ home in Kristinehamn, is a unique hybrid film with scripted and documentary elements, with Nelson, her daughter Oona, and her mother as ‘performers,’ punctuated by readings of letters from Calamity Jane to her daughter. Old Digs weaves together a murmuring soundtrack of a family gathering with roaming color images of a rustic village, layered with cut-out images added through stop-motion animation.” —Series curator David Schwartz

Frame Line (Gunvor Nelson, 1983, 22 mins)

Red Shift (Gunvor Nelson, 1984, 47 mins)

Old Digs (Gunvor Nelson, 1993, 21 mins)
