movies.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 3
movies.description:
"Gunvor Nelson’s experience as a painter before becoming a filmmaker is at its most evident in these strikingly graphic films, all of which involve hands-on manipulation of the surfaces and textures of still and moving images. Light Years and Light Years Expanding use collage techniques while traversing the Swedish landscape, by train in the former and car in the latter. The final two works are made entirely in the studio. Nelson describes Natural Features as ‘a free associative and playfully bizarre form of animation. Here I used mirrors, water, toys, cut-outs, photographs, paint, ink … in many different combinations. The central theme is face.’ Experimenting with video, Nelson performs magic in Trace Elements, creating a visual dance between her camera and her shadow.” —Series curator David Schwartz

Light Years (Gunvor Nelson, 1987, 28 mins)

Natural Features (Gunvor Nelson, 1990, 28 mins)

Trace Elements (Gunvor Nelson, 2003, 9 mins)

movies.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty
movies.description: Haru and Luis love competing in Tokyo’s ballroom dance scene, but after tragedy strikes, Haru withdraws into isolation. When friends coax her back to the studio, she develops an infatuation with the new instructor and must face what comes next as sparks fly. Steeped in sorrow but bursting with joy, Wladyk’s tight feature marries exhilarating choreography with equally dynamic camera movement, cultivating a vibrant visual ode to dance and its power to transcend grief.

movies.title: Hamnet
movies.cast: Jessie Buckley, Paul Mescal, Emily Watson, Joe Alwyn, Jacobi Jupe, Noah Jupe
movies.description: In 16th-century England, an impoverished Latin tutor named William Shakespeare (Mescal) meets free-spirited Agnes (Buckley), sparking an affair that leads to marriage and three children. As Will seeks his fortune in the London theater, Agnes anchors the domestic sphere alone. The couple’s bond is tested when tragedy strikes, but their shared experience sets the stage for the creation of Shakespeare’s timeless masterpiece, Hamlet . Academy Award-winning filmmaker Chloé Zhao ( Nomadland , The Rider ) illuminates the complexities of love and the healing power of art and creativity.

movies.title: Hope
movies.cast: Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Hoyeon, Alicia Vikander, Michael Fassbender, Taylor Russell
movies.description: In the remote South Korean village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung-min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the area. In a forest nearby, a party of hunters including Sung-ki (Zo In-sung) set out to track the beast, only to find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading: what begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through into a tragedy of cosmic proportions. Premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, Hope “races from modern-day western to action thriller to horror film to science-fiction epic—all while retaining the full-throttle energy and sweaty cult-movie atmosphere of a 1970s exploitation flick,” according to the BBC.

movies.title: How to Rob a Bank
movies.cast: Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz, Anna Sawai, Rhenzy Feliz, Pete Davidson, John C. Reilly
movies.description: We love a good heist movie, especially when the getaway is as stylish as the score. In HOW TO ROB A BANK, JOHN WICK director David Leitch brings his kinetic action sensibilities to a crew of social media-savvy robbers (Nicholas Hoult, Pete Davidson) who broadcast their daring heists for the world to see. But viral fame attracts the wrong kind of attention, and a veteran FBI agent (John C. Reilly) and a brilliant software engineer (Zoë Kravitz) are closing in. Assemble your wolfpack and catch this one on the big screen.

movies.title: I Love Boosters
movies.cast: Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie, Taylour Paige, Poppy Liu, Eiza González, LaKeith Stanfield
movies.description: In another surreal, politically-charged, and straight-up weird outing from eccentric director Boots Riley ( Sorry to Bother You ), I Love Boosters follows a crew of professional shoplifters (Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie) as they take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven (Demi Moore)—in an effort they deem a community service. Sneak preview screening on May 19 at 7:30pm followed by a Q&A with Boots Riley

movies.title: I Play Rocky
movies.cast: Anthony Ippolito, AnnaSophia Robb, Tracy Letts, Jay Duplass, Matt Dillon, Stephan James, Kiki Seto
movies.description: An electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn’t just meant to write Rocky –he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. Told “no” at every turn, Sylvester Stallone bets everything on himself, holding the line on playing the lead against seemingly impossible odds. The result is the ultimate underdog story behind the ultimate underdog movie.

movies.title: I Want Your Sex
movies.cast: Olivia Wilde, Cooper Hoffman, Mason Gooding, Chase Sui Wonders, Johnny Knoxville, Margaret Cho
movies.description: The latest from New Queer Cinema pioneer Gregg Araki ( Mysterious Skin , The Doom Generation , White Bird in a Blizzard ), I Want Your Sex follows Elliot, a kind-hearted if unmotivated twentysomething (Hoffman), whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes young Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries, and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli XCX) and repressed roommate (Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the lines between satire, romantic comedy, mystery, and murder blur through the colorful and edgy visual language for which Araki is best known.

movies.title: In Cold Blood
movies.cast: Robert Blake, Scott Wilson, John Forsythe, Jeff Corey
movies.description: In this adaptation of Truman Capote's seminal true-crime novel, ex-convicts Perry Smith (Robert Blake) and Richard Dick Hickock (Scott Wilson) hatch a plan to rob a wealthy Kansas family, the Clutters. The men enter the Clutter home expecting to find a safe filled with cash, but in fact find no money at all. Enraged, they kill the entire family and flee. While on the run, they face not only the realities of their terrible crime but also their own earthly impermanence.

movies.title: In the Mouth
movies.cast: Colin Burgess, Paul Rothery, Sage Francis, Caren Lioce, Earl Fechter, Edward Green
movies.description: A perpetual worrywart finds himself unable to leave his house after discovering a giant version of himself protruding from his front lawn. A Slamdance 2025 entry.

movies.title: Indonesian Mystery Movie
movies.description: Is this the most fun you can have on a vacation to Jakarta? Grab a Freddy glove and find out when you join us for this 1990s Indonesian mystery movie starring Southeast Asia’s preeminent scream queen.

movies.title: Is This Thing On?
movies.cast: Will Arnett, Laura Dern, Andra Day, Bradley Cooper, Christine Ebersole, Ciarán Hinds
movies.description: As their marriage quietly unravels, Alex (Arnett) faces middle age and an impending divorce, seeking new purpose in the New York comedy scene while Tess (Dern) confronts the sacrifices she made for their family—forcing them to navigate co-parenting, identity, and whether love can take a new form. Bradley Cooper writes, directs, and co-stars in this understated, affecting portrait of the challenges and opportunities of starting over in middle age.

movies.title: It Ends
movies.cast: Billy Bush, Michael DeBarge
movies.description: A group of recent grads head out on a late-night drive for grub, hoping to enjoy one final hangout before their paths diverge. Instead, they accidentally turn onto an endless two-lane hellscape surrounded by untold horrors and cosmic forces beyond their understanding. Written, directed, and edited by Alexander Ullom in his directorial debut, It Ends premiered at the 2025 South by Southwest Festival, and has been praised by Variety as a “brilliant” modern retelling of Jean-Paul Sartre’s No Exit .

movies.title: It Follows
movies.cast: Maika Monroe, Keir Gilchrist, Daniel Zovatto, Jake Weary, Olivia Luccardi, Lili Sepe
movies.description: Mitchell’s Detroit-shot sophomore film, winner of the Next Wave award at Austin’s Fantastic Fest in 2014 and the breakout horror phenomenon of the following year, is a work of potent sexual dread, in which erotic congress transmits something much worse than a dose of clap: the attentions of a spectral, shape-shifting entity that pursues the afflicted with methodical single-mindedness, a pursuit that ends in terrible carnage. Enigmatic and unsettling, its thick atmosphere of paranoia incalculably added to by a soundtrack courtesy electronic musician Disasterpiece (Rich Vreeland), per Pitchfork “a score that announces when something is about to happen, only to suddenly upend expectations and leave the room on edge.”

movies.title: Je t'aime, je t'aime
movies.cast: Claude Rich, Olga Georges-Picot, Anouk Ferjac, Van Doude, Claire Duhamel, Bernard Fresson
movies.description: A “quiet mixture of science fiction with a love story as subtle as anything in Rohmer or Rivette” [Raymond Durgnat], Resnais’s definition-defying film stars Claude Rich as an unsuccessful suicide who, on leaving hospital, agrees to participate in an experiment in time travel—one that will bring fragments of his past rushing back is disordered shards.
notes: Introduction by filmmaker Kogonada on Sunday, November 8th

movies.cast: Mason Reeves, Channing Tatum, Gemma Chan, Phillip Ettinger
movies.description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Mason Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence.

movies.title: Jurassic Park
movies.cast: Sam Neill, Laura Dern, Jeff Goldblum, Richard Attenborough, Bob Peck, Martin Ferrero
movies.description: The prehistoric and the state-of-the-art meet in Spielberg’s game-changing adaptation of Michael Crichton’s novel, which lays its scene on a Costa Rican island newly populated with regenerated saurians. The CGI was all anyone could talk about when it was released, but today you may notice the extensive use of sophisticated analog effects, and of course the peerless ensemble cast including Sam Neill, Laura Dern, Jeff Goldblum, Newman from Seinfeld, and the “six-foot turkey” kid—the human factor that makes Jurassic Park truly timeless.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Kaili Blues
movies.cast: Chen Yongzhong, Daqing Zhao, Feiyang Luo, Xie Lixun, Shuai Zeng, Qin Guangqian
movies.description: Chinese filmmaker Bi Gan’s award-winning directorial debut is an audacious work that announced a major new filmmaking talent. Country doctor Chen Sheng sets out on a train journey to search for his brother’s abandoned child, only to find himself in a dreamlike world where the boundaries between past, present, and future—and between fantasy and reality—are porous. This remarkable visual achievement, which feels as singular and alien as the films of Apichatpong Weerasethakul, was shot in the mining village Kaili, the director’s birthplace, and incorporates poetry he’s been writing since he was a teenager.

movies.title: Keane
movies.cast: Damian Lewis, Abigail Breslin, Amy Ryan, Tina Holmes, Liza Colón-Zayas, John Tormey
movies.description: Kerrigan, whose debut Clean, Shaven was one of the most harrowingly immersive portrayals of schizophrenia ever put on screen, dove back into the depths of a turbulent, fractured mind with the equally-if-not-more accomplished Keane, in which Damian Lewis, playing a mentally unsound William Keane, wanders the dingy corridors of the Port Authority Bus Terminal and other sordid pockets of New York City. Haunted by the memory of his young daughter’s abduction, he eventually strikes up a relationship with a young mother and her child (Amy Ryan and Abigail Breslin). A work of brilliantly sustained discomfort and tactile seediness, raw, rigorous, and entirely riveting.

movies.title: L'Amore
movies.cast: Anna Magnani, Federico Fellini, Peparuolo, Amelia Robert In Italian with English subtitles.
movies.description: Conceived as an homage to the range and artistry of Anna Magnani, L’AMORE is a diptych that drags the actress to the brink and watches, mouth agape, as she leaps into the abyss. The first part—“The Human Voice”—adapts a one-act play by Jean Cocteau, which Magnani had performed on stage in 1942, playing a woman whose only connection to her lover runs through the telephone wire. Shot in a French studio over two weeks with money that Rossellini had procured for GERMANY YEAR ZERO, this intensely claustrophobic showcase for Magnani (and her dog, Micia) renders a break-up as a world-historic event—as it always is for those so spurned. The second episode—“The Miracle”—was based on an original idea by Fellini, who also co-stars as a silent vagabond whom Magnani’s talkative goatherd believes to be the incarnation of Saint Joseph. Throwing herself upon the saint’s blissful body, Magnani wakes in a daze, pregnant and ever closer to the divine. If the monks can report sightings of the Madonna, why cannot Magnani follow her holy path? Although “The Miracle” aroused no complaints from the Vatican, it faced extraordinary hostility in the US, where the lay Catholics of the Legion of Decency launched a successful campaign for the New York Board of Regents to rescind the film’s exhibition license on the basis of alleged sacrilege. Distributor Joseph Burstyn appealed the decision all the way to the Supreme Court, which ultimately ruled in his favor, belatedly bringing cinema under the protection of the First Amendment, and sowing the seeds of censorship’s demise. A miracle indeed.

movies.title: La Bola Negra
movies.cast: Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Lola Dueñas, Penélope Cruz, Glenn Close
movies.description: LA BOLA NEGRA is a bold, passionate triptych spanning nearly a century of Spanish history from the 30s to modern day. The film tells the story of three men whose lives are intimately connected through desire, pain, and inheritance.

movies.title: La Bola Negra
movies.cast: Guitarricadelafuente, Milo Quifes, Carlos González
movies.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

movies.title: Lady Killer
movies.cast: Jean Gabin, Mireille Balin, Pierre Etchepare, Henri Poupon, Jean Aymé, Pierre Magnier
movies.description: Grémillon was still in the employ of Berlin’s UFA Studios when he began shooting this adaptation of an André Boucler novel which stars Jean Gabin as a Don Juan of the French Foreign Legion who sets his sights on seducing Mireille Balin—and accidentally falls in love for real. The atmospheric work of cinematographer Günther Rittau (The Blue Angel) connects Grémillon’s film to the legacy of German expressionism, while the electric reunion of Pépé le Moko co-stars Gabin and Balin and the film’s pervasive air of tragic romantic fatalism show an affinity with French poetic realism. Distributor: Grasshopper Film

movies.title: Lady Windermere's Fan
movies.cast: May McAvoy, Ronald Colman, Irene Rich
movies.description: May McAvoy’s long-lost and now-notorious mom Irene Rich returns, but demands money from her aristocratic son-in-law for her silence, then tries to stymie Lord Ronald Colman’s designs on her daughter—but there’s that darn fan to be accounted for. Witty visual storytelling makes up for the absence of Oscar Wilde’s epigrams.

movies.title: Leviathan
movies.cast: Declan Conneely, Johnny Gatcombe, Adrian Guillette, Brian Jannelle, Clyde Lee, Arthur Smith
movies.description: Setting out on the high seas of the North Atlantic aboard a Massachusetts-based commercial fishing trawler, Castaing-Taylor and Paravel produced one of the most mesmerizing, visually distinctive, and startlingly immediate documentaries of the 21st century, using the unique agility of their lightweight GoPro cameras to capture perspectives unlike anything theretofore seen in cinema, from gull-like views of the vessel to plunges into the slimy viscera of the day’s catch. “The density of aural and visual stimuli overwhelms—and liberates.”—Melissa Anderson, The Village Voice
notes: Q&A with filmmaker Lucien Castaing-Taylor on Sunday, December 6th

movies.title: Leviticus
movies.cast: Joe Bird, Stacy Clausen, Mia Wasikowska, Nicholas Hope, Tyallah Bullock, Ewen Leslie
movies.description: In a conservative Australian town, the most terrifying thing facing two queer teens isn’t just the ostracization of their community, but a more sinister entity that takes the form of the person they desire most: each other. With captivating performances from its breakout stars, this striking debut from director Adrian Chiarella deftly weaves a truly haunting premise and moments of sweet romance into a larger tapestry investigating the toll of contemporary bigotry.

movies.title: Littermates
movies.cast: Joey Bader, Kaylee McGregor, Oliver Woolf, Jack Redmayne, Kenichiro Thomson, Honor Koe
movies.description:
At Chester’s cottage, good behavior earns karaoke. Getting answers is a little more complicated.

After a mysterious apocalyptic(ish) attack leaves them bloodied, disoriented, and unable to speak, Liam (Joey Bader) and Mel (Kaylee McGregor) take refuge in the English countryside. Their oddball host, Chester (Oliver Woolf), feeds them, helps them recover, and introduces a system of rewards: behave yourself, earn “nifties,” cash them in for hot-tub time and dance parties.

Beyond the cottage, things are less nifty. But within it, a makeshift family is taking shape. While Liam embraces their new life, Mel grows increasingly curious about the world Chester insists is too dangerous to enter…

In their feature debut, directors Scott Tinkham and Michael Woloson mix deadpan comedy, sibling rivalry, and creeping unease in a coming-of-age story about people who have to grow up all over again. Winner of the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Manchester Film Festival and the Narrative Feature Audience Award at Dances With Films LA 2026, this has the sort of sensibilities that fans of Yorgos Lanthimos and Ben Wheatley will adore… and it’s a natural fit as an Alamo Exclusive.

movies.title: Little Fugitive
movies.director: Morris Engel, Ruth Orkin, Ray Ashley Co-written and Co-produced by Ray Ashley
movies.cast: Richie Andrusco WINNER Venice Film Festival – Silver Lion, 1953 NOMINEE Academy Awards® – Best Writing, 1954
movies.description: Brooklynite Richie Andrusco’s on the run from the cops after the accidental shooting of his big brother—only trouble is, Richie’s only seven, the “shooting” was just a dumb ketchup-splashed gag by his brothers and cronies, and Mom won’t be back from Grandma’s till the next day. But with six bucks in his pocket and all of Coney Island for a hide-out, how tough can things be, as Richie rides the merry-go-round, takes a cowboy photo, tries out his swings in the batting cage, scarfs down hot dogs, soda, watermelon, and corn on the cob, and gets hooked on the pony ride—he refinances by scouring under the boardwalk for two-cent deposit soda bottles—and even his frantically searching big brother takes a break to ride The Parachute Jump. With a concealed custom-made 35mm camera (which Godard later asked to borrow), legendary photographer Engel—and crew including future wife Ruth Orkin, herself a photography titan—captured unknowing crowds, a phenomenal performance by pint-sized non-pro Richie, and a perfect time capsule of Coney in the waning years of its heyday.

movies.title: Lost Highway
movies.cast: Patricia Arquette, Bill Pullman, Balthazar Getty, Robert Blake, Robert Loggia, Michael Massee
movies.description: Few filmmakers have shown themselves so adept at plumbing the depths of the subconscious without coming up for air as Lynch, whose Lost Highway—inspired loosely by still-fresh coverage of the O. J. Simpson trial—begins as a dark domestic drama concerning a sexually incompetent saxophonist (Bill Pullman) and his wife (Patricia Arquette), morphs into a movie about a cocksman mechanic (Balthazar Getty) who gets involved with a gangster’s girl (Arquette, again), and ends with an unleashing of apocalyptic, purgative flame… Whether you take it as a cinematic depiction of a psychogenic fugue state or a free-associative disgorging of images from Hollywood’s id, Lynch’s film has the pull of a whirlpool and the terrible logic of a nightmare.

movies.title: Maddie’s Secret
movies.cast: John Early, Kate Berlant, Eric Rahill, Kristen Johnston, Claudia O'Doherty, Conner O'Malley
movies.description: Inspired by Douglas Sirk, Todd Haynes, Showgirls , and the nearly pornographic world of online food influencers, comedian, writer, and actor John Early makes his critically acclaimed directorial debut with the story of a breakout new-media star who’s hiding a secret. Early portrays Maddie, a dishwasher at L.A. food-content creation studio Gourmaybe, who makes her own vegetarian cooking videos at home with help from her adoring husband (Eric Rahill). When one of her videos goes viral, Maddie is thrust into the influencer sphere herself, straining her bond with her sassy queer BFF (Kate Berlant) and threatening to expose her struggle with an eating disorder. Blending satire and melodrama, the film announces a bold new voice in contemporary cinema.

movies.title: Mandy
movies.cast: Nicolas Cage, Andrea Riseborough, Linus Roache, Ned Dennehy, Olwen Fouéré, Richard Brake
movies.description: After Nicolas Cage’s pacific, reclusive life with his girlfriend Mandy is interrupted by the arrival of members of an apocalyptic cannibalistic cult, the Children of the New Dawn, he’ll have to pay a visit to his old pal, Caruthers (Duke), to pick up his trusty crossbow, sights set on revenge. Duke provides a moment of authority and gravity, just before this strikingly styled early ‘80s-set instant cult classic plunges into madness courtesy of Cage at his most frantic, feral, and fatally fierce.

movies.title: Manhunter: The Final Cut
movies.description: The film that introduced audiences to psychiatrist-cum-serial killer Hannibal Lecter—here spelled “Lecktor,” the role originated by a wonderfully gelid Brian Cox—Mann’s magnificent thriller stars William Petersen as Will Graham, an FBI profiler whose day-and-night dedication to his work threatens to unravel his psyche, recruiting Dr. Lecktor to help him track down an at-large murderer whose penchant for masticating his prey has led police to dub him the Tooth Fairy. (The part is played by a looming, melancholy Tom Noonan.) Mann, whose “MTV cops” series Miami Vice was a primetime giant when Manhunter was released, recognized the crucial importance of a good soundtrack, and this one’s a doozy, with tracks from Shriekback, The Reds, and The Prime Movers, and Iron Butterfly’s “In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida” providing a needle drop for the ages.

movies.title: Married To The Mob
movies.cast: Michelle Pfeiffer, Alec Baldwin, Dean Stockwell, Matthew Modine, Mercedes Ruehl, Oliver Platt
movies.description: An undercover FBI agent falls in love with a recently widowed mafia wife, who is trying to restart her life following her husband's murder while being pursued by a libidinous mafia kingpin seeking to claim her for himself.

movies.title: Marty Supreme
movies.cast: Timothée Chalamet, Gwyneth Paltrow, Odessa A'zion, Kevin O'Leary, Tyler, The Creator, Fran Drescher
movies.description: Timothée Chalamet “makes one of the most colossal movie performances of the 21st century seem as natural as a lay-up” ( IndieWire ) in the latest offering from director Josh Safdie (co-director, Good Time , Uncut Gems ). Performing with a distinguished cast that includes Gwyneth Paltrow, Odessa A'zion, and Tyler Okonma (a.k.a. Tyler, the Creator), Chalamet gives “the defining performance of his still-burgeoning career” ( Variety ) as would-be ping-pong champion Marty Mauser, a young man with a dream no one respects, who goes to hell and back in pursuit of greatness.

movies.title: Medea
movies.cast: Udo Kier, Kirsten Olesen, Henning Jensen, Solbjørg Højfeldt, Preben Lerdorff Rye, Baard Owe
movies.description: Based on an unfilmed screenplay by Carl Theodor Dreyer and, of course, Euripides’s tragedy of the same title, von Trier’s made-for-television film—save for two epiphanic eruptions—is uncharacteristically austere, the enfant terrible of Danish cinema making himself a medium for the Old Master’s vision, setting the source material in a pre-Christian Denmark. “An experimental film in the true sense of the word… Taking the greatest limitation of video—the medium’s lack of depth of field—Mr. von Trier turns it into a strength, flattening perspectives in a way that collapses his foreground characters into the tumultuous backgrounds (waves, wind-swept fields) that surround and dominate them.” —Dave Kehr, The New York Times

movies.title: Memento
movies.cast: Guy Pearce, Carrie-Anne Moss, Joe Pantoliano, Mark Boone Junior, Russ Fega, Jorja Fox
movies.description: The indie sensation that put a young English director named Christopher Nolan on the map for good, this strikingly original, ornately structured neo-noir stars Guy Pearce as Leonard, a man on a mission of revenge after a savage attack that left his wife dead and him with anterograde amnesia, unable to store new short-term memory and forced to rely on an elaborate note-taking system in order to continue his single-minded pursuit of justice. “A brilliant feat of rug-pulling… [Nolan is] clearly excited by the way the medium can manipulate time and information, folding straightforward events and simple motives into Möbius strips of paradox and indeterminacy… Like an existential crossword puzzle, or a pungent 50’s B-thriller with a script by Jorge Luis Borges.” —The New York Times
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Millennium Mambo
movies.cast: Shu Qi, Jack Kao, Duan Chun-hao, Doze Niu Cheng-Tse, Jun Takeuchi, Yi-Hsuan Chen
movies.description: A stylish and seductive submersion into the techno-scored neon nightlife of Taipei, Hou’s much-misunderstood marvel stars Shu Qi (The Assassin) as an aimless bar hostess drifting away from her blowhard boyfriend and towards Jack Kao’s suave, sensitive gangster. Structured as a flashback to the then-present from the then-future of 2011, it’s a transfixing trance-out of a movie, drenched in club lights, ecstatic endorphin-rush exhilaration, and a nagging undercurrent of ennui. Hou and longtime cinematographer Lee here break from their familiar pattern of elegantly composed long shot long takes to create something both more intimate and hectic, a film whose shallow-focus images, jittery camerawork, and cramped locations evoke both the claustrophobic character of Taiwan’s capital city and, in Lee’s words, “the feeling of youth.”

movies.title: Minotaur
movies.cast: Dmitriy Mazurov, Iris Lebedeva, Boris Kudrin
movies.description:
Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in.

The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev ( Loveless , Leviathan ), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times.

Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence.

A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

movies.title: Miroirs No. 3
movies.cast: Paula Beer, Barbara Auer, Matthias Brandt, Enno Trebs, Philip Froissant, Victoire Laly
movies.description: When piano student Laura (Beer) miraculously survives a car crash, she finds herself in the devoted care of a local woman. Her recovery becomes two-fold as she heals physically and attempts to reconnect with the world, finding a strange harmony with her new adoptive family. Acclaimed director Christian Petzold ( Phoenix , Transit ) spins a modern gothic fairytale revolving around the lies we tell ourselves and the strange ways that grief, connection, and humanity bind and sustain us.

movies.title: Moonlight Superman
movies.cast: Kuei Chih-Pang, Lai Te-Nan, Wai Wang, Liu Ching, Wu Min, Yang Wei-Hsi
movies.description:
Kuei Chih-pang returns as newspaper reporter San Lin and his alter ego, scourge of Taiwan’s evildoers, in this first sequel to Dragon Superman, a palpable hit when released earlier the same year. His foes are, again, the indefatigable Cosmic Gang; his allies include La Te-nan’s gormless photographer “Mr. Mischief” and a trio of junior crime-fighters called the “Detective Boys,” in desperate need of Dragon Superman’s help when taken hostage after bearing witness to a crime. Will Moonlight Superman come to the rescue in time? What, precisely, is the role of the Flying Tiger magic troupe in all of this mischief, and how did they obtain the secret of invulnerability? Your ticket buys you the whole seat, but you’ll only be using the edge when you experience… Moonlight Superman!

movies.cast: Anne Hathaway, Michaela Coel, Hunter Schafer, FKA twigs, Sian Clifford, Kaia Gerber

Between original songs from Charli XCX, a protagonist loosely-inspired by Taylor Swift, and a cast including Hathaway, Coel, Hunter Schafer, and FKA Twigs, Lowery’s ( The Green Knight ) latest combines striking fashion with daring drama.

movies.cast: Sophie Okonedo, Katherine Mallen-Kupferer, Tara Mallen, Chloe Coleman, Iman Vellani, David Hyde Pier

movies.title: Museum Hours
movies.cast: Mary Margaret O'Hara, Bobby Sommer, Ela Piplits, Marcus O'Hara, Deborah Gzesh, Marco Calamita
movies.description: A chance meeting between Johann (Bobby Sommer), a guard at Vienna’s Kunsthistorisches Museum with a philosophical bent, and Anne (Mary Margaret O’Hara), a Canadian stranger newly arrived in the city who has taken refuge in its galleries, is the jumping off point for Cohen’s sublimely cerebral, dialogue-driven film of ideas, chockablock with observations on urban life, the role of the museum as repository of living history, the paintings of Pieter Bruegel the Elder, and much else besides. “Fluidly mixes fiction and non-fiction, scripted and improvisational scenes into a narrative collage that feels organic… Allows meaning to accrete through the mingling of open-ended meditations on history, art, urbanism, and personal biography.” —The Brooklyn Rail

movies.title: My Brother's Wedding
movies.cast: Everett Silas, Jessie Holmes, Gaye Shannon-Burnett, Ronnie Bell, Dennis Kemper, Sally Easter
movies.description:
South Central LA, the early 1980s. Pierce Mundy (Everett Silas) is always on the move without ever really getting anywhere – kept busy by his parents, their dry cleaning shop, friends and neighbors. His childhood buddies are all in prison or dead and his best friend Soldier (Ronnie Bell) is just getting out of jail. Pierce’s brother Wendell (Monte Easter), on the other hand, is an up-and-coming lawyer set to marry an upper-middle-class woman (Gaye Shannon-Burnett). Pierce is entirely lacking in ambition, to the consternation of his Bible-thumping mother (Jessie Holmes), and yet he is an integral part of life in the neighborhood. When Soldier is killed in a car accident, Pierce’s conflicting obligations to family and friends manifest in the choice between his brother’s wedding and his best friend’s funeral, both falling on the same day. Charles Burnett’s second feature after Killer of Sheep is a tragicomic classic of New Black Cinema in which lived realities are shown in even the smallest of supporting roles, complex and attentive. Pierce’s wanderings reveal a portrait of a young man and a community defined in equal measure by stagnation, resignation, resistance and joie de vivre.

Digitally restored and remastered by Milestone Films in collaboration with the UCLA Film & Television Archive and the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive. A Milestone Films release.

movies.title: National Theatre Live: Dear England
movies.cast: Joseph Fiennes, Gina McKee, Will Fletcher, Crystal Candie, Will Close, Tony Turner
movies.description: Part love letter to the beautiful game, part biographical retelling, writer James Graham’s play Dear England follows the trajectory of manager Gareth Southgate and his attempted resurrection of the historically underperforming English national football team through three pivotal tournaments: the 2018 World Cup, UEFA Euro 2020, and the 2022 World Cup. Nominated for nine Olivier awards upon its 2024 run (including Best New Play for Graham), the National Theatre’s screening of the football stage sensation arrives on BAM screens for a select engagement. Presented as part of a multi-year partnership with BAM and National Theatre. Bringing the National Theatre to New York—on stage, on screen, and in the classroom.

movies.title: Nayak (The Hero)
movies.cast: Uttam Kumar, Sharmila Tagore, Bireswar Sen, Kamu Mukherjee, Susmita Mukherjee, Jamuna Sinha
movies.description:
Uttam Kumar, one of the leading matinee idols of Bengali cinema in his day, plays a film star who, depressed by the middling box office of his latest film, decides to hop a train from Calcutta to Delhi, where he’s slated to receive a prestigious national award, en route baring his soul in a lengthy interview with a journalist played by Sharmila Tagore.

“Trains often spell escape for characters in Ray’s films; Pather Panchali’s image of children running through a field to chase a locomotive is one of his most poignant. Nayak reverses the situation somewhat. For fading movie star Arindam Mukherjee (played uncomfortably close to type by matinee idol Uttam Kumar), the train he boards to avoid a flurry of bad press ends up returning him, nightmarishly, to himself.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.title: Naza
movies.cast: Yuval Abraham, Benjamin Netanyahu
movies.description:
In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them.

We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

— Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

movies.title: News from Home + Interior NY Subway, 14th Street
movies.description:
Akerman was 26 years old and living in New York City, away from her native Belgium and her mother, when she teamed with DP Babette Mangolte to film this diary/essay/poem in subway stations and on street corners, their images to eventually be paired with Akerman’s recitals of her mother’s fretful letters. Arguably this extraordinary filmmaker’s most perfect and poignant nonfiction work, both one of the greatest portraits of a city ever put on film and a troubling, touching depiction of maternal love. Screens in the English-language version.

“Though Chantal Akerman’s voice can be heard throughout News from Home, her image is only briefly glimpsed, in a reflection on the train. We can’t quite see her, but others undoubtedly can—men, especially, gawk unashamedly, a reminder that the graffiti-covered subway of 1976 New York was often a place of danger and hostility.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.title: Nightcrawler
movies.cast: Jake Gyllenhaal, Rene Russo, Riz Ahmed, Bill Paxton
movies.description: Jake Gyllenhaal gives an acting masterclass in this instant classic thriller set in Los Angeles’ nocturnal underbelly. Gyllenhaal stars as Lou Bloom, a sociopathic creep who discovers the high-stakes world of freelance crime journalism. Accidentally stumbling across a news crew while at the scene of a car wreck, Lou muscles into the dangerous cutthroat realm of “nightcrawling”: where each police siren wail equals a possible windfall and victims are converted into dollars and cents. Aided by a veteran amoral TV producer (Rene Russo), a naive camera assistant (Riz Ahmed) and an equally creepy competitive nemesis (Bill Paxton), Lou blurs the line between observer and participant to become the star of his own story.

movies.title: Nirvanna the Band the Show Season 1
movies.description: Two lifelong best friends and roommates are planning the greatest musical act in the history of the modern world. Without ever playing a note, Nirvanna the Band plan to take Toronto by storm, one scheme at time.

movies.title: Nirvanna the Band the Show Season 2
movies.description: A quest to perform at a rock club is at the center of this comedy series that melds fiction with reality. Show creators Matt Johnson and Jay McCarrol star as best friends and roommates who devise a number of schemes in the hopes of getting their band booked to play a show at the Rivoli, a modest Toronto club. The duo goes to unnecessary extremes to land the gig, sometimes causing real-world madness with thousands of extras who are unaware they're on a TV show. Their adventures include sneaking a film into the Sundance Film Festival and disrupting the "Star Wars: The Force Awakens" premiere.

movies.title: No Other Choice
movies.cast: Lee Byung-hun, Son Ye-jin, Park Hee-soon, Lee Sung-min, Yeom Hye-ran, Cha Seung-won
movies.description: South Korea’s Academy Awards submission for Best Foreign Film is being hailed by critics as an utter masterpiece and earned a rapturous nine-minute standing ovation at this year’s Venice Film Festival. No Other Choice follows one man’s berserk search for a new job after he is abruptly laid off from the paper company where he worked for 25 years. The visionary Park Chan-wook ( Oldboy , Decision to Leave ) helms this captivating black-comedy thriller—one of the most highly anticipated and acclaimed films of the season—adapted from Donald E. Westlake’s 1997 novel The Ax .

movies.title: Nocturama
movies.cast: Finnegan Oldfield, Vincent Rottiers, Hamza Meziani, Manal Issa, Laure Valentinelli, Martin Petit-Guyot
movies.description: Bonello’s ingeniously structured terror attack thriller opens with a group of tense, shifty teens prowling the streets and subways of Paris, in the midst, as it happens, of pulling off an intricately planned bombing plot. After the explosions, however, the film becomes something altogether different, as these pretty, vacant subversives tuck away inside a luxe department store and lose themselves in consumer culture—clothes, televisions, toys, and a stirring soundtrack that includes Blondie, Chief Keef, Shirley Bassey, Willow Smith, and Bonello’s menacing electronic score—all the while oblivious to the authorities tightening a net around them. A damning “allegory of nihilism and decadence” (Film Comment), fairly steeped in late Millennial malaise.

movies.title: NOFX: 40 Years of Fuckin' Up
movies.cast: Fat Mike, El Hefe, Eric Melvin, Erik Sandin
movies.description: 40 YEARS OF FUCKIN' UP is SPINAL TAP, but real. It's a film about the infamous, fairly unfamous, and beloved punk rock band NOFX. This is the unbelievable story about how a group of untalented, drug-addicted teenage punks somehow became the most successful independent band in history – and they did it haphazardly, entirely on their own.

movies.title: Obsession
movies.cast: Michael Johnston, Inde Navarrette, Cooper Tomlinson, Megan Lawless, Andy Richter, Haley Fitzgerald
movies.description: After breaking the mysterious “One Wish Willow” to win his crush’s heart, a hopeless romantic finds himself getting exactly what he asked for. He soon discovers that desire comes at a dark, sinister price in this equally haunting and amusing supernatural horror.

movies.title: On Cinematography: Arthur Jafa & Bradford Young
movies.description:
Dash’s debut feature became the first American film directed by an African American woman to receive a general theatrical release in 1991. However, her intricately constructed domestic drama, concerning an enclave living on the islands off the Georgia-South Carolina coast in 1902, would’ve secured a place in film history even if it didn’t represent such a breakthrough, thanks to its extraordinary ensemble cast, sensitive exploration of family tradition and spirituality, and the lush, almost dreamlike cinematography of Arthur Jafa. A film of rare, rhapsodic power and poetry.

“In conjunction with the New Museum’s exhibition I Am Tony, artist Arthur Jafa presents a screening of director Julie Dash’s award-winning Daughters of the Dust (1991), on which Jafa served as cinematographer. The screening will be followed by a conversation between Jafa and acclaimed fellow cinematographer Bradford Young, touching on Jafa’s work in filmmaking and the two artists’ shared engagement with image-making and Black visual culture.” —Thalia Stefaniuk, series co-curator and New Museum Curatorial Assistant
notes: Post-screening conversation with cinematographers Arthur Jafa and Bradford Young on Friday, December 4th

movies.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
movies.cast: Aaron Douglas, Richard Bruce Nugent, Ernest Crichlow, Eubie Blake, Leigh Whipper, Arna Bontemps
movies.description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

movies.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
movies.cast: Aaron Douglas, Richard Bruce Nugent, Ernest Crichlow, Eubie Blake, Leigh Whipper, Arna Bontemps
movies.description: Conceived in 1972 by legendary filmmaker William Greaves and completed 50 years later by his son David, Once Upon a Time in Harlem documents an extraordinary gathering of Harlem Renaissance luminaries for a cocktail party at Duke Ellington’s home. For four hours, this extraordinary group—many of whom had not seen each other in 50 years—reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed, and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape. Shot on 16mm film and newly restored, this landmark film is an invaluable document of an era’s artists and intellectuals as they discuss their lives’ work and legacies, illuminating how culture is preserved and passed along from one generation to another.

movies.title: Once Upon A Time In The West
movies.cast: Claudia Cardinale, Henry Fonda, Jason Robards, Charles Bronson, Gabriele Ferzetti, Paolo Stoppa
movies.description:
"Along with dream team collaborators Leone and Bernardo Bertolucci, Dario Argento is credited with the story for this epic oater, a sort of link between the established Spaghetti Western and the rising giallo, both genres defined by their elaborate and sometimes insanely involved set pieces. Honest Henry Fonda goes bad—very bad—as a railroad baron’s hired gun, facing off against Bronson’s lethal loner Harmonica, in the soaring, musically composed movie that really earns the label of “horse opera.”

“The train delivers characters of mythic proportions to the dusty outpost of Flagstone: a tubercular train daddy, a hero who wields a diegetically unstable harmonica, and a prostitute-turned-newlywed-turned-widow (a magnificent Claudia Cardinale) whose hair remains as sturdy as her resolve, which is to say, perfectly coiffed.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue "

movies.title: Other People's Children
movies.cast: Virginie Efira, Roschdy Zem, Chiara Mastroianni, Callie Ferreira-Goncalves, Yamée Couture, Henri-Noël Tabary
movies.description: “Efira may be as radiant as a Botticelli angel, but it’s her no-nonsense directness that gets to you” writes TIME’s Stephanie Zacharek of the actress’s performance in the comic drama Other People’s Children as Rachel, a childless fortysomething middle-school teacher who, shortly after entering a new relationship with Ali (Roschdy Zem), the father of a four-year-old girl, finds herself increasingly besotted with the kid—and terrified of the risks that come along with such a consuming affection. A poignant, layered, and unerringly compassionate character study, featuring Efira at her most luminous and, at the same time, her most emotionally grounded.

movies.title: Paisan
movies.cast: Carmela Sazio, Robert Van Loon, Dots Johnson
movies.description: The story of Italy’s liberation, told in six episodes, traveling from the first Allied landing in Sicily to the battle of the Po Delta, PAISAN demonstrated that OPEN CITY had been no fluke. Conceived on a vaster scale, with a considerably higher budget, and international distribution from MGM, PAISAN is a national epic that still startles for its immediacy, its technical mastery, its unpredictable rhythms. Scenes of unbearable suspense on the streets of Florence alternate with lighter fare, such as the doctrinal scuffles between Italian monks and American chaplains in Romagna. Stitched together like a newsreel (and skillfully edited to blend in stock footage and suggest off-screen pyrotechnics with creative sound effects), PAISAN became a worldwide sensation, an intellectual action film that pictured recent history with an unprecedented heft and scope. The film became a lodestar for filmmakers from Gillo Pontecorvo to Martin Scorsese, with the latter remarking, “The result... is still startling: it’s like seeing reality itself unfolding before your eyes.”

movies.title: Palestine ‘36
movies.cast: Karim Daoud Anaya, Hiam Abbass, Robert Aramayo, Billy Howle, Dhafer L'Abidine, Yasmine Al Massri
movies.description: In 1936, Yusuf (Karim Daoud Anaya) oscillates between his rural home in Mandatory Palestine and an increasingly restless Jerusalem. Chronicling what would become the largest uprising against Britain’s 30-year colonial project in the region, writer-director Annemarie Jacir (who was last at BAM for a full retrospective in 2018) returns with her most ambitious project to date. Anchored by performances from Hiam Abbass ( Succession ) and Saleh Bakri ( All That’s Left of You ), the only feature to shoot in Palestine in the last two years arrives at a critical time. Advance screening followed by a Q&A with Annemarie Jacir on Mar 20, followed by our run of the film starting Mar 27

movies.title: Panelstory, or How a Housing Development Is Born
movies.description: In a sprawling, labyrinthine prefab housing development in Prague, already occupied but very far from being completed, exasperated tenants struggle with the malfunctioning fixtures inside while outside, they negotiate vast plains of excavated earth that turn to muck and mire with the rain. Depicting one day in the life of this disorderly community, a day rife with aggravations and jerry-rigged solutions, Chytilová’s stinging satire of utopian social engineering and the drab reality that follows its faulty execution drew the ire of Czechoslovak authorities, who held it back from exhibition until 1981. Panelstory remains today a too-little-seen highlight of a brilliant, unruly, and obstinate career.

movies.title: Paper Tiger
movies.cast: Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson, Miles Teller
movies.description: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense drama, two brothers become entangled in a scheme that turns out to be too good to be true. As they try to navigate their way through the dangerous world of the Russian mafia, family bonds begin to fray with life-altering consequences.

movies.title: Paper Tiger
movies.cast: Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson, Miles Teller
movies.description: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense crime thriller, set in 1986 New York, a naïve engineer, Irwin (Miles Teller) accepts a seemingly lucrative business proposition from his brother, Gary (Adam Driver), a former cop. But when Irwin witnesses something he wasn’t meant to see at the Gowanus Canal, the brothers find themselves pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia. As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves.

movies.title: Pearl
movies.cast: Mia Goth, David Corenswet, Tandi Wright, Matthew Sunderland, Emma Jenkins-Purro, Alistair Sewell
movies.description:
The allure of stardom on the big screen proves to be a road to some very dark places for Mia Goth’s titular PEARL in this stylish and gruesome prequel to Ti West’s X. With her husband away at war, Pearl finds herself dreaming of a way to escape from her boring life on the farm. She sees the silver screen as her way to find stardom and the love she so desperately needs, but her overbearing mother and her own dark impulses might hold her back from the fame she craves.

PEARL proves to be a delightfully perverse study on a standout character from writer/director Ti West’s tribute to ‘70s grindhouse, X. Its vibrant, candy-coated veneer plays wonderfully against the depraved desires of the main character bubbling just below the surface. Co-writer/star Mia Goth gives another deliciously unhinged performance as Pearl, a not-quite-innocent farm girl looking for love in all the wrong places. As much a love letter to the Golden Age of Hollywood as it is a demented look at the darkness bubbling just below the surface of rural America, PEARL is colorful, unnerving, and twisted in all the right ways.

movies.title: Pillion
movies.cast: Harry Melling, Alexander Skarsgård, Lesley Sharp, Douglas Hodge, Jake Shears, Mat Hill
movies.description: Timid Colin (Melling) is swept off his feet when Ray (Skarsgård), an enigmatic, impossibly handsome biker, takes him on as his submissive. Subversive, sexy, and surprisingly tender, this unconventional romance between an inquisitive young gay man and his leatherman lover was written by director Harry Lighton, based on the 2020 novel Box Hill by Adam Mars-Jones.

movies.title: Poetry
movies.cast: Yoon Jeong-hee, David Lee, Kim Hee-ra, Ahn Nae-sang, Kim Yong-taek, Park Myung-shin
movies.description: Mija (Yun Jung-hee) has been tasked with raising her troubled teenaged grandson, Jong-wook, while her daughter, Jong-wook’s single mother, works in far-off Busan. When her capacity as a caregiver is threatened by a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s, Mija begins to study poetry composition at the local cultural center—first inspired by beauty in the natural world, then, when Jong-wook is mired in shameful scandal, inspired by new depths of disappointment and pain. Written specifically for Yun, a leading light of ’60s and ’70s South Korean cinema who gives an achingly vulnerable performance, Lee’s poignant, penetrating drama was awarded Best Screenplay at Cannes in 2010.

movies.title: Powwow People
movies.cast: Gina Bluebird, Jacque Clark
movies.description: Powwow People is a vérité-style documentary grounded in the rhythms, relationships, and lived experience of a contemporary Native gathering. Rather than entering as outside observers, the filmmakers organized the powwow itself, inviting dancers, singers, vendors, and community members to participate in the making of this film. Structured around the arc of a single day, the film follows four central figures: Gina Bluebird, who frames the powwow’s shape and guides its setup; Ruben Littlehead, the MC whose presence anchors the present moment; Jamie John, a non-binary dancer imagining the future of these traditions; and Freddie Cozad, a singer and drummer considering the past. The film culminates in a 30-minute unbroken shot of a Northern Traditional dance special, drawing the viewer into the textures, movement, and collective presence of the powwow. It is both a reflection of a beloved community and a gesture toward the continuities of Native life. Q&A with Sky Hopinka following the 7pm screenings on 9/11 and 9/12

movies.title: Primetime
movies.cast: Robert Pattinson, Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, Matthew Maher, Phoebe Bridgers, Victor Brunette
movies.description: Based on the 2007 Esquire article "Tonight on Dateline This Man Will Die”, Oppenheim’s crime thriller follows To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen in his mission to make television history. In more than an encomium to a vigilante, the Some Kind of Heaven director exposes the morbid voyeurism that spurred a genre of television and social media in its wake. With a spine-tingling performance from Pattison, oscillating between the surreal and the all too real, Primetime is an immersive drama, thoughtful expose, and a hallucination rolled into one.

movies.title: Project Hail Mary
movies.cast: Ryan Gosling, James Ortiz, Sandra Hüller, Lionel Boyce, Milana Vayntrub, Ken Leung
movies.description: School-teacher-turned-astronaut Ryland Grace (Gosling) awakes on a space station with no memory of who he is or his mission. As fragments of memory return in bursts, he pieces together his objective to reverse the impact of a space event that hurled Earth into the early stages of an Ice Age, and soon realizes he may not be alone in his quest. Based on the novel by Andy Weir ( The Martian ), Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s adaptation invokes elements of puppetry and practical effects in its conjuring of Grace’s companion, propelling a visual style reminiscent of some of sci-fi’s trailblazing works.

movies.title: Railway Sleepers preceded by A Child Already Knows
movies.description:
Shot over the course of eight years on every line and spur of Thailand’s rail system, its mountains of footage culled down to appear as one 48-hour journey, Chidgasornpongse’s Apichatpong Weerasethakul–produced documentary is both a mesmeric travelogue and a portrait of a country and a people in flux. Screens with A Child Already Knows, in which Sia, employing Mao-era kid’s cartoons and other archival morsels, recounts her family’s flight from Shanghai to Hong Kong.

“The train is unusually vibrant in Chidgasornpongse’s Railway Sleepers, maybe because the windows are open in most of the compartments, which are full of people, music, the occasional grasshopper, and hawkers of fermented pork and Pepsi. By contrast, the parallel journeys in A Child Already Knows—a train ride once taken by Sia’s father, and a parade of 1950s cartoons produced by Shanghai Television—are subdued and tinged with danger.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.title: Raise the Red Lantern
movies.cast: Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles
movies.description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film.

movies.title: Rashomon
movies.cast: Toshirō Mifune, Machiko Kyō, Takashi Shimura, Masayuki Mori, Minoru Chiaki, Kichijirō Ueda
movies.description: A riveting psychological thriller and arthouse sensation starring Toshiro Mifune and Machiko Kyō which investigates the nature of truth and the meaning of justice, widely considered one of the key texts of Japanese—and world—cinema. Four people give different accounts of a man’s murder and the rape of his wife, which Kurosawa presents with striking imagery (those shafts of sunlight streaming through the forest canopy!) and ingenious use of flashbacks. Shooting the celebrated opening of his film—a torrential downfall at Rashomon Gate—Kurosawa and crew mixed water with black ink in the rain tank, creating one of the most sinister soaks in cinema history.

movies.title: Remake
movies.cast: Ross McElwee, Adrian McElwee, Charleen Swansea
movies.description: Setting out to document the process of turning his 1985 nonfiction classic Sherman’s March into a fiction film—while reeling from the death of his 27-year-old son, Adrian—McElwee, in his first film following a 14-year hiatus, gives an enormously tender cinematic eulogy that is also something of a summation of his filmmaking life, describing among many things the tenuous tightrope walk between necessary consideration of practical, commercial concerns and a relentless striving towards honesty and integrity. All of the elements that constitute McElwee’s peculiar genius—the diarist’s warts-and-all self-revelation, the paring away of inessentials in pursuit of universal truths, the off-kilter comic vision—are to be found in spades in the many layers that comprise the extraordinary Remake.

movies.title: Resident Evil
movies.cast: Austin Abrams, Paul Walter Hauser, Kali Reis, Zach Cherry, Johnno Wilson, Shaun W. Loeser
movies.description: From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger ( Weapons , Barbarian ) comes a thrilling reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, a medical courier unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos. Reuniting with Austin Abrams ( Weapons ), Cregger again toes the line between terrifying and ebullient, delivering another entry into the filmography of one of modern horror’s most entertaining auteurs.

movies.title: Rex: A Dinosaur's Story
movies.cast: Yumi Adachi, Shinobu Otake, Tsunehiko Watase, Yuta Yamazaki, Mitsuko Kusabue, Toki Shiozawa
movies.description:
Released just two weeks before Jurassic Park and famed for the off-camera exploits of its director, flamboyant media mogul Kadokawa, Rex: A Dinosaur’s Story managed to do a brisk business at the Japanese box office, tugging heartstrings in telling the story of Chie (Yumi Adachi), a paleontologist’s daughter who discovers a Tyrannosaurus egg with her father (Tsunehiko Watase) and then forms an unlikely friendship with the hatchling that emerges from within. Made with a lavish budget that allowed for contracting the services of special-effects world megastar Carlo Rambaldi (E.T., Possession, Lizard in a Woman’s Skin), Kadokawa’s charmingly bonkers, Christmas-set blockbuster has now been remastered, primed to meet a new generation of international fans.

movies.title: Rome, Open City
movies.director: Roberto Rossellini Co-written by Federico Fellini
movies.cast: Anna Magnani, Aldo Fabrizi
movies.description: Rome, winter 1943: as screeching-tired Gestapo dragnets blanket the “open city,” Resistance leader Marcello Pagliero escapes from his apartment by running across the rooftops (as did co-screenwriter Sergio Amidei in real life), as pregnant widow Anna Magnani prepares for her wedding, parish priest Aldo Fabrizi uses the “frying pan method” to hide the local boys’ bomb brigade’s hardware, and effete Major Harry Feist riffles through his collection of incriminating ID photos—but betrayal, a broad-daylight machine-gunning, a Partisan ambush, blowtorch torture, and death by firing squad loom… Based on actual people and all-too-recent incidents (Magnani’s electrifying final scene was inspired by her enraged pursuit of her boyfriends’s escape by truck); written in a week in Federico Fellini’s kitchen (the only place with heat); shot on a number of the real locations, and cast mainly with non-pros (Fabrizi and second-choice Magnani were already famous, albeit for comedy), OPEN CITY’s documentary look and still hair-raising violence rocked audiences and critics around the world, making Neo-Realism, Rossellini, and Magnani world-famous, sharing the top prize at Cannes, and running twenty-one consecutive months at a single New York cinema.

movies.title: Rose of Nevada
movies.cast: George MacKay, Callum Turner, Francis Magee, Edward Rowe, Rosalind Eleazar, Mary Woodvine
movies.description: Three decades ago, the Rose of Nevada vanished at sea along with its crew. Now, it has returned, convincing desperate locals that the economic devastation their Cornish coastal village has faced might finally be reversed if the ship sails again. Two new crewmen come aboard—Nick (George MacKay), desperate to provide for his young family, and Liam (Callum Turner), eager to escape his past—but when they return to harbor, nothing is as they remember it. Shooting on a 16mm Bolex camera and constructing the sound in post, Mark Jenkin ( Bait ; Enys Men ) writes, directs, edits, and scores a haunting, hallucinatory time-travel mystery that further solidifies him as one of the most distinct, singular artists working in film today.

movies.title: Sad Vacation
movies.cast: Tadanobu Asano, Eri Ishida, Aoi Miyazaki, Yuka Itaya, Katsuo Nakamura, Kengo Kora
movies.description: The third and final film of Aoyama’s “Kitakyushu Saga,” adapted from his own novel, stars Tadanobu Asano as Kenji, a young man still nursing the wounds of an unhappy childhood as he goes through the desultory motions of various odd jobs, who catches sight of an opportunity for closure—or, perhaps, revenge—when one night he recognizes the wife of one of his employers as the mother who’d abandoned him years ago, and conspires to infiltrate their household. A rich, moving human drama of families arbitrarily assigned and chosen, its large ensemble cast handled adroitly, and the proceedings given a striking, somber beauty by prodigiously gifted cinematographer Masaki Tamura.

movies.title: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom
movies.cast: Paolo Bonacelli, Giorgio Cataldi, Uberto Paolo Quintavalle, Aldo Valletti, Caterina Boratto, Elsa De Giorgi
movies.description: Pasolini’s final film remains one of the most shocking ever made. Set during a waning fascist Italy’s dark days amidst World War II, Salò updates the writings of Marquis de Sade to create a repugnant tale of four wealthy libertines who kidnap a group of teenage boys and girls and enact horrific humiliations and violence upon them. A formally and conceptually brilliant, if relentlessly nauseating, portrayal of man’s most debased instincts and the capitalist systems that allow them to thrive. Per Pasolini, “The most sincere thing I could do at that moment was to make a film about a mode of sexuality whose joyousness is a compensation for repression—a phenomenon that was about to come to an end, forever.”
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Scarface
movies.cast: Al Pacino, Steven Bauer, Michelle Pfeiffer, Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio, Robert Loggia, Miriam Colon
movies.description: De Palma’s ultraviolent, ultra-quotable, ultra-colorful, ultra-everything remake of Howard Hawks’s gangster classic is the crass, visually loud flipside to the sober, muted The Godfather, a massively deranged and gleefully disreputable tale of the rise and plunging downfall of a Cuban immigrant turned Miami drug kingpin. Al Pacino throws himself into the title role with the fury of an angry Rottweiler, while Michelle Pfeiffer glowers gorgeously in her breakthrough role as his trophy wife. Featuring cinema’s second most shocking shower scene, a script by Oliver Stone, and a surging soundtrack by Giorgio Moroder, Scarface might just be the film of the Reagan ’80s.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Secrets & Lies
movies.cast: Brenda Blethyn, Marianne Jean-Baptiste, Timothy Spall, Phyllis Logan, Claire Rushbrook, Lee Ross
movies.description: The winner of the Palme d’Or at the 1996 Cannes Film Festival, Leigh’s tender, funny, fearless film has Brenda Blethyn in a career-best performance as Cynthia, a white working-class woman who has a life-changing revelation when she meets Black middle-class optometrist Marianne Jean-Baptiste, who informs Cynthia she’s the little girl Cynthia had given up for adoption 27 years ago, all grown up. Developed, like all of Leigh’s films, through a process of collaborative improvisation, it’s a film of startling spontaneity and uncomfortable, unflinching emotional honesty.

movies.title: Sentimental Value
movies.cast: Renate Reinsve, Stellan Skarsgård, Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas, Elle Fanning, Anders Danielsen Lie, Jesper Christensen
movies.description: Sisters Nora (Reinsve) and Agnes (Lilleaas) reunite with their estranged father, the charismatic Gustav (Skarsgård, in a remarkable performance), a once-renowned director who offers stage actress Nora a role in what he hopes will be his comeback film. When she declines, Gustav casts an up-and-coming young Hollywood star (Fanning) instead, forcing the family to confront long-buried tensions as the striving outsider becomes entangled in their fraught dynamic. With Sentimental Value , Danish-Norwegian auteur Joachim Trier follows his critically acclaimed The Worst Person in the World (2021) with a magnetic comedy-drama about legacy, art, and the performances that bind—and divide—families.

movies.title: Sheep in the Box
movies.cast: Haruka Ayase, Daigo Yamamoto, Kuwaki Rimu, Nana Seino, Kanichiro, Hinata Hiiragi
movies.description: In the near future, grieving couple Otone (Haruka Ayase) and Kensuke (Daigo Yamamoto) bring into their lives an artificial child identical to the son they lost. Japanese writer and director Hirokazu Kore-eda ( Shoplifters , Monster ) shows his signature restraint in this poignant meditation on loss, grief, and healing, screened in its world premiere at the main competition of the 2026 Cannes Film Festival in May. According to Deadline Hollywood Daily , “Kore-eda has taken the stuff of dystopian cyberpunk nightmares and turned it into an elegant, wistful fairytale.”

movies.title: Shutter Island
movies.cast: Leonardo DiCaprio, Mark Ruffalo, Ben Kingsley, Max von Sydow, Michelle Williams, Emily Mortimer
movies.description: An infamous triple filicide has escaped from Ashecliffe Hospital, located on a rugged islet in Boston Harbor that bears a striking resemblance to Arnold Böcklin’s Island of the Dead, and US Marshal Chuck Aule and his new partner (Leonardo DiCaprio and Mark Ruffalo) are on the scene to investigate. Set in the postwar period that gave birth to some of the most anguished of all film noir, Scorsese’s feverish thriller is awash in the psychic trauma of the mid-century, its soundtrack a catalog of jarring modernist classical compiled by collaborator Robbie Robertson and including work by Krzysztof Penderecki, John Cage, and Max Richter, among others, with Robert Richardson’s cinematography suggesting a particularly jaundiced, blighted version of the Technicolor process.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Sibyl
movies.cast: Virginie Efira, Adèle Exarchopoulos, Gaspard Ulliel, Sandra Hüller, Laure Calamy, Niels Schneider
movies.description:
Four years before her Palme d’Or triumph with Anatomy of a Fall, Triet produced this comic thriller starring Virginie Efira in the title role as a psychotherapist who, fed up with her métier, decides to return to writing fiction—and, in the person of one of her patients, a young, tumultuous actress named Margot (Adèle Exarchopoulos), finds an absolutely irresistible source of literary inspiration. Impassioned performances by both leads make Sibyl a compelling study in obsession and self-delusion, with the added inducement of Anatomy star Sandra Hüller’s appearance in a side-splitting role as the director of a film-within-the-film.

Distirbutor: Music Box Films

movies.title: Silent Friend
movies.cast: Tony Leung Chiu-wai, Luna Wedler, Enzo Brumm, Sylvester Groth, Martin Wuttke, Johannes Hegemann
movies.description: From visionary Hungarian director Ildikó Enyedi, Silent Friend follows three loosely interconnected vignettes revolving around a gingko tree over the course of a century. Taking place in 1908, 1972, and 2020, each moment captures people—like Dr. Wong (played by legendary Hong Kong actor Tony Leung Chiu-wai) and Alice (Léa Seydoux)—in often clumsy but sincere attempts to free themselves from life’s monotony by creating harmony with plants and the garden world the tree inhabits.

movies.title: Sirât
movies.cast: Sergi López, Bruno Núñez, Stefania Gadda, Joshua Liam Henderson, Richard Bellamy, Tonin Janvier
movies.description: Searching for his missing daughter, middle-aged Luis (Sergi López) travels with his son Esteban (Bruno Núñez Arjona) to a rave in the mountains of Morocco. Bound for a mythic party deep in the desert as an armed conflict erupts with a neighboring nation, Luis, Esteban, and a small band of ravers confront perilous conditions—a journey evoking the Arabic word sirât , in Islam a reference to the razor-thin bridge all must cross on the Day of Judgment, when only the righteous survive. Awash in penetrating light and pulsating sound, Sirāt shared the Jury Prize at this year’s Cannes Film Festival. 2026 Academy Award nominee, Best International Feature Film, Best Sound

movies.title: Six Suspects
movies.cast: Cheung Ching-Ching, Wai Wang, Chang Pan-Yang, Chen Yun-ching, Hsia Chin-Hsin, Kai Yin
movies.description:
Keeping an eye on his ex-lover (Zhang Qingqing), the personal assistant to the chairman of a large steel company, private eye Kong-hui (Wu Dongru) picks up ample fodder to blackmail the folks in the front office—and so, when Kong-hui is found murdered, detective Yi Yuan won’t lack for suspects… though each trail he follows seems to lead to a dead end. A jazzy, ingeniously plotted urban whodunnit set in a Taipei in the first flush of postwar prosperity, Six Suspects was not granted a theatrical release on completion but has now been revealed, thanks to restoration work by the Taiwan Film Institute, as a darkly glittering gem of the mid-century Taiyupian.

© 1965 Giok Hong Film Company / 2017 Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute

2K digital restorations courtesy of Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute

movies.title: Skyfly Superman
movies.cast: Chih-Bang Kuei, Te-Nan Lai
movies.description:
The third and final Dragon Superman adventure opens with a pack of masked baddies kidnapping two children in a Japanese garden, a high-kicking, bone-cracking donnybrook, and some sinister plotting involving a “mummy drug” and “invisibility experiments”… and that’s just the first five minutes! The gonzo action rarely lets up from then on, as Kobayashi and Shao go out both guns blazing, throwing in hair’s breadth escapes, buried treasure, jangly surf guitar, a fatal silly string cannon, plenty of 20-against-one brawls, gun-to-the-temple child endangerment, shameless sentimentality, a cracking motorboat chase, and further bumbling comic relief from La Te-nan’s Mr. Mischief. Pop cinema at its buoyant best, and a fitting goodbye to San Lin and the gang.

© 1968 Shin Gor Production Company / 2024 Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute

2K digital restorations courtesy of Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute

movies.title: Somewhere in the Night
movies.cast: John Hodiak, Nancy Guild, Lloyd Nolan, Richard Conte, Josephine Hutchinson, Fritz Kortner
movies.description: Mankiewicz’s sophomore effort as director was this sinisterly atmospheric, baroquely plotted, deliriously disorienting “nervous nightmare” [The Village Voice] starring John Hodiak as an amnesiac ex-Marine who returns to his native Los Angeles to trawl its nightclubs, sanitariums, and docks in search of clues to his identity and traces of a mysterious stranger by the name of “Larry Cravat.” It’s a mission that puts him in close contact with the criminal underworld and a rogue’s gallery of unusual characters (Richard Conte, Josephine Hutchinson, and Fritz Kortner are on-hand in piquant supporting parts) while tying him up in a hunt for Nazi-plundered treasure.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Song Sung Blue
movies.cast: Hugh Jackman, Kate Hudson, Michael Imperioli, Fisher Stevens, Jim Belushi, Ella Anderson
movies.description: Written and directed by Craig Brewer ( Hustle & Flow , Dolemite Is My Name ), Song Sung Blue is based on a 2009 documentary of the same name. Recounting the true story of Mike and Claire Sardina (Jackman and Hudson), two down-on-their-luck musicians who form a joyous Neil Diamond tribute band, Lightning & Thunder, Song Sung Blue suggests it's never too late to find love and follow your dreams—and that singing a pop hit like its originator can allow an earnest belter to tap into something magical. “Brewer navigates this terrain like a jukebox Jonathan Demme,” Variety proclaims.

movies.title: Soul Patrol
movies.cast: Danielle Lyn, Michael Oloyede, Deion Smith, Okea Eme-Akwari, Elijah Richardson, Myles Simms-Aur
movies.description:
SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

Previously screened as part of our DOC NYC SELECTS series

movies.title: Spellbound
movies.cast: Ingrid Bergman, Gregory Peck, Michael Chekhov, Leo G. Carroll, Rhonda Fleming, John Emery
movies.description: Hitchcock goes in for psychoanalysis in this singular thriller, made under the influence of Sigmund Freud and Salvador Dalí, the latter of whom designed the dazzling dream sequence. Analyst Ingrid Bergman falls for amnesiac patient Gregory Peck—but is there a murderer’s heart lurking beneath that dapper exterior? The delirium only grows more intense and Miklós Rózsa’s theremin-inflected score becomes more urgent as her doubts grow and she draws closer to the truth.
notes: Please note: Spellbound begins with an approximately four-minute musical overture played over a black screen, recreating its original 1945 theatrical presentation. This is an intentional part of the film, not a technical issue.

movies.title: Stalker
movies.cast: Alisa Freyndlikh, Aleksandr Kaydanovskiy, Anatoliy Solonitsyn, Mykola Hrynko, Natalya Abramova, Faime Jurno
movies.description: Tarkovsky’s stunning, haunted sepia-toned sci-fi masterpiece follows a scientist and a writer who, living in a broken-down totalitarian dystopia, recruit the help of a “Stalker”—a kind of post-apocalyptic Sherpa—to guide them on a voyage of self-discovery, passing through the bleak, otherworldly Zone in hopes of finding therein a haven that will fulfill their secret desires. An enigmatic, austere, and utterly immersive experience that combines religious allegory and political prophesy, and has kept cinephiles debating its meaning for some 50 years.

movies.title: Still Life + Train-Trains #2: A Bypass
movies.description:
A program of two formally adventurous trainspotting films from the Middle East. Stephan’s memory piece Train-Trains #2: Bypass follows the weed-choked rails of a former train line, an extension of the Orient Express that once linked Lebanon to Palestine, which lives on in the memories of those who reside near its long-abandoned stations; Saless’s Still Life, a key film of the early Iranian New Wave and winner of the Silver Bear at the 24th Berlin International Film Festival, observes the daily lives of a longtime crossing guard (Zadour Bonyadi) at a remote train station and his wife, whose well-worn routine will be upended by an unexpected development.

“Still Life plays like a silent film that happens to have sound. Elderly crossing guard Mohamad is almost completely wordless, even before he receives the news that changes everything. In Train-Trains #2: A Bypass, the people along the abandoned Haifa-Beirut-Tripoli Line are more voluble, but they share a similar grief over a world that has since passed them by.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

Train-Trains #2: A Bypass (Rania Stephan, 2017, 30 mins)

Still Life (Sohrab Shahid Saless, 1974, 93 mins)
