movies.title: Sunshine Express
movies.cast: Babak Karimi, Sam Nakhai, Mohammad Aghebati, Sajad Hamidian, Amirhossein Hosseini, Shayesteh Sajadi
movies.description: Each participant is assigned a unique role they must maintain throughout the show. If they succeed in carrying out their assignment, they earn the chance to journey to Hermia, a mythical land of dreams. But as the show unfolds, hidden truths and conflicts emerge—is the mission as straightforward as it seems? Followed by a Q&A with filmmaker Paxton Winters and Steve Macfarlane (MoMA Film), in conversation with Lila Nazemian (ArteEast)
notes: Co-presented by ArteEast In this Iranian drama from Amirali Navaee, a group of strangers signs up to board a staged train for a reality show.
Presented by ArteEast

movies.title: Suspiria
movies.cast: Jessica Harper, Stefania Casini, Flavio Bucci, Miguel Bosé, Barbara Magnolfi, Susanna Javicoli
movies.description:
A fairy tale construction at once grim and florid, Argento’s best-known film finds Jessica Harper’s American ballet dancer arriving at an exclusive academy in Germany where she discovers a dark past and occult forces at work in the present. With some of Argento’s most perversely ingenious set pieces, a plum part for former Fritz Lang muse Joan Bennett, and a spine-tingling theme by Goblin that will haunt you to the grave.

Presented in the English-language version

movies.title: Suzhou River
movies.description: Taking its name from the polluted river that flows through Shanghai, director Lou’s hometown, the brooding Suzhou River uses the singular first-person perspective of its unseen videographer-narrator to explore the grubby underbelly of the city, observing the story of an unsuspecting motorcycle courier who finds himself snared in a kidnapping plot and murder rap. A seductive, intricately structured stylistic coup from the Sixth Generation filmmaker, drawing on influences from film noir to Vertigo (1958) while developing its own idiosyncratic and haunting visual vocabulary.

movies.title: Tainted Horseplay
movies.cast: Tomáš Hanák, Milan Šteindler, David Vávra, Ivana Kuntová, Tereza Kučerová, Renata Becerrová
movies.description: Three thirtysomething friends united by their sybaritic appetites for booze, sexual shenanigans, and other assorted hijinks—František (David Vávra) a restaurateur; Milan (Milan Šteindler), a veterinarian; and Pepe (Tomáš Hanák), an auditor—lead a life of feckless, reckless promiscuity… until a HIV-positive diagnosis hits the group like a nailbomb, rending old allegiances asunder and lowering a paranoiac pall over the trio. A stinging rebuke to boomer narcissism and the overindulgence of eternally extended adolescence, phenomena evidently as epidemic in the soon-to-fall Soviet territories as in Manhattan, London, or the 16th arrondissement, cast with members of Prague’s Sklep theater group, who bring to the proceedings a snarky vivacity.

movies.title: Tangles
movies.cast: Bryan Cranston, Seth Rogen, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Pamela Adlon, Sarah Silverman, Beanie Feldstein, Ab
movies.description:
Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Sarah Silverman, Abbi Jacobson, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston voice a family struggling with their mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis in this deeply moving, animated adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s acclaimed graphic novel.

movies.title: Taxi Driver
movies.cast: Robert De Niro, Jodie Foster, Cybill Shepherd, Harvey Keitel, Peter Boyle, Leonard Harris
movies.description: “Suck on this!” A pure distillation of needling isolation, inadequacy, and anguish, all roiling in the tortured gut of Robert De Niro’s insomniac cabbie Travis Bickle, who cruises all night through a stygian, steam-choked Manhattan, nursing his fears and hatreds. A defining picture of New York City in 1976, and a movie that is wrenched straight from the unquiet psyche of its screenwriter, exorcizing his personal demons.

movies.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
movies.cast: Hannah Einbinder, Gillian Anderson, Amanda Fix, Arthur Conti, Eva Victor, Zach Cherry
movies.description: Hired to inject fresh blood into the threadbare Camp Miasma slasher-film franchise, ambitious young queer director Kris (Hannah Einbinder, of Hacks ) sets out to cast Billy Presley (Gillian Anderson), the now reclusive actress who played the “final girl” in the film that launched the series. But when the two begin to work together, the connection sparks desire, fear, and delirium. Written and directed by Jane Schoenbrun ( We’re All Going to the World's Fair , I Saw the TV Glow ), Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma opened the Un Certain Regard section at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Queer Palm. According to Time magazine, “Schoenbrun’s delirious third film is their most accomplished, most persuasive and most playful movie yet.” Q&A following the Aug 16, 3pm show with Jane Schoenbrun

movies.title: That Day, On The Beach
movies.cast: Sylvia Chang, Terry Hu, Hsu Ming, David Mao, Hsiao Hou Tao, Lee Lieh
movies.description:
The little-screened debut feature by Yang, prophet of and proselytizer for the Taiwanese New Wave, features Sylvia Chang and Terry Hu as two female friends, an unhappily married housewife and a concert pianist, brought together after a 13-year separation: their process of catching up illustrated through an innovative, ingeniously layered flashback structure which shows the director’s air for formal experimentation already fully in operation. Shot by renegade cinematographer Christopher Doyle, also on his first feature, Yang’s gorgeous and deeply felt memory piece/mystery uses its intricate structure to explore, among other things, “the ways in which patriarchal authority stunts young people’s lives.” US theatrical premiere of new 2K restoration.

An American Genre Film Archive (AGFA) release

movies.title: The Aristocats
movies.cast: Phil Harris, Eva Gabor, Sterling Holloway, Scatman Crothers, Paul Winchell, Lord Tim Hudson
movies.description: A big-screen outing for this flight of feline fun from the Disney vaults, the last animated feature to be signed off on by Walt himself is a purr-fect Parisian period piece featuring a family of nose-in-the-air cats who, after being kidnapped away from the accustomed baronial splendor of their home, have to rely on the streetwise wiles of alley cat O’Malley to keep them safe. Featuring animation supremely attentive to the syntax of kitty motion and the vocal talents of Eva Gabor and Scatman Crothers who gets to lead on the boppin' classic “Everybody Wants to Be a Cat.”

movies.title: The Ascent
movies.cast: Boris Plotnikov, Vladimir Gostyukhin, Anatoliy Solonitsyn, Lyudmila Polyakova, Viktoriya Goldentul, Sergei Yakovlev
movies.description: The bloodthirsty and seemingly unstoppable Nazi war machine is on the march towards Moscow in Shepitko’s wrenching, snow-swept World War II drama, which begins with two Soviet peasant soldiers foraging for food in a Belarusian village and proceeds to tell an emotional, lyrical tale of loyalty and betrayal, partisanship and collaboration, and, ultimately, the possibility of transcendent redemption. Shepitko’s final feature, frequently cited as among the greatest of Soviet films, won the Golden Bear at the 1977 Berlin Film Festival, just two years before its director’s tragic death in a car accident at age 41.

movies.title: The Best Secret Agent
movies.cast: Hung Pai, Hung Li
movies.description:
The movie that lit the fuse on an explosion of espionage thrillers in Taiwan, Zhang’s box-office phenomenon is a twisty tale of star-crossed love and sabotage during the years of the Sino-Japanese war, featuring Bai Hong as a refugee from the marauding Japanese who land in Shanghai, Ke Junxiong as the man she falls for, and Tian Qing as the collaborationist stooge of the puppet Manchukuo state that she reluctantly marries—his schemes constantly undermined by the actions of a mysterious “Secret Agent Heaven No. 1.” A spry, stylish, sexy cloak-and-dagger melodrama, based on a homonymous 1945 film from the Mainland, with Hong a delight as she dons several walk-in closets’ worth of disguises.

© 1964 Wan Shou Film Company / 2015 Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute.

2K digital restorations courtesy of Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute

movies.title: The Cat in the Hat
movies.cast: Bill Hader, Xochitl Gomez, Tiago Martinez, Quinta Brunson, America Ferrera, Matt Berry
movies.description: In the wonderfully whimsical tradition of Dr. Seuss, The Cat in the Hat comes to the big screen in his animated theatrical feature film debut, an all-new, epic adventure with an edge, where mischief, magic and mayhem reign supreme. Doing what he does best, the Cat–voiced by Bill Hader–spreads joy to kids in his hilarious, signature and singularly irreverent way, transporting them and audiences on a fantastical journey through a world they’ve never seen before. In the film, our hero takes on his toughest assignment yet for the I.I.I.I. (Institute for the Institution of Imagination and Inspiration, LLC): to cheer Gabby and Sebastian, a pair of siblings struggling with their move to a new town. Known for taking things too far, this could be this agent of chaos’s last chance to prove himself… or lose his magical hat!

movies.title: The Cat in the Hat
movies.cast: Bill Hader, Xochitl Gomez, Tiago Martinez, Quinta Brunson, America Ferrera, Matt Berry
movies.description: Dr. Seuss’s iconic Cat in the Hat gets its first animated big-screen adventure, with Bill Hader voicing the striped-hat troublemaker on a mission to cheer up siblings Gabby and Sebastian after a move to a new town. Fantastical worlds, magical mayhem, and Matt Berry voicing a goldfish – this movie has everyTHING. And if you’re still recovering from the emotional trauma of the 2003 live-action Mike Myers version, consider this your chance to make some new memories.

movies.title: The Celebration
movies.description: The opening salvo in Dogme 95’s all-out assault on cinematic artifice, revolutionary in its emancipated use of the Sony DCR-PC7 Handycam, Vinterberg’s scorched earth melodrama/farce takes place during a gathering of the extended Hansen clan at a family-run hotel to mark the 60th birthday of solid burgher patriarch Helge (Henning Moritzen)—an event that takes a turn for the chaotic when Helge’s eldest son, Christian (Ulrich Thomsen), accuses his father of molesting both himself and his recently deceased twin sister during a dinner table toast. Abrasive, volatile, savagely funny, and endlessly inventive, one can scarcely feel indifferent towards such a blood-on-the-walls affair as this.

movies.title: The Christophers
movies.cast: Michaela Coel, Ian McKellen, Jessica Gunning, James Corden, Ferdy Roberts, Tilly Botsford
movies.description: The estranged children (Corden, Gunning) of a beloved dormant artist (McKellen) hire Lori (Coel), an art restorer and former forger, to pose as a prospective assistant in an effort to access some unfinished canvases they believe to be instrumental to conjuring a worthwhile inheritance. As always, Steven Soderbergh is a master of embedding the formal and technical flourishes of the arthouse inside seemingly populist fare, as exemplified in his Ocean ’s trilogy and last year’s Black Bag (2025). In turns that Deadline deemed an "unusually emotional film for Soderbergh,” McKellen’s and Coel’s tête-à-tête makes for a quintessentially funny and engrossing addition to the director’s oeuvre.

movies.title: The Cook, The Thief, His Wife, & Her Lover
movies.cast: Michael Gambon, Richard Bohringer, Helen Mirren, Alan Howard, Tim Roth, Ciarán Hinds
movies.description:
Peter Greenaway's 1989 magnum opus THE COOK, THE THIEF, HIS WIFE & HER LOVER is neo-noir for the hungry, devious soul. Released at a time when crime cinema was growing increasingly perverse with the likes of ANGEL HEART (1987), BLUE VELVET (1986), and BODY DOUBLE (1984), Greenaway's film out-shocks the buch by intertwining two of human nature's favorite pastimes: food and sex. Like Marco Ferreri's LA GRAND BOUFFE (1973) and Paul Bartel's EATING RAOUL (1982) before it, food and sex quickly turn into a recipe for something decidedly more sinister and... cannibalistic. Shocking audiences at the time of its release, time has not tamed Greenaway's film at all, and you'll never look at Helen Mirren or Michael Gambon the same way again. (Justin LaLiberty)

DCP courtesy of Universal Pictures

movies.title: The Currents
movies.cast: Isabel Aimé González Sola, Esteban Bigliardi, Claudia Sánchez, Ernestina Gatti, Jazmín Carballo, Sara Bessio
movies.description: Lina (Isabel Aimé González Sola), an accomplished Argentine artist and designer, is in Switzerland to receive an award when she jumps from a bridge into the icy waters below. As she later confesses to a friend, she experienced a moment of deep peace until the thought of her young daughter drew her back to life. But the incident leaves her with a paralyzing fear of water and a growing sense of isolation that threatens both her career and her personal life. Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Milagros Mumenthaler ( Back to Stay ), The Currents is a quietly gripping portrait of a woman on the verge of unraveling.

movies.title: The Debut
movies.cast: Julianne Moore, Paul Giamatti, Halle Bailey, Jesse Eisenberg, Bernadette Peters, Craig Bierko
movies.description: When Mona Friedman lands a small part in a community theater production, she transforms from a shy housewife into a zealous method actor who's willing to do anything to protect the artistic integrity of her role -- even if it means waging war against the show's domineering director.

movies.title: The Devils
movies.cast: Vanessa Redgrave, Oliver Reed
movies.description:
New 4K Restoration!

An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell.

Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.
notes: Presented in 35mm
Screening on 35mm Sat, Nov 7 at 7:25!

movies.title: The Drama
movies.cast: Zendaya, Robert Pattinson, Alana Haim, Mamoudou Athie, Hailey Benton Gates, Sydney Lemmon
movies.description: Days before they’re set to tie the knot, a happily engaged couple (Zendaya, Pattinson) is put to the test when one partner discovers some shocking truths about the other. In Kristoffer Borgli’s ( Dream Scenario ) highly-anticipated pairing of two of contemporary cinema’s brightest stars, Zendaya and Pattinson (set to appear onscreen together again this year in Dune: Part Three ) deliver a wedding movie for the ages.

movies.title: The Elephant Man
movies.cast: Anthony Hopkins, John Hurt, Anne Bancroft, John Gielgud, Wendy Hiller, Freddie Jones
movies.description: New 4K Restoration Before Blue Velvet cemented Lynch as one of the century’s preeminent directors, he released The Elephant Man , an atmospheric historical drama and important moment in understanding the development of the auteur’s signature style. Set in Victorian England, the black-and-white film follows London surgeon Frederick Treves (Anthony Hopkins) and his developing friendship with freak-show performer John Merrick (John Hurt), challenging perceptions around disability and human dignity. With a stellar supporting cast that includes Anne Bancroft, John Gielgud, and Wendy Hiller, Lynch’s surreal take on a biopic was nominated for eight Academy Awards, cementing his reputation as one of American cinema’s most visionary talents.

movies.title: The Empty Man
movies.cast: James Badge Dale, Marin Ireland, Sasha Frolova, Samantha Logan, Evan Jonigkeit, Virginia Kull
movies.description:
One of the most original and visually striking horror feature debuts in recent memory—thanks in no small part to the air of ambient dread sustained by Anastas Michos’s photography—The Empty Man, a burgeoning cult phenomenon, follows burned-out ex-detective James Badge Dale on an investigation into the disappearance of a friend’s teenaged daughter that leads him into a hidden world of eerie idolatry, eldritch evil, and psyche-shattering terror.

“The Empty Man is about what moves in when belief moves out. People get so hungry for meaning that they’ll take any signal from any source. In 2020, it was a horror film. In 2026, it’s the evening news.” —Anastas Michos, ASC
notes: Q&A with cinematographer Anastas Michos on Sunday, December 13th

movies.title: The General
movies.cast: Buster Keaton, Marion Mack, Glen Cavender, Jim Farley, Frederick Vroom, Frank Barnes
movies.description:
Keaton’s engineer Johnnie Gray is another of his big-hearted little guys, rejected by the Confederate Army, though when the Union tries to make off with his train, runt Johnnie shows his mettle in the most incredible sustained chase sequence in all of silent comedy. Wall-to-wall with elaborate, antic gags, though also marked by a quiet sense of pastoral beauty that had previously been given little outlet.

“While shooting The General, the locals and crew played baseball together every Sunday. Keaton was apparently very good. It’s not surprising that such a virtuosic physical performer, who did all of his own stunts, would be an excellent athlete. But his eyes seem to tell a different story. To me they always appear a bit hapless and sad, even when his characters persevere.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue
notes: Introduction by series curator Genevieve Yue on Sunday, November 8th

movies.cast: John Wilson, Michael Imperioli, Jack Macco, Nathan Fielder, Timothée Chalamet, Josh Safdie
movies.description:
Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

movies.title: The Holy Mountain
movies.cast: Alejandro Jodorowsky, Horacio Salinas, Zamira Saunders
movies.description:
The follow-up to his Midnight Movie sensation El Topo , writer-director Alejandro Jodorowsky’s THE HOLY MOUNTAIN caused a scandal at the 1973 Cannes Film Festival with its flood of sacrilegious imagery, existential symbolism and outrageous violence. Once again, Jodorowsky plays the allegorically named lead, “The Alchemist,” who assembles a group of people from all walks of life and renames them for the planets in the solar system. Putting his recruits through strange mystical rites and divesting them of their worldly baggage, he leads them on a trip to Lotus Island to ascend the Holy Mountain and displace the immortal gods who secretly rule the universe. This gorgeous new digital restoration, overseen by the filmmaker himself, returns Jodorowsky’s most visually extravagant film to all its trippy splendor.

Screening as part of Late Night Favorites: Fall 2026

movies.title: The Host
movies.cast: Song Kang-ho, Byun Hee-bong, Park Hae-il, Bae Doona, Ko A-sung
movies.description:
When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic .

“A thing of beauty, the perfect mixture of the silly and the grave.” – The New Yorker
notes: Fri Nov 20 – Thu Nov 26: All 6:30pm shows (6:20pm on Mon Nov 23) are followed by a pre-recorded Q&A with director Bong Joon Ho, moderated by Edgar Wright!

movies.title: The Host
movies.cast: Kärin Strom, Laurie Powers Going
movies.description: 20 years after becoming a worldwide sensation, Bong Joon Ho’s acclaimed creature-feature THE HOST returns to theaters in a stunning new 4K restoration, featuring an exclusive conversation with the Oscar®-winning filmmaker.

movies.title: The Housemaid
movies.cast: Lee Eun-shim, Kim Jin-kyu, Ju Jeung-nyeo, Um Aing-ran, Go Seon-ae, Gang Seok-je
movies.description: Cited by Bong Joon-ho as an inspiration on his Parasite and widely regarded by South Korean cinephiles and scholars as one of the country’s greatest films, The Housemaid can now be discovered by the rest of the world thanks to a restoration by the Korean Film Archive and Martin Scorsese’s World Cinema Project. The routine domestic life of a middle-class family is turned upside-down after a young woman (Lee Eun-shim) joins the household to help with the chores—though what she does instead is turn the house into a boiling cauldron of lust. A mélange of melodrama, morality tale, noir thriller, and horror film that, in Kim’s handling, come together to exercise a vice-like grip.

movies.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
movies.cast: Joseph Zada, Jennifer Lawrence, Mckenna Grace, Ralph Fiennes, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin, Maya Hawke, Glenn Close, Lili Taylor
movies.description: Before Katniss Everdeen volunteered as tribute, a teenage Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada, East of Eden ) had his own date with destiny in Panem’s deadliest televised sporting event. This prequel to THE HUNGER GAMES sends Haymitch into the 50th annual Games, aka the Second Quarter Quell, where twice the tributes means twice the bloodshed. With President Snow (Ralph Fiennes) calling the shots, Haymitch joins forces with fellow tributes to fight back. Turns out humanity just can't get enough of sadistic game shows, and we have to admit, they look great on the big screen.

movies.title: The Inugami Family
movies.cast: Koji Ishizaka, Yoko Shimada, Teruhiko Aoi, Mieko Takamine, Mitsuko Kusabue, Miki Sanjō
movies.description: Based on Seishi Yokomizo’s 1951 bestseller The Inugami Curse, adapted before and after Ichikawa’s 1976 blockbuster, but arguably never bettered—mystery/melodrama The Inagami Family takes place in the fallout following the death of the wealthy patriarch of the eponymous clan, whose members start to drop off like flies in the most unnatural of ways, leaving detective Kosuke Kindaichi (Kōji Ishizaka, who would play the same role for Ichikawa in four more Kindaichi films) on a race to ferret out a culprit before the reading of the will. Simmering resentments, a veritable army of closeted skeletons, and more twists than a super-coaster make this a must-see for the whodunnit addict.

movies.title: The Invite
movies.cast: Olivia Wilde, Seth Rogen, Penélope Cruz, Edward Norton
movies.description: Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela’s (Olivia Wilde) marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors (Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton) for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down? A remake of the 2020 Spanish film The People Upstairs , Olivia Wilde’s star-studded take on a dinner party dramedy (written by Will McCormack and Rashida Jones) is a timely portrait of a modern marriage, teeming with wit, belly laughs, and a surprising poignancy.

movies.title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
movies.cast: Colin Farrell, Nicole Kidman, Barry Keoghan, Raffey Cassidy, Sunny Suljic, Bill Camp
movies.description: The year before enjoying enormous popular success with The Favourite, Lanthimos rolled out perhaps his most difficult and disquieting film to date, a Greek tragedy transplanted to the American suburbs starring Colin Farrell as Steven Murphy, a cardiothoracic surgeon who opens his home in an unguarded moment to a fatherless 16-year-old (Barry Keoghan)… and, as it happens, to a terrible retribution that threatens Murphy’s wife (Nicole Kidman), teenaged daughter, and adolescent son. “A typically arch dramatic conundrum, laced with Lanthimos’s trademark off-kilter artifice and deadpan humour… An increasingly sickening hunger game driven by an inflexible moral imperative.” —The Observer

movies.title: The Manchurian Candidate
movies.cast: Frank Sinatra, Laurence Harvey, Angela Lansbury, Janet Leigh, James Gregory, Henry Silva
movies.description: The 1960 U-2 incident, and rumors of the brainwashing of downed Air Force pilot Francis Gary Powers by Soviet captors, were fresh in the imagination when Frankenheimer’s taut political suspenser hit screens, featuring Laurence Harvey as Raymond Shaw, a Korean War vet returned stateside with decorations after going MIA—unbeknownst to himself and the wider world, a sleeper agent programmed to do the bidding of the Commies—and Frank Sinatra the Army Intelligence officer who suspects all might not be right with Sgt. Shaw. “One of the strangest and most mercurial movies ever made in Hollywood… Conceivably the only commercial American film that deserves to be linked with the French New Wave, full of visual and verbal wit that recalls Orson Welles… A powerful experience, alternately corrosive with dark parodic humor, suspenseful, moving, and terrifying.” —Jonathan Rosenbaum, The Chicago Reader

movies.title: The Matrix Revolutions
movies.cast: Keanu Reeves, Laurence Fishburne, Carrie-Anne Moss, Hugo Weaving, Jada Pinkett Smith, Mary Alice
movies.description: A digital downpour of Matrix code drenches the final showdown between Neo (Keanu Reeves) and Agent Smith (Hugo Weaving) in but one show-stopping moment in the third entry of the Wachowskis’ fin-de-millenium-defining series, which brings back Laurence Fishburne’s Morpheus, Carrie-Anne Moss’s Trinity, Jada Pinkett Smith’s Niobe, and other familiar-the-world-over faces for one more raucous round of raging against the machine. “An exercise in spectacular mayhem… There’s a hint of Burroughsian grandeur to [it’s] cyborg-against-cyborg ballet mécanique… BX cable squid spaghetti static electricity! Machine-gun machine-hell Armageddon!! Infernal orange and blue orgone-light tentacle vortex!!!” —J. Hoberman, The Village Voice

movies.title: The Odyssey
movies.cast: Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Himesh Patel, John Leguizamo
movies.description: Shooting around the globe using 70mm IMAX film cameras, director Christopher Nolan ( Oppenheimer , Tenet , Inception ) transforms Homer’s ancient Greek epic into a luxuriously cast summer blockbuster inspired by Ray Harryhausen’s 1970s sword-and-sandal adventures and informed by Emily Wilson’s admirably savvy 2017 English translation of the original poem. The Odyssey recounts the tale of Ithacan king Odysseus (Matt Damon), confronted by literal monsters and menaces as he returns with his soldiers from the Trojan War, while at home his wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Tom Holland) send off scheming suitors like Antinous (Robert Pattinson).

movies.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
movies.cast: John Turturro, Giancarlo Esposito, Will Price, Tatiana Maslany, Victoria Moroles, Steve Buscemi
movies.description: Harry Lehman (John Turturro) is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily canceled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

movies.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
movies.cast: John Turturro, Giancarlo Esposito, Will Price, Tatiana Maslany, Victoria Moroles, Steve Buscemi, and Jamie Lee Curtis
movies.description:
Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun.

THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

movies.title: The Piano
movies.cast: Holly Hunter, Harvey Keitel, Sam Neill, Anna Paquin, Cliff Curtis, Kerry Walker
movies.description: Gale-force winds and interminable lashing rain render colonial New Zealand a nigh uninhabitable mire in Campion’s elemental Antipodean Gothic romance, in which mute Scotswoman Ada and her young daughter (Holly Hunter, Anna Paquin) arrive under the Southern Cross so that Ada can be wed to stiff-backed settler Alisdair Stewart (Sam Neill)—an arranged union that quickly sours when Stewart separates Ada from her lone means of expression, her piano, and Ada drifts into an increasingly compromising and sexualized relationship with neighbor George Baines (Harvey Keitel), an ex-sailor and the instrument’s new owner. With its Palme d’Or win at Cannes, Campion became the first female director to receive that honor—and a shower of Academy Awards still lay ahead.

movies.title: The Power of Kangwon Province
movies.cast: Baek Jong-hak, Oh Youn-hong, Kim Yu-seok, Chun Jae-hyun, Park Hyun-young, Im Sun-young
movies.description: A film of narrowly missed encounters, effortlessly tossed-off beauty, lightly worn narrative complexity, and (of course) slurry, sloppy binge drinking, Hong’s bracingly brilliant sophomore feature, which premiered in Cannes’s Un Certain Regard section, follows the separate trajectories of a man and a woman (Baek Jong-hak and Oh Yoon-hong) traveling through South Korea’s ruggedly mountainous east, the two drifters gradually revealed, in their individual encounters, to be tied together by a shared past. “Etched with precision and conveying a world of feeling… One of the best films you can see this year… [Hong is] a master of ellipsis.” —Manohla Dargis, The New York Times

movies.title: The Price of Forgiveness
movies.description:
In collaboration with Brooklyn-based Jollof Films, co-founded by Senegalese artists Assane Sy and Ahmad Cissé, and their pan-African cinema club, we present a screening of Mansour Sora Wade’s 2001 The Price of Forgiveness, an atmospheric and dexterously directed film fable that lays its scene in a Senegalese fishing village where the locals struggle to lift an all-encompassing fog that’s keeping their boats on shore, and two childhood friends vie for the attentions of the same woman.

“We are excited to share Wade’s The Price of Forgiveness with our audience. The film’s poetic approach to storytelling and its deep connection to Senegalese culture make it an essential viewing experience, and we are honored to bring this work to Metrograph.” —Assane Sy and Ahmad Cissé, Jollof Films curators
notes: Post-screening discussion with Jollof Films on Saturday, December 12th
Post-screening discussion with Jollof Films on Saturday, December 12th/p>

movies.title: The Rescuers
movies.cast: Bob Newhart, Eva Gabor, Geraldine Page, Joe Flynn, Jeanette Nolan, Pat Buttram
movies.description: Geraldine Page, Bob Newhart, and Eva Gabor are among the vocal talent assembled for Disney’s vivacious adaptation of Margery Sharp’s beloved book series about the Rescue Aid Society, a group of dauntless mice who travel the world to lend aid to kidnapping victims. Here R.A.S. representatives Miss Bianca (Gabor) and Bernard (Newhart) rush to Devil’s Bayou, Louisiana, where they liberate a little girl named Penny from the clutches of the nefarious Madame Medusa (Page) and her trained crocodiles, Brutus and Nero, while at the same time tasked with keeping a precious gemstone safe from the villainess. A spirited, swashbuckling adventure, made with brio by Disney’s crack animation team led by rising star Don Bluth.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: The Sacrifice
movies.cast: Erland Josephson, Susan Fleetwood, Allan Edwall, Guðrún Gísladóttir, Sven Wollter, Valérie Mairesse
movies.description: Made when Tarkovsky was already suffering greatly from the lung cancer that would end his life, his last film is one of cinema’s greatest final testaments, a work that puts both pagan and Christian traditions of self-sacrifice into dialectic conversation. Shot in Sweden with renowned cinematographer Sven Nykvist and featuring several other Ingmar Bergman collaborators, including actor Erland Josephson, the gorgeous and deeply affecting film, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes, takes place at a birthday gathering that’s interrupted by news warning of an imminent nuclear holocaust.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: The Saga of Anatahan
movies.cast: Akemi Negishi, Tadashi Suganuma, Kisaburo Sawamura, Shoji Nakayama, Jun Fujikawa, Hiroshi Kondō
movies.description: Visionary Josef von Sternberg had once been a feared and revered presence on the Paramount Studios lot, but after one too many clashes over his obsessive perfectionism rendered him all but unemployable, and a falling out with Howard Hughes over his Jet Pilot, “Jo” went independent, directing, writing, shooting, and narrating this sublimely artificial picture, shot entirely on a Kyoto soundstage, about a dozen Japanese seamen stranded on a Pacific Island with one woman—unaware that World War II has long since ended, and that a little war of their own is in the making. A favorite film of one of von Sternberg’s students during his tenure teaching at UCLA, none other than Mr. Mojo Rising himself, Jim Morrison.

movies.title: The Samurai and The Prisoner
movies.cast: Masahiro Motoki, Masaki Suda, Yuriko Yoshitaka, Munetaka Aoki, Ryota Miyadate, Tasuku Emoto
movies.description: Celebrated Japanese horror director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ( Cure , Serpent’s Path ) explores a new path in this lush treatment of Honobu Yonezawa's prizewinning historical novel, detailing palace intrigue in the court of a samurai nobleman during the Azuchi era at the end of the 16th century. Turning against Oda Nobunaga, the ruthless, power-hungry warlord he previously served, Araki Murashige (Masahiro Motoki, of Departures ) is besieged by Oda’s forces and bedevilled by a series of inexplicable crimes in his household. As tension rises and loyalties fray, Murashige is forced to strategize with Kuroda Kanbei (Masaki Suda, of Kurosawa’s 2024 thriller Cloud ), a samurai envoy sent by Oda and imprisoned by Murashige, while his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and loyalists fight to preserve order.

movies.title: The Scout
movies.cast: Mimi Davila, Rutanya Alda, Max Rosen, Ikechukwu Ufomadu, Sarah Herrman, Otmara Marrero
movies.description: A New York City location scout photographs the homes of strangers for a T.V. pilot, stepping into their private lives while trying to satisfy her erratic employers.
notes: Q&A on 11/9 with director Paula Andrea Gonzalez-Nasser, producer/editor Ryan Martin Brown, and actor Mimi Davila. Moderated by Carrie Carusone ( It Ends ).

movies.title: The Secret Agent
movies.cast: Wagner Moura, Alice Carvalho, Gabriel Leone, Isabél Zuaa, Maria Fernanda Cândido, Udo Kier
movies.description: Set in Brazil in 1977, the most awarded film at Cannes this year stars Wagner Moura ( Narcos , Civil War ) as Marcelo, a former teacher and political dissident on the run during the waning years of Brazil’s military dictatorship. Hoping to reunite with his son, he travels to Recife during Carnival but quickly realizes that the city is not the safe haven he expected. Critics are calling Kleber Mendonça Filho’s vivid neo-noir thriller “a masterpiece” ( The Playlist ) and “superb in every way” ( The Guardian ).

movies.title: The State of Things
movies.cast: Isabelle Weingarten, Rebecca Pauly, Jeffrey Kime, Geoffrey Carey, Camila Mora-Scheihing, Alexandra Auder
movies.description:
German filmmaker Friedrich (Patrick Bauchau) is holed up at a hotel on the storm-lashed Portuguese coast, using American funding to shoot a shoestring budget post-apocalyptic thriller, though mostly he winds up playing a waiting game with cast and crew (including Warhol star Viva, Sam Fuller, Isabelle Weingarten, and co-writer Robert Kramer) after their producer disappears without a trace. An intermediate production made during the difficult shoot of Wenders’s 1982 Hammett for Francis Ford Coppola’s Zoetrope Studios in the US, sumptuously shot in black and white by legendary DP Henri Alekan, The State of Things is Wenders’s meditation on the complicated co-dependence of the European and American film industries.

“The State of Things is as perfect a summation of our time as it was of 1982—then, as now, a time of artistic expatriation, abandonment, and a film industry in crisis. When a movie crew (an all-almost star cast in beautiful black and white) is stranded on location in Portugal, their director must fly to Los Angeles to confront their producer, a man circling the drain in an Airstream trailer he drives continually around Hollywood.” —A.S. Hamrah
notes: Introduction by cartoonist Nathan Gelgud and writer A. S. Hamrah + a book signing with Nathan Gelgud on Saturday, November 14th
Introduction by cartoonist Nathan Gelgud and writer A. S. Hamrah on Saturday, November 14th
Book signing with Nathan Gelgud following the screening

movies.title: The Stranger
movies.cast: Utpal Dutt, Dipankar Dey, Mamata Shankar, Bikram Bhattacharya, Rabi Ghosh, Dhritiman Chatterjee
movies.description:
The coda of perhaps the most celebrated career in subcontinental cinema, Ray’s The Stranger adapts one of the director’s own short stories into a comic, poignant film about the upheaval in a middle-class Calcutta family’s home that follows the appearance of a man, Manmohan (Utpal Dutt, himself approaching the end of a legendary life in pictures), who claims to be a long-lost uncle returning from globe-trotting travels. One of Cahiers du Cinéma’s films of the year, praised by critic Vincent Canby as “a small, gentle, exquisitely realized comedy about, among other things, family loyalties and trust in a world in which traditions have been devalued.”

Print courtesy of the Packard Humanities Institute Collection at the Academy Film Archive.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: The Testament of Ann Lee
movies.cast: Amanda Seyfried, Lewis Pullman, Thomasin McKenzie, Matthew Beard, Christopher Abbott, Viola Prettejohn
movies.description: From award-winning writer-director Mona Fastvold ( The World to Come , The Brutalist ) comes the extraordinary true legend of Ann Lee, founder of the Shakers. Academy Award nominee Amanda Seyfried stars as the devotional sect’s irrepressible leader, who preached gender and social equality and was revered by her followers. The Testament of Ann Lee captures the ecstasy and agony of her quest to build a utopia, featuring more than a dozen traditional Shaker hymns reimagined as rapturous movements with choreography by Celia Rowlson-Hall ( Vox Lux ) and original songs and score by Academy Award winner Daniel Blumberg ( The Brutalist ). Join us for a Q&A with director Mona Fastvold, co-writer Brady Corbet, and actor Tim Blake Nelson following the 6:40pm screening on Friday, January 16.

movies.title: The Thing
movies.cast: Kurt Russell, Wilford Brimley, Keith David, David Clennon, T.K. Carter
movies.description:
Snuggle up! Kurt Russell battles against the cold and a mysterious alien life-form in the John Carpenter version of The Thing .

A team of scientists working in the frozen landscape of the Antarctic encounter a shape-shifting and killer alien being after a strange dog enters the camp. This is, of course, after witnessing a Norwegian team chasing the dog to kill it but perish in a helicopter crash before they can and before they can explain. Isolated in a part of the world nearly as remote as space, Kurt Russell’s R.J. MacReady leads the charge for survival not just his team but for the entire human race. Overshadowed upon its release by the more family friendly film E.T., Carpenter’s The Thing is a terrifying look at outer space in our own world that combines brilliant special effects and humorously scary scenes to punctuate this contemporary version of The Thing from Another World .
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: The Voice of Hind Rajab
movies.cast: Hind Rajab, Motaz Malhees, Saja Kilani, Amer Hlehel, Clara Khoury, Nesbat Serhan
movies.description: Calling for help from inside a car under heavy Israeli military fire in Gaza, Hind Rajab, a 5-year-old Palestinian girl, reached countless listeners around the world after recordings of her desperate pleas were released online. This new film, made by Academy Award nominee Kaouther Ben Hania ( Four Daughters ) in collaboration with Hind’s family and the Palestine Red Crescent Society, combines archival audio with dramatic recreations of the emergency workers at the call center as they try to dispatch rescuers. Winner of the Grand Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice Film Festival, this powerful film compels us to face this tragedy with open eyes. Join us for a Q&A with lead actor Saja Kilani following the 7:30pm screening on Tuesday, January 13.

movies.title: The Wild Bunch
movies.cast: William Holden, Ernest Borgnine, Robert Ryan, Edmond O’Brien, Warren Oates, Ben Johnson, Jaime Sánch
movies.description:
An aging group of outlaws look for one last big score as the “traditional” American West is disappearing around them.

Screening as part of Late Night Favorites: Fall 2026

Previously screened as part of our Weekend Classics series Uneasy Riders: 60s Hollywood , part of Carnegie Hall’s The ’60s: The Years that Changed America festival.

movies.title: The Woman in the Window
movies.cast: Edward G. Robinson, Joan Bennett, Raymond Massey, Edmund Breon, Dan Duryea, Thomas E. Jackson
movies.description: Alone for the holiday while his wife and children are on vacation, the staid, middle-aged college professor Richard Wanley (Edward G. Robinson) is about to settle in to an uneventful stretch of nights spent sipping port by the fireplace of his club—but then he catches a glimpse of a beguiling brunette in a gallery window and, in short order, finds himself having a drink with the model (Joan Bennett), after which everything goes straight to hell. Involved in a self-defense killing and its subsequent cover-up, Wanley finds himself investigating his own crime at the elbow of fellow clubman and D.A. Frank Lalor (Raymond Massey), the noose tightening around his neck with the emergence of every fresh clue and misstep. A high-style turning-of-the-screws noir suspenser, with a wonderfully oleaginous turn from heel extraordinaire Dan Duryea.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: The Woman on the Beach
movies.cast: Joan Bennett, Robert Ryan, Charles Bickford, Nan Leslie, Walter Sande, Irene Ryan
movies.description:
Though mutilated by RKO Pictures following a disastrous test screening, Renoir’s final Hollywood feature remains a film unlike any in its director’s filmography—not to speak of contemporary American cinema—a marvel of brooding atmosphere in which a Coast Guard officer haunted by the memory of a maritime tragedy (Robert Ryan), recently engaged, is bewitched by a dark beauty (Joan Bennett), the wife of a blind painter, whom he meets while riding at seaside, his attraction to her by no means unrequited. A disarmingly frank depiction of consuming, destructive erotic obsession, with a roiling, elemental score by Hanns Eisler contributing to the palpable sense of gathering doom.

Restored by the Library of Congress and The Film Foundation. Funding provided by the Hobson/Lucas Family Foundation.
notes: Presented in 35mm
35mm print courtesy of The Library of Congress.

movies.title: threeASFOUR: Full Circle
movies.cast: Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, Adi Gil, Kai Kühne
movies.description: Avant-garde designers and best friends Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, and Adi Gil have spent 25 years working together as the NYC fashion collective threeASFOUR. Although they have built an impressive reputation and a following that includes Björk, Marisa Tomei, and Chloë Sevigny, they find themselves struggling to pay the rent on their Chinatown studio while financing the intricate creations for their next runway collection. Drawing from a captivating trove of archival footage alongside intimate observations of the trio at work, Sean Ono Lennon forges an affectionate portrait of uncompromising artists who have chosen experimentation over commercial success and a moving reflection on artistic collaboration and creative resilience.

movies.title: Thunder Alley
movies.cast: Annette Funicello, Fabian, Diane McBain, Warren Berlinger, Jan Murray, Stanley Adams
movies.description: After eleven films produced in three years, the seemingly endless BEACH PARTY franchise finally came to a screeching, slam-bang stop with Richard Rush’s THUNDER ALLEY. Race car driver Tommy Callahan (Fabian) decides to retire after inadvertently causing the death of a fellow driver on the track. Working at a stunt show, he soon befriends the boss’s daughter Francie (Annette Funicello) and her wannabe racer boyfriend Eddie (Warren Berlinger). As Tommy shows Eddie the ropes, the teacher’s jealous ex-girlfriend Annie (Diane McBain) schemes to steal the student’s girl from him. Who will end up with who, and who will win the big race?

movies.title: Tickets
movies.director: Abbas Kiarostami, Ken Loach, Ermanno Olmi
movies.cast: Carlo Delle Piane, Valeria Bruni Tedeschi, Silvana De Santis, Filippo Trojano, Martin Compston, Gary Maitland
movies.description:
Bringing together the formidable talents of Ermanno Olmi, Ken Loach, and Abbas Kiarostami, the genre-hopping anthology Tickets presents three discrete but interconnected stories—involving a daydreaming Italian scholar, a brooding ex-soldier reduced to being browbeaten by a general’s widow, and an encounter between a pack of Celtic F.C. fans and a group of Albanian refugees—that unfold on a train travelling from Innsbruck in the Austrian Tyrol to Rome.

“You will be tempted to pick a favorite among the three sections of this omnibus—resist! Try, instead, to appreciate the way they link together, as only a long-distance train ride, its many moods, can allow.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.title: Time Indefinite
movies.cast: Steve Ascher, Michael Blumenthal, Robert Gardner, Natalie Hawley, Ross McElwee, Charleen Swansea
movies.description: His complicated relationship with his aging surgeon father, his settling into married life and fatherhood in early middle-age—these subjects, the sort of foundational building blocks of life so central as to often be taken for granted, are at the center of McElwee’s autobiographical documentary Time Indefinite, a film that brings a dry, laconic humor to its very serious meditations on mortality, family, and spirituality. “A rich and compelling cinematic experience… Conveys a sensuous appreciation of the physical world that is so acute that the environment is almost as important as the people… Communicates a sense of the elusive moment in all its complexity and richness being captured.” —The New York Times
notes: Q&A with filmmaker Ross McElwee on Saturday, December 5th

movies.title: To Die For
movies.cast: Nicole Kidman, Joaquin Phoenix, Matt Dillon, Illeana Douglas
movies.description: Suzanne Stone is a weather reporter at her small-town cable station, but she dreams of being a big-time news anchor. However, she feels that her middle-class husband is holding her back, so she decides to have him murdered. For this, she enlists Jimmy, a high school boy who is enamored with her. The plan doesn't work exactly as she intended, though, and her husband's family starts to suspect that she was involved in his death.

movies.title: Tokyo Sonata
movies.cast: Teruyuki Kagawa, Kyoko Koizumi, Kai Inowaki, Yu Koyanagi, Haruka Igawa, Kanji Tsuda
movies.description: Kurosawa’s reputation was made as perhaps the most formidable figure in the “J-horror” boom, so his about-face into contemporary-set shomin-geki melodrama à la Yasujirō Ozu was an unexpected—but not unwelcome—surprise… though beneath the placid surface of Tokyo Sonata, sinister stirrings are very much visible. Salaryman Teruyuki Kagawa, newly out of work, struggles to keep up the illusion of employment for his family, consisting of one son who lights out to join the US Army, another with a not-so-dirty secret of his own (the scamp is taking piano lessons), and a wife (Kyōko Koizumi) who finds an unlikely solution to her unhappy domestic existence when she’s kidnapped by a home invader. Winner of the Prix Un Certain Regard at the 61st Cannes Film Festival.

movies.title: Tony
movies.cast: Dominic Sessa, Antonio Banderas, Emilia Jones, Stavros Halkias, Leo Woodall, Monica Raymund
movies.description: When 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain (Sessa) travels to Provincetown, happenstance propels him into a restaurant kitchen, kickstarting one of the most watched (and read about) careers in contemporary cooking. From Canadian indie darling Matt Johnson ( BlackBerry , Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie) comes a portrait of one of food media and literature’s most provocative minds. Pulled from excerpts of Kitchen Confidential , Tony eschews traditional sprawling biographical encomium, instead offering a candid glimpse into an especially formative season of Bourdain’s life.

movies.title: True Stories
movies.cast: David Byrne, John Goodman, Annie McEnroe, Jo Harvey Allen, Spalding Gray, Alix Elias
movies.description: Talking Heads frontman David Byrne co-wrote, composed, directed, and starred in this quirky musical journey into the odder side of small-town America. The residents of Virgil, Texas, are a motley crew – from the woman who's too lazy to get out of bed (Swoosie Kurtz) to the shy man who must advertise for a wife (John Goodman). Byrne serves as our tall-hatted tour guide through the town's sesquicentennial "Celebration of Specialness."

movies.title: Tuner
movies.cast: Leo Woodall, Dustin Hoffman, Havana Rose Liu, Lior Raz, Tovah Feldshuh, Jean Reno
movies.description: A gifted piano tuner's meticulous skills for maintaining instruments lead him to discover an unexpected aptitude for cracking safes, turning his life upside down, in the debut feature by Canadian documentary filmmaker Daniel Roher ( Navalny ; Once Were Brothers: Robbie Robertson and the Band ). RogerEbert.com commends the “quiet yet compelling performance” by Leo Woodall as Niki White, the titular tuner, in a film that also provides a “lovely late-career showcase” for veteran actor Dustin Hoffman as Niki’s mentor, Harry Horowitz.

movies.title: Two Pianos
movies.cast: François Civil, Nadia Tereszkiewicz, Charlotte Rampling, Hippolyte Girardot, Alba Gaïa Bellugi, Jeremy Lewin
movies.description: Once a rising star of the French musical scene and Eléna’s (Charlotte Rampling) prized pupil, pianist Mathias (François Civil) returns to France after many years spent teaching and performing in Japan. Soon after his arrival, a chance encounter with a child who looks just like him throws Mathias into turmoil, and leads him back to his first love, Claude (Nadia Tereszkiewicz). French master Arnaud Desplechin ( My Sex Life… , A Christmas Tale ) returns to some of his favorite themes—psychologically charged homecomings and unexpected reunions (romantic and otherwise)—in this sensual, Hitchcockian melodrama featuring one of Rampling’s most delicious roles in years.

movies.title: Union County
movies.cast: Will Poulter, Noah Centineo, Elise Kibler, Emily Meade, Danny Wolohan, Kevin P. Braig
movies.description: This unflinching look at the opioid epidemic follows brothers Cody (Poulter) and Jack Parsons (Centineo) as they navigate a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program, and pursue the promise of a brighter, sober future together. Anchored by poignant, moving performances from its leading duo, Ohio-born filmmaker Adam Meeks’ creates a film imbued with realism for an honest, compassionate portrait of a battle being fought across America and the solidarity that flowers on its front lines.

movies.title: Unstoppable + The Lonedale Operator
movies.description:
A snafu at a railway yard in Pennsylvania sends an unmanned freight engine, 39 cars, and a helluva lot of toxic, flammable phenol speeding full throttle towards possible catastrophe, and only veteran engineer Denzel Washington and untested conductor Chris Pine stand in the way of disaster in Scott’s kinetic white-knuckler. Screens with The Lonedale Operator, a Biograph one-reeler courtesy D.W. Griffith whose advanced intercutting did much to create the template for the modern suspense-thriller.

“Sometimes equipment breaks down, bosses suck, or security falters, but the demands of the rail never let up. Unstoppable and The Lonedale Operator, each on their own side of a century, imagine the worst possible day on the job. The irony for seasoned engineer Frank Barnes (Denzel Washington) and the station operator’s daughter (Blanche Sweet), is that neither is properly employed: Frank was recently fired, and Sweet’s character is only filling in for her sick dad. Luckily for a perennially imperfect American railroad system, these two heroes happened to be around!” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.description: Set in 1858 England, VICTORIAN PSYCHO sees an eccentric governess arrive at a remote gothic manor, where strange happenings stir suspicions that she's not what she seems.

movies.title: Voyage to Italy
movies.cast: Ingrid Bergman, George Sanders, Maria Mauban In Italian with English subtitles.
movies.description:
In Naples to sell a late uncle’s villa, London business man George Sanders and wife Ingrid Bergman find that, after eight years of marriage, they have little to say to each other. And as the closing drags on, Bergman remembers a died-too-young poet who loved her, Sanders frets about time away from work, and they split apart—she to stare at the rawness of the statuary in the Museum, the ionization of Vesuvian craters, the skeletons at the cemetery; he to dally with friends on Capri, languidly pursue an estranged wife, and to wave off an attractive prostitute; both to finally view the plaster molds of the dead of Pompeii. Little happens, and yet subtly we see the degeneration of a marriage. Will it take a miracle to save it? Unsuccessful on first release, but over the years steadily climbing the ranks of All-Time Ten Best lists.

In this centenary tribute to her father and his cinema of thought, Isabella Rossellini plays herself, her mother Ingrid Bergman, David O. Selznick, Alfred Hitchcock, Federico Fellini, Charlie Chaplin, and others.

movies.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Classic Shorts
movies.cast: Nick Park, Anne Reid
movies.description:
Along with the Academy Award–winning success of Aardman Animations’ 1990 Creature Comforts, it was this trio of inspired shorts featuring cheese-loving, jug-eared, Wigan-based crackpot inventor Wallace and his erudite pet dog/straight man/frequent savior Gromit that established the company as a stop-motion dynasty to delight all ages. Featuring A Grand Day Out, in which Wallace whips up a homemade spaceship in order to sample lunar cheddar; The Wrong Trousers, in which nefarious penguin Feathers McGraw employs a new Wallace patent in a daring heist; and A Close Shave, in which our heroes must step away from their window washing concern to foil a sheep rustling operation.

The Wrong Trousers (Nick Park, 1993, 30 mins)

movies.title: Whisper of the Heart
movies.cast: Yoko Honna, Issey Takahashi, Takashi Tachibana, Shigeru Muroi, Minami Takayama, Mayumi Izuka
movies.description: New 4K Restoration A chance encounter with a mysterious cat sends Shizuku, a girl with her head in the clouds, on a quest for her true talent. Together with a new friend Seij, and enchanted by The Baron, an antique cat figurine who guides her to listen to the whispers of her heart, Shizuku embarks on a life-changing adventure that takes her beyond the boundaries of her imagination. This precious gem from the Studio Ghibli catalog—based on a screenplay and storyboards from Hayao Miyazaki—was directed by veteran animator Yoshifumi Kondō, who the studio hoped would become Miyazaki’s successor before his untimely passing in 1998.

movies.title: Wicker
movies.cast: Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Peter Dinklage, Elizabeth Debicki, Marli Siu, Nabhaan Rizwan
movies.description: An audacious comedic fable about sex, marriage, and the absurdities of social convention, WICKER tells the wholly original love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who commissions a husband to be made by the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). When her wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård) proves more spectacular than she ever imagined, his soulful spirit and unique prowess awaken something inside her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination, and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of village life.

movies.title: Wild Boys of the Road
movies.cast: Frankie Darro, Edwin Phillips, Rochelle Hudson, Dorothy Coonan Wellman, Sterling Holloway, Arthur Hohl
movies.description:
Perhaps no other film to emerge from the depths of the Great Depression captured the essentials of the era—the queasy feeling of plummeting social status, the touching sense of solidarity in fresh adversity, the danger of desperation—as Wellman’s Wild Boys of the Road, starring Frankie Darro and Edwin Phillips as two Midwestern high schoolers who, seeing their families suddenly skint, decide to relieve their folks of the financial burden of raising them and ride the rails toward an uncertain destiny.

“By the time Eddie breaks down and cries, ‘I’m sick of being hungry and cold! I’m sick of freight trains!’ both the romantic notion of the train and the idle fantasies of boyhood have been demolished. Suffering is everywhere and there’s no one to blame for it. Though this was a Pre-Code film, its intended ending was still too bleak for producer Jack Warner. If the new ending feels off, it’s a credit to the mounting sense of desperation Wellman built with the rest of the film, where there are no easy answers.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.title: Wild Horse Nine
movies.cast: John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi, Mariana di Girolamo, Ailín Salas, Tom Waits, Parker Posey
movies.description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island’s iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris’s newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

movies.cast: John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi, Mariana di Girolamo, Ailín Salas, Tom Waits, Parker Posey
movies.description: We’re excited for any new movie by Martin McDonagh (THE BANSHEES OF INISHERIN, IN BRUGES), but especially one starring Sam Rockwell, John Malkovich, Parker Posey, and Steve Buscemi. Set on Easter Island just before the 1973 Chilean coup, WILD HORSE NINE sends two CIA agents into a remote paradise where old grudges, conspiracies, and rebellious students complicate their mission. Did we mention Tom Waits is also in this movie? Prepare to be utterly charmed.

movies.title: Wildwood
movies.cast: Peyton Elizabeth Lee, Jacob Tremblay, Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, Richard E. Grant, Angela Bassett
movies.description: From LAIKA, the studio behind CORALINE, WILDWOOD is a handcrafted epic fantasy that transports audiences into a secret, dangerously alive world. After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness, an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything.

movies.title: Wolf's Hole
movies.cast: Miroslav Macháček, Tomáš Palatý, Štěpánka Červenková, Jan Bidlas, Rita Dudušová, Irena Mrozková
movies.description: Wolf’s Hole opens looking very much like a Czechoslovak take on the contemporary American ski chalet-set teen sex romp, with a group of hand-selected youngsters coming together at an exclusive skiing workshop… but by the time it’s wrapped up, Chytilová’s film has arrived a million miles downhill from the likes of Hot Dog… The Movie and Ski Patrol. Strange goings-on will be nightly occurrences at the titular getaway, the instructors seem to be conspiring on a sinister plot that makes the Stanford prison experiment seem benign by comparison, and as a creeping paranoia gradually overtakes the group, the sick comedy that unfolds inside the lodge turns as black as the powder outside is white.

movies.title: You Can See Everything
movies.cast: Elizabeth Holmes, Nathan Fielder, Billy Evans, Amanda Seyfried, Christopher Abbott, Lance Oppenheim
movies.description:
“Why would I deceive you?”

Is there anything Nathan Fielder can’t do? He turned a struggling frozen yogurt shop into a poop-themed tourist destination, helped a Bill Gates impersonator track down his high school sweetheart, and, most recently, learned to fly a commercial jet. But he may have met his awkwardness match in Elizabeth Holmes. Thirty-four days before reporting to prison, the disgraced Theranos founder invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. Thus begins a mind-bending, three-year descent into the abyss for directors Fielder and Lance Oppenheim (PRIMETIME). This kind of social discomfort only comes around once a decade. Don’t miss it in theaters.

movies.title: “Wuthering Heights”
movies.description: Academy Award-winning writer and director Emerald Fennell ( Saltburn ) takes on Emily Brontë’s quintessential gothic novel. A ferocious love story set on the moors, “Wuthering Heights” follows Heathcliff (Elordi) and Catherine (Robbie) as desire gives way to obsession—and vengeance ripples across generations. After decades of adaptations by filmmakers from William Wyler to Luis Buñuel, Emerald Fennell’s glossy reimagining rejects strict fidelity in favor of an unconventional reinvention for a new generation.
